evidence.claim: Event is a Community Team event in which Community Team Ambassadors hide inside Blackspore and players search for them.
Client quest title is 'Ambassador Haunt and Seek' (locale:14562, quest_title).
Client quest objective: 'The Community Team Ambassadors are haunting Blackspore. Can you find them? Listen to the Zone Chat channel for clues!'
Article 1851 schedules a run on Server 1 for Thursday October 14, 2010 at 3pm Pacific Time (U.S. and Latin America).
Article 1851 schedules a second Server 1 run for Friday October 15, 2010 at 9:00am Pacific Time / 4:00pm GMT (UK and Europe).
After a player scares an Ambassador properly, the player sends a trade request and receives a treat; the found Ambassador vanishes and reappears elsewhere.
Ambassadors give instructions and hints in the Zone Chat tab (article 1851 quote: 'The Ambassadors will be using the ZONE CHAT tab in your chat window to give instructions and hints').

Spanish article 1859 describes the same event type (Ambassadors hide in Blackspore, players scare them and request a trade for a prize, clues via Zone Chat) in future tense, as a pre-launch announcement. It gives no date.

open: Live status is unsure, not yes. Article 1851 gives scheduled run times in future-tense wording ('will be using'), and no fetched source confirms that the Oct 14 or Oct 15 2010 runs happened. Occurrences are scheduled, not confirmed as run.

Year and dates come from the article text (Oct 14-15, 2010). The pack has date: null for both articles, so the post date is not known. Oct 14 2010 was a Thursday and Oct 15 a Friday, and 9am PDT equals 4pm GMT, so the stated times are internally consistent.

Critique fix applied: 'Blackspore Ambassador Haunt and Seek' removed from aliases. ids and locale show only locale:14562 ('Ambassador Haunt and Seek') and no row with a 'Blackspore' prefix. Evidence[1] restated to cite locale:14562 only.

The 'Show Area Chat' / wrench icon instruction is dropped. The pack's fact row contains it, but no quote supports it and the article 1851 Zone Chat sentence is the only sourced text. Confirm against the full text of articleId=1851 before reinstating it.

Article 1859 is kept as a same-type announcement, not as evidence for the Oct 14-15 runs. It has no date, its run times come only from the pack summary, and no source ties it to the same occurrence. Its 'rather than outside it' wording was not used.

Alias: article 1851 titles the event 'Community Event: Ambassador Haunt and Seek' (per the pack). Article 1859 uses the Spanish title 'Posee y Busca a los Embajadores', a translation, not a verified alias, so it is not listed.

Possible merge or alias problem: the client and articles contain a family of 'Ambassador Hide and Seek' events in other zones (locale 6673 Briarwood, locale 15045 Snowhill, birthday parties in articleId=1308). They are different events and are not counted here.
Recurring is null. The only sourced occurrences are the two scheduled Oct 2010 Server 1 runs, and no source says the event recurs.
NPCs: only the generic 'Community Team Ambassadors' is sourced. No named NPC is tied to this event. The Ambassador Events friend-list character (articleId=2407) is not tied to it in any source.
Items: none. The treat (article 1851) and prize (article 1859) are not named as items, and no price or currency is sourced. Item list left empty.
Locale 6622 mentions Ambassadors with stolen cake, which belongs to a different event and is not counted.
Zone is Blackspore, from locale 14566 and articles 1851 and 1859. The Spanish text calls it Esporaumbria.
No quest answers mention this event and no wiki category page ties to it. The client rows 14562 and 14566 show the quest title and objective only, not the date or the prize.

evidence.claim: Free Realms players could buy a Cherry Blossom Tree for 500 Station Cash as part of the Japan earthquake relief fundraiser (SOE-wide promotion across EverQuest, Free Realms and Clone Wars Adventures)
Cherry Blossom items were sold via the in-game Marketplace from Friday March 25 to Monday March 28, 2011 (the 2011 year is confirmed by dated articles 2070 and 2071, not by 2068's null metadata date)
Free Realms players could buy a Cherry Blossom Tree for 500 Station Cash as a show of support for Japan earthquake relief, dated 2011-03-25
The Cherry Blossom Tree is a virtual home decoration meant to show community support for Japan's devastation, dated 2011-03-25
Free Realms offered a Cherry Blossom Tree for 500 Station Cash as support for Japan earthquake relief, dated 2011-03-25

SOE pledged a $10 donation to the American Red Cross for each Cherry Blossom item bought during the March 25-28 window. This is a pledge in the source text ('SOE donará', future tense); payment completion is not shown
Client locale 434304 names the item Cherry Blossom Tree
Client locale 434306 describes the Cherry Blossom Tree as purchased to show support for the earthquake relief effort in Japan

Client locale 434305 says that for every Cherry Blossom Tree purchased, SOE will donate 10 dollars to the Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort (future tense; recipient wording differs from the articles)

open: Name and merge: the pack names the event after its item only. The event is the Japan earthquake/tsunami relief fundraiser, and Cherry Blossom Tree is one part of it. Working title only; aliases to add: 'Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort' (locale 434305), 'Cherry Blossom sale', 'Apoyo a los Damnificados del Terremoto y Tsunami ocurrido en Japon' (articles 2070/2071 titles).

Scope: the sale was SOE-wide across EverQuest, Free Realms and Clone Wars Adventures (article 2068). Free Realms' share is only the in-game catalog/marketplace listing. The $10 donation was SOE's, not Free Realms'.

Donation recipient differs by source: articles 2068/2070/2071 say the American Red Cross; client locale 434305 says the Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort. Probably the same fund; not confirmed. Payment of the donation is not confirmed by any source.

Extension (article 2076, Spanish): the catalog sale of a Cherry Blossom item was extended to April 1, with the same $10 per item donation. It has no exact post date (only relative 'Posted 2 months, 6 days ago'), so its year and end date are unconfirmed. Not used as evidence or an occurrence. Keep as an unconfirmed extension of the March 2011 sale until a dated source is found.

Base window: March 25-28, 2011 (Friday to Monday), from article 2068 body text, with articles 2070/2071 dated 2011-03-25. Article 2068 metadata date is null, so the year rests on its text and on the dated 2070/2071.

Memorial tree (article 2066): a 'memorial Cherry Blossom Tree' sold for 500 Station Cash in Free Realms, shown in player homes where applicable. It was seen only in lookup output, not in the evidence pack, and has no date. Its tie to this sale (matching wording and price) is a likely inference, not confirmed. It may be the same item as the tree above. Not counted as evidence until a dated source ties it to the 2011 sale.

Items: only the Cherry Blossom Tree (500 Station Cash) is listed, because it is the only item tied to the event by a source with a price. The Cherry Blossom item in article 2076 has no confirmed identity or price and is not listed.
Locale 434306 supports only the purchase-for-support wording. The 10-dollar donation is cited to locale 434305 and articles 2068/2071.
Locale 7788 'Bamboo and cherry blossom combat outfit' is not tied to this event and is excluded.

Zones, NPCs, quests and rewards are empty for lack of source, not because they do not exist. No wiki category members and no quest answers were found for this event. Home display in player houses is stated only in article 2066 (unconfirmed tie) and article 2068 lookup text ('can be placed in a player's house'), so zones stay empty.
No video frames were checked for this event.
Recurring is null: only one occurrence is sourced (March 2011). Nothing says it recurs.

All article dates in the pack are null. The year 2010 comes from article text. The only posting date is about 2010-11-23, from the summary of article 1918, which says the date is inferred and not shown.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

Articles 2031 and 2032 are titled 'Evento Comunitario: Duelo Ninja', and their dates, times and Server 1 match the English 2029 sessions. No single source names both titles, so the merge is inferred and 'Duelo Ninja' / 'Ninja Duel' are NOT listed as aliases. Confirm before adding them.

Conflict in article 1391: it lists a UK/Europe session at 9:00am Pacific / 6:00pm GMT on Server 1 dated 'Friday April 14th, 2010', but its main session is dated May 13, 2010 (a Thursday). The April 14 date conflicts with the May 13 date and with its weekday. Unresolved; not counted as an occurrence.
The 2010 run has no held-session report, so it is not an occurrence.
Article 2041 (French, undated) describes a Ninja Brawl on server 1 with duel invitations but gives no date. Not counted.
Pack covers the 2009 and 2011 runs; no sources were found for any other years.
The 2009 run is sourced to article 311 only. The 2009 zone (Shrouded Glade) is confirmed by 311; the 2011 zone is confirmed by 2029, not by the Spanish posts, which name only Server 1.
NPCs: Tim in Villadelago appears in the Spanish posts only as the fighter-to-ninja job trainer, a separate path, so he is not listed.
Quests: none tied to this event in the pack or lookup. Generic 'Win the duel' ninja level-20 quest hits in video are not event-specific and are left out.
Items, prices, currency and rewards: none sourced for this event.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

open: Split: the pack merges two events. This object is only the standing weekly House Party. The 2010 Summer Camp season is a separate event and is not in this object. Its details, for a second calendar entry: name 'Summer Camp 2010', kind 'other', live 'no' (season ended Sept 2010). Occurrences: season of 13 themed weeks, June to early September 2010 (tentonhammer node 85170; June 4 2010 update via articleId 1498 as the pack states); Pet Parade Thursday 2 Sept 2010 3pm PT and Friday 3 Sept 2010 9am PT on Server 1 (articleId 1780, from the pack and not re-read here). Themes with their articles: Sports Week (1596), Arts and Crafts (1624), Treasure Hunting (1757), Pirates Week (1661), Fashion Week (1592), Pet Week (1775). Activities also include Robbie's camp party in Greenwood Forest (1534), Robbie's tent treasure hunt (1637, 1644) and daily TCG events (1596, 1592). Quests (exact titles, client-tagged): 'Chatty's Summer Camp Party' (locale:7037), 'Robbie's Summer Camp Party' (locale:7039), 'Jojo's Mojo' (locale:441714), 'Jojo's Dojo' (locale:441718). Items, price and currency null (articles 1498 and 1502): Chatty and Robbie camp banners, campfires, tents, stackable totems and playgrounds, sold in the Summer Camp Coin Shop (currency not named). Zones: Greenwood Forest, Crossroads, Sanctuary, Seaside (Pirate's Plunder, per the wiki page and locale 424963), Blackspore (locale 31294). Snowhill is only in the Sports Week activity text (1596). NPCs: Chatty, Robbie (locale:429097, articles 1498, 1510, 1534), Jojo (tied by quest text only).

Pirate's Plunder Party and Pirate Week belong to the Summer Camp 2010 event, not the weekly. Sources: articleId 1661 (Pirates Week theme post) and the wiki 'Community Events' page ('the main focus on the Summer Camp Pirate Week').

Thursday and Friday sessions are not part of the weekly pattern. They come from Summer Camp season posts (1596, 1624, 1757, 1775) and are expectations only. Article 1854 gives Thursday 4pm, which is a further conflict.

Time conflicts for the weekly are unresolved. 1552 (French): Tuesday 18:00 and 16:00 PST, Thursday 15:00, 'Friday morning at 18h'. The 18h Friday reading is probably a transcription error, so it was not used. 1596 group: Tuesday 9am and 4pm PT, Thursday 3pm, Friday 9am. The House Party time is not confirmed.
Year is missing for articleId 2286 (Tuesday, October 3rd). It is not in occurrences because no year is stated. Confirm the year before adding it.

Locale 441832 is tied to Summer Camp by its text only ('Speak to the camp counselors at Summer Camp and deliver Glugmort's package to Jojo'). The lookup tag reads 'Jojo A-go-go'. The critique's 'Wilds South' tag was not reproduced by the lookup, so that claim is not used. Its link to quest 441714 is by name only.
The pack's date 2010-07-01 for articleId 1592 is not in the article text and is unverified. The Summer Camp posts 1552, 1596, 1624, 1757, 1775 and 1854 have no absolute date.

Wireable is false: the weekly Tuesday time is unresolved and the event has no confirmed time of day. The Summer Camp 2010 entry can be wired for its dated span and the 2-3 Sept 2010 Pet Parade once split out.
Client strings 'Community Event:' (Story Time, Farming Fun, Lot Racing, Memory Match and others), the Launch Pad Party and Tiger the Party Animal are other events and are excluded.
Pet Parade locales 424963 and 424964 carry a dev_note flag on the 'SERVER 1' tag, which may be internal. The event text is used and the flag is noted.
Wiki category members and quest answers are empty in the pack. The House Party's NPCs and quests are not sourced, so npcs and quests are empty for the weekly object.

The winter 2010 return posts (articleId 1950, 1953, 1956, 1957) print no year. They are used as context only, not as dated occurrences. The Dec 9/10 season-party dates are inferred from capture dates and are not used.
Article 892's 2010-01-26 date is pack metadata; its body says only 'over until next year'.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

evidence.claim: Article 1958 announces the Winter Basin (Cuenca Invernal) Snow Days party on Server 1 as 'the first Snow Days party of the season'. It is a pre-event notice and does not confirm the party was held. Held status stays open.
Article 1958 gives the Americas session as Thursday 9 December 2010 at 15:00 Pacific Time on Server 1.

Article 1958 gives the UK and Europe session as Friday 10 December 2010 at 09:00 Pacific Time on Server 1. Its 16:00 GMT figure does not match December Pacific time (PST, UTC-8, which gives 17:00 GMT), so only the Pacific time is used.
Article 1958 tells players to wear winter outfits and seasonal costumes and bring a boombox.
Article 1953 calls the party 'the first Snow Days party of the season'. It gives no date and does not say the party ran.
Snow Days 2011 was live when the community webcast aired; the recap says 'Snow Days is HERE!'. It gives no month or day.
Article 892 says Snow Days ended and would return the following year, so the event recurs.
During Snow Days, players could talk to Candi Ivy daily to get a present from under the Gifting Tree, and spin the Snow Days prize wheel.
The Mayor and other Snow Hill residents had daily Snow Days quests. The quest titles are not in the pack.
Snow Days outfits were sold in the Marketplace for a limited time and did not return until the next Snow Days.
Fighting Robgoblins during Snow Days earns special Snow Days clothing.
The client holds the quest title 'Snow Days'.
'Snow Days Wheel' is a client place name (checked with ids).

Articles 2827 and 2813 describe a 12 Days of Holidays event: one daily challenge from December 13 to 24, with presents opened on December 25. Neither gives a year, and neither says whether it is part of Snow Days.

The wiki files the 12 Days of Presents items under Category:12 Days of Presents and calls them part of 'an annual Snow Days quest event' (2012 for Snow Days Lot and Snow Days Unicorn Sweater; 2013 for Icy Snowflake Glasses and Figgy Pudding Critter). Wiki-only, with no article confirmation of the year. Whether 12 Days is a sub-event of Snow Days or a separate event is unresolved.
evidence.source: wiki: Category:12 Days of Presents; wiki: Snow Days Lot; wiki: Snow Days Unicorn Sweater; wiki: Icy Snowflake Glasses; wiki: Figgy Pudding Critter

open: Merge question (unresolved): the pack title names the Winter Basin party, which is the 2010 notice, not the whole Snow Days event. The 12 Days of Presents series is not folded into Snow Days occurrences, items, or rewards here, because the articles do not say it is part of Snow Days. The wiki does file it under Snow Days (Category:Snow Days, Icy Snow Days Flair Shard, Snow Days Builders Pack), so the answer may be a sub-event. Calendar fit: give 12 Days of Presents its own entry, kind holiday, window Dec 13 to Dec 25, with the years 2012 and 2013 from the wiki only and not article-confirmed. Its quest titles are exact client titles: '12 Days of Presents' (locale:441931) and 'Snowhill 12 Days of Presents' (locale:441964). Its items are Snow Days Lot, Snow Days Unicorn Sweater, Icy Snow Days Flair Shard, Snow Days Builders Pack, Icy Snowflake Glasses and Figgy Pudding Critter, all wiki-only.

Held status for 2010: article 1958 is a pre-event notice and article 1953 gives no date or outcome. The 2010 occurrence is an announced schedule only. The pack's summary that the party was 'held on Server 1' overclaims and is not used. Year 2011 is live by article 2428, but no month or day is given for it.
Time conflict: article 1958 gives 09:00 Pacific as 16:00 GMT. December Pacific is PST (UTC-8), which gives 17:00 GMT. The GMT figure is not used.
Mittens: the pack's fact says players should bring mittens, but the quoted text in article 1958 does not include mittens. Left out of activities.

Items: no price or currency for any item in the pack. Marketplace outfit names and Robgoblin clothing names are not in the pack, so no item names are listed. Snow Days Present (locale:1729), Snow Days Floor (locale:441325) and Snow Days Pillar (locale:441326) exist in the client, but no article, wiki page or video ties them to the event. They are name-match only and are not listed as items. Snow Days Lot (locale:441205) is a place. Its item role is wiki-only under the 12 Days series.
Quests: the daily Snow Hill quest titles are not in the pack, so quests lists only 'Snow Days'.
Mystery chest: the Seasonal Snow Days Mystery Chest comes from one undated video frame (yJ2KHN9I7EI/00008.jpg) with no price. Excluded from items.
NPCs: the Mayor of Snow Hill is unnamed in article 828. The client has 'Mayor Crystalline in Snowhill' (locale:778), but nothing ties that NPC to Snow Days, so it is excluded.
locale:829 'Snow Days Housing Update!' names the event, but its content is not verified, so no claim is made from it.
Article dates are null in the pack. The 2010 year comes from the article text, not a dated source.
Wireable: false for the Snow Days umbrella. The answer format has no wireable field, so it is recorded here.
Kind: holiday is chosen because Snow Days is the winter seasonal event. The 2010 community party is one session inside it.

Aliases: the pack's title merges the 2010 party with the Snow Days umbrella. The Spanish name 'Días de Nieve' and the party name are both kept. The pack may miss an alias for the 12 Days series, which is not listed here.

evidence.claim: Promotion: pre-paid Free Realms Station Cash retail game cards, redeemed in a set window, gave double value in Station Cash for players with accounts in good standing; Starter Cards excluded.

Article 346 and 1186 share the title 'Double Station Cash Weekend. Don't Miss Out!!' and the same offer wording. Their redemption windows are: Fri Sept 18 (after 7:00am PDT) to Sun Sept 20 (before 10:00pm PDT) [346, no year stated]; Fri April 2 (after 4:00pm PDT) to Sun April 4 (before 11:00pm PDT) [1186, no year stated].

Neither article states a year. The 2009 year for the September window comes only from a cross-game TenTonHammer post (node/74525, Free Realms/EQ/EQ2 double face value Sept 18-20 2009); the link to article 346 rests on the date match, not a title match. The April year (2010) is inferred from the capture date and is not stated by any source.

Not this event (separate promotions in the pack's merged set): articleId 2893 (Spring Celebration, Mar 29-31, purchases and cards); 1970 (purchase bonus, ran until Dec 19, no year); 2754 and 2763 (Labor Day weekend, Sept 1-3 2012); 2483 (CVS/pharmacy card weekend); 2806 (7-Eleven SOE Game Card); 2146 (Memorial Mania, triple); 2294 (Europe Oct 2011); tentonhammer node/97967 (PSN compensation); locale:465 (CVS Jan 2012, not_live); wiki image Newbestbuy.jpg (Best Buy exclusive card, separate retailer promotion).

Unconfirmed candidates, not counted: articleId 1974 (same card-redeem wording, Dec 2010 capture, no window); articleId 1590 (Fourth of July weekend card double, captured July 2010, different title); tentonhammer node/78284 (Dec 23 2009 to Jan 3 2010, 100% bonus, not verified).
No zones, NPCs, quests, wiki category members or item prices are tied to this event in the sources. Retailers are not named in the article text.

open: Live status unsure: the articles describe a promotion that ran, but no article states a year. The September window's 2009 year rests on a cross-game TenTonHammer post (node/74525) matched by date only, so the occurrence is not schedulable from the article itself.

Occurrences left empty on purpose. Dated candidates for the calendar, if the year is confirmed: Sept 18-20 (year 2009 per node/74525, title-unconfirmed); April 2-4 (year 2010 inferred from capture date only). Do not count as recurring: two same-title windows exist, but neither article gives a year, so no pattern is proven.
Recurring is null. Two same-title windows (Sept and April) would suggest a pattern, but neither is dated by its own article.

The pack's name merges several different promotions (Spring Celebration, Labor Day, CVS, 7-Eleven, Best Buy, Memorial Mania, Europe). Only articleIds 346 and 1186 share this title and wording; split the rest into their own records.
Items: no price or SKU is tied to this event. The $5/$10/$15 card values in the client or wiki are not linked to this promotion's text, so price and items stay empty.
Locale ids 465, 2790, 2806, 2807 are client strings (or flagged not_live); article ids 2806 and 2483 are retailer articles, not locale ids. Do not mix them up.
Confidence is low (0.25): no year in either article, one cross-game year link, and an unverified 2010 inference.

wiki_page.title: Pumpkin Prince
wiki_page.text:
The Pumpkin Prince is an enemy NPC boss featured as the main antagonist of the Super Spooktacular. He is the pumpkin monster, his main goal while arrived is to terrorizing the four locations, though his goal was said to rule all of Sacred Grove.

Battle
Open World
During the Super Spooktacular, a message will pop up saying "The Pumpkin Prince is terrorizing in <Warpstone>". While the Pumpkin Prince is arrived, ectoplasmic destabilizer dispseners appear on the pathways of four locations which you will find somewhere near where the Pumpkin Prince is (he is walking around somewhere in that area and anyone can attack him). All you must do is keep firing at him with your ectoplasmic shooter which will be at the bottom of your screen where your combat moves are.

The Pumpkin Prince can spawn undead enemies such as grave elementals or necrowart zombies that will attack you with effects that slow you down. The Pumpkin Prince can also attack you with himself and if he strikes you will be turned into a necrowart zombie and lose your ectoplasmic shooter ability. You will have to pick up another one when the effect wears off.

Once defeated, he will cry a call in defeat and drop a treasure chest, which will give you a limited Super Spooktacular reward. If he wins he will cry a call of victory and will not drop anything.

Bone Bog Cemetery
The Pumpkin Prince appears in the Bone Bog Cemetery, located in Blackspore Swamp during the Super Spooktacular, which at one point will require you to encounter him in a battle which requires you to be level 13 combat job or above to enter. You going to the dungeon with Lucinda. You will go to fight against the Pumpkin Prince, and send his undead army back to the ghost world. The Pumpkin Prince also spawn the ghosts which will heal him in a battle

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

The lookup output did not show the 9am time in article 1918, so this stays unresolved and is not cited for the 3pm figure.
Time zone error in article 1927 and in the pack: 18:00 CET equals 17:00 UTC, not 16:00. The article's '4:00pm GMT' is wrong by one hour. The pack's hour_gmt 16 should be 17.

Date conflict: article 1927's summary says 'the day after US Thanksgiving', but its stated sessions are Thursday 25 Nov 2010 (US Thanksgiving itself) and Friday 26 Nov. Article 645 says 'the Friday after US Thanksgiving'. The Friday session is the day after Thanksgiving; the Thursday session is Thanksgiving Day itself.
Article 1931 (Spanish, 'Baile de Pavos') is in the lookup, but its date is not in the pack. Its event tie is only its title and location, and it is not used as an occurrence source.
Recurring is unknown. The pack has one year (2010). No article says it recurs, and wiki says 'was a dance party'. Check 2011-2013 Thanksgiving articles before setting a recurring rule.

Currency is Station Cash per the wiki 'Station Cash Marketplace' wording. The wiki category membership ('SC Marketplace', 'Marketplace Items') is not visible in the lookup output and the pack's wiki_category_members is empty, so category membership is unverified. Prices are blank in the wiki text.

The wiki 'Turkey Outfit' and 'Turkey Hat' pages say they were sold from mid to late November. The claim that they were introduced in November 2009 for Fall Harvest, made in the critique, does not appear in the lookup output and is unverified. If verified, a 2009 item sale would be outside the 2010-only occurrence record.

Article 1930 says the hat was bought 'from the catalog' (Spanish 'del catalogo'), while articles 1918 and 645 say 'Marketplace'. This conflict is unresolved. Article 1927's 'turkey costumes sold at the Marketplace' is secondary (LLM summary); the Marketplace claim rests on 1918 and 645 quotes.

Client text locale:4178 ('Wear on Thanksgiving at own risk') ties the Turkey Hat to Thanksgiving but not to the dance. Not counted as an event tie. Likewise the Raw/Roasted/Burnt Turkey mounts and Giant Turkey are Thanksgiving promos with no tie to the dance; excluded.

Unresolved candidate, excluded from activities: client dialog locale:9247 (npc_dialog tagged 'Turkey Dance'): 'What are you thankful for? Meet at the Farnum Farmstead ... Wear your best turkey outfit!'. No article or wiki line ties it to the Dance de Dinde, and the meeting place contradicts Pixiewood in articles 1927, 1918, 645 and 1931. The NPC for this dialog is not named. It may be a separate event or a second part. Keep it out of the record until a source links it.

Name merge risk: 'Turkey Dance' may be confused with Thanksgiving turkey promos or the Harvest Picnic Party (article 2407, a different event that also names the turkey hat and outfit). This record keeps only the 2010 Dance de Dinde. Rewards are not in the pack; no reward source. npcs and quests are empty: no source names an NPC or quest for the event.

svrobgoblin-rave.title: Community Event: Robgoblin Rave

evidence.claim: Client locale 9106 names the event 'Community Event: Robgoblin Rave'. The client tags it kind 'other'. This is the event's name in the client.

Community event announced for the Robgoblin Camp north of the Lakeshore Warpstone, with music and dancing. The article is future-tense ('Our next community event will be at the Robgoblin Camp north of the Lakeshore Warpstone'), so it is a pre-event announcement, not a record that the event ran.
U.S. and Latin America session scheduled for Thursday 13 January 2011, 3pm Pacific Time, Server 1.
UK and Europe session scheduled for Friday 14 January 2011, 9:00am Pacific Time, stated as 6:00pm GMT, Server 1.

open: Live status unknown: both articles are pre-event announcements of scheduled sessions. No source here confirms the sessions ran, so 'live' stays unsure. The announcement itself is a pre-launch note: posted about January 2011, inferred from a relative 'Posted 6 days, 8 hours ago' stamp in the pack summary. Posting date is not stated and is not used as a fact. The two session times are scheduled occurrences, separate from the announcement.

GMT conflict in the sources: article 1993 and article 1998 both state 6:00pm GMT. Their own Pacific and CET times agree with each other: 9:00am Pacific in January (UTC-8) and 18:00 CET (UTC+1) are both 17:00 GMT. So the stated GMT figure is one hour off by arithmetic. The Pacific time (9:00am, Server 1, Friday 14 January 2011) is the primary timing. The stated GMT is recorded as the source's figure, not as a corrected one. Calendar consumers should not trust the GMT number.

Merge: the French article 1998 (18:00 CET / 6:00pm GMT, Friday 14 January) is the same session as article 1993's UK and Europe session (9:00am Pacific). It was double-counted in the earlier answer and is now one occurrence.

Alias: article 1998 (French) names the event 'Rave Party Robgobeline' (the French text is partly garbled in the lookup output, so the exact wording is summarised, not quoted). Listed as an alias of the same event. The pack missed it.
Recurring is null. Two regional sessions of one announced event do not make it a recurring event, and no article says it recurs.
Items and rewards: none. The wiki category members list is empty, and no source ties any item or reward to the event.
Quests: none. The quest-answer list for this event is empty.

NPCs: none listed as event participants. Fizzlesticks is a location tie only, as the article gives no evidence he took part. The earlier answer's listing of him as an event NPC was wrong and is removed.
Pack merge risk: the pack has one title for two articles that describe the same event, so no second event is merged here. Both articles describe one Robgoblin Rave with two regional sessions.

Spells and wallets: the 'cast spells' and 'guard their wallets' wording is from a lookup fact tied to article 1998 (French). The earlier answer dropped it. It is restored here with that source. The French quote is partly garbled in the tool output, so the wording is summarised only.

wiki_page.title: Player Studio
wiki_page.text:
thumb
Player Studio is a program that offered U.S. based players, 18 and older who have a Station Account in good standing, the opportunity to design potential in-game items to be sold through the SC Marketplace of their participating online game of choice.

Players also receive the opportunity to suggest: the item name, item description, Station Cash value for the market, and rationale for how it fits into the ongoing storyline. If a player-created item is selected for inclusion in the SOE Marketplace, SOE will share 40% of the net amount it receives from the sale of the item with the player that created the item.

(Players under 18 may participate with the help of a parent or a legal guardian).

wiki_page.title: 12 Days of Presents
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The 12 Days of Presents is an annual event that takes place from December 13th through the 24th as a part of SOE's 12 Days of Holidays. Each day, a quest is made available which upon completion on its first day offered; a present is rewarded along with its bow for that specific day. If the quest is completed on another day, only the present is granted leaving the bow to be acquired through the SC Marketplace. 

On December 25th, players that log in can open the presents that have a bow to redeem an exclusive item. Players get a bonus “Big Present” for every 4 of the daily presents they are able to open. The event was introduced in 2012, and each year players have the opportunity to receive a total of 15 presents.

open: MERGE WARNING: the pack treats the dance as the whole event. The dance is a community event inside the Festival of Hearts holiday (annual, Valentine's-themed, February through March, Merry Vale, wiki "Festival of Hearts"; Ten Ton Hammer node 80708). Holiday-wide content (She-Rex, Snowheart, Lovelectric Boombox, Dove via the "Sleeping Pixie" quest, Festival of Hearts Mystery Gift locale:4418, Festival of Hearts TCG Bundle locale:4874 / article 1009, Heart Breakers, Cudip quest text locale:1418) is left off this record. It belongs on a separate kind=holiday record for Festival of Hearts. Recommend splitting the pack into two events.

ALIAS: the pack's name uses a Spanish alias and the English Festival of Hearts Semi-Formal item name. Client name 'Community Event: Festival of Hearts Dance Party' (locale:2778) is an extra alias not in the pack.

RECURRING: the dance has only one dated occurrence (2010). Article 957 says 'first annual', which states an intent to repeat but no second dance is shown in the pack, so recurring is null. The annual pattern belongs to the holiday, not the dance.

OCCURRENCES for the holiday are not established beyond 2010. Articles 969, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2499, 2500, 2501 say 'annual Festival of Hearts has returned/begun' (Merry Vale; Vegalegre in 2018/2019), but the pack gives no dates for them and the lookup excerpts show none. Article 2499 (PS3 launch) also has no date. The 2011 Teddy Bear Costume (wiki) is a February 2011 Monthly Membership Pack item linked only by category, so it is not counted as an occurrence.
ARTICLE DATE: article 960 and 957 pages show no post date (pack date null). The 2010 year and the Feb 12 date come from the event text itself, not a post date.

PRICES: the outfit has no stated price. The wiki She-Rex page's price text is truncated ("at the regular price [of] ,"), so no number was recoverable. She-Rex and Lovelectric Boombox are holiday items sold through the SC Marketplace; not dance items.
REWARDS: no rewards are stated for the dance in any source in the pack.

PLAN VS LIVE: article 957 'join us for our first annual...' reads as an announcement, but article 960 and 959 are past tense ('was held'), and locale and article 967 confirm the event ran, so live=yes. Article 957 has no date of its own, so the announcement timing is unverified.
ZONES: Merry Vale is from locale:6676 ('semi-formal dance in Merry Vale'). Vegalegre appears only for a later year's festival (article 2018), not this dance.
QUESTS: the pack lists none. Wiki 'Dove' names the 'Sleeping Pixie' quest as part of the holiday questline, not the dance. No quest title is tied to the dance, so the quests list is empty.

TIME ZONE: article 960 gives UK/Europe as 09:00 Pacific / 18:00 'Tiempo Europeo'. 09:00 PST is 17:00 GMT and 18:00 CET. Calendar entries must say 17:00 GMT / 18:00 CET (09:00 PST).

REWARDS: none sourced.

TRANSLATION: the Spanish quotes in articles 959 and 960 are translated approximately. The 'Festival de Corazones' naming relies on the Spanish article text.

open: Critique fix 1 (quests): 'Trick-or-Treat' (locale:415050) is removed from this row. It goes to the Super Spooktacular umbrella row. This row's quests are only ['Trick-or-Treat around Sanctuary'].
Critique fix 2 (costumes): the costume claim now cites article 1864 and article 1870. Article 1870 is undated in the archive, but its text gives the 21 October 2010 session date.

Critique fix 3 (occurrences): two occurrences are recorded as separate rows. The first is 2010-10-21 15:00 Pacific (US/Latin America, Server 1). The second is 2010-10-22 09:00 Pacific / 16:00 GMT (UK/Europe, Server 1). Both are sourced to article 1864. Article 1864 has date null in the pack, so the year comes from its quoted session dates.

Critique fix 4 (parent): the format has no parent field, so parent_event is added as an extra top-level key. Parent is 2nd Annual Super Spooktacular (2010), per article 1864 and article 1870 ('second anniversary of the Super Spooktacular edition'). Super Spooktacular stays a separate umbrella row, with the dated years from articles 476, 1854 and 2949.
Pack merge: the pack merges two things. The single-session 2010 party (Oct 21-22, Sanctuary) is one row. The repeatable Trick-or-Treat quest (locale:415050) and the umbrella belong to another row.

Items are empty. The Chiller Boombox is a Super Spooktacular TCG Quest Pack reward (wiki 'Chiller Boombox'; articles 1854, 476), tied only as a prop at this party (article 1864). Its station_cash price comes from an undated store frame (video:1LjCvhboCkQ/00190.jpg). Neither is tied to this party as an item, so both are excluded. Article 516 mentions a separate earlier Chiller Boombox dance party, also not this event.

Zones: Sanctuary only. Pixiewood is the decoration location mentioned in undated article 1870. Article 1857 (undated) says Harry Halloween starts Trick or Treat on the road to Pixiewood, which is a quest-start location and not a party zone.

Aliases: 'Trick or Treat party' is kept (article 1870 wording). 'Sanctuary Trick-or-Treat party' and '2nd Annual Super Spooktacular Trick or Treat party' are dropped because they are not in the pack's names_seen or any cited source wording.
Recurring: null. Only one dated party year (2010). No source says the party recurs. The annual pattern belongs to Super Spooktacular.
Rewards: none. No source gives a candy turn-in reward or a quest reward for this party.

Separate event not merged: SOE cross-game Trick-or-Treat promotion, October 2011 through Oct 31 2011, in which Free Realms was a participating game (articles 2322, 2325). It needs its own promotion row.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

open: Live status unsure: article 1888 has no posting date (only 'Posted 3 weeks, 2 days ago') and no post-event report confirms the party ran.

Only one occurrence is sourced to this event (Nov 4-5, 2010, article 1888). Recurring is null because two or more occurrences are needed. Article 906 (Jan 29, 2010) is dropped from occurrences: it names the event 'Seaside Launch Pad Leap', and nothing in it ties it to the November party. It may be an earlier occurrence of the same series, but that link is unconfirmed. Article 1254 (Lakeshore, Apr 15, 2010) is a separate event and is excluded.

Merge risk: the name family 'Launch Pad Leap' spans Seaside (906, 1888) and Lakeshore (1254). Aliases 'Launch Pad Leap' and 'Seaside Launch Pad Leap' from the earlier pack are left out because they name the Jan 2010 article's event, not this one. Lakeshore is kept separate. Only 'Launchpad Leap Party' is kept, because locale:7117 names it with Seaside.

Activities: the group launch pad jumping and bouncing activity came from article 906's summary, so it is removed. Client locale:6908 ('Wear your swim suits and beach wear. We'll be playing on launchpads and partying on the beach!', quest_dialog, unattributed) matches the wording, but no source names this party, so it is left unassigned and not cited.

Quest locale:7038 'Seaside Launchpad Leap' is NOT wired to this event. It is tied only by name and place, and article 906 shows the same name family ran in January 2010, so the quest may belong to that occurrence. Ids check: 7038 exists as quest_title.

Time zone inconsistency in the sources: articles 906 and 1254 state '9:00am Pacific / 6:00pm GMT' for January and April, but 9am Pacific is 5pm GMT in January (PST) and 4pm GMT in April (PDT). Article 1888 gives 4pm GMT for November 5, which is consistent with PDT. The GMT figures in 906 may be wrong. The Pacific times are the ones used here.
No NPC is named in a source tied to the party. locale:7117 is an unnamed NPC dialog line, so npcs is empty.

Launch pad furniture (locale:6178 Small Launch Pad, 6179 Medium Launch Pad, 6180 Large Launch Pad, wiki 'Large Launch Pad', article 1435 coin shop listing) is not tied to the party by any source, so items is empty.
Rewards are not stated in any source, so rewards is empty.

Snow Day items (locale:31301 'Snow Day: Launch Pad Leap', locale:426678 'Snow Day: Snowhill Leap') are undated and not tied to this party, so they are not counted as occurrences or aliases. They may be a separate winter event.
The pack's own description calls it a community event. Kind is set to community, though article 1888 also reads as a party on the launchpads with no ticket or currency.

evidence.claim: Announced as this week's community event: a kart race on the Torrentrueno racing circuit where the winner takes the whole race (Spanish: 'el ganador se lleva toda la carrera').
The announcement scheduled the event for Thursday 27 January 2011 at 15:00 Pacific Time (US and Latin America), on Server 1.
The announcement scheduled the event for Friday 28 January 2011 at 09:00 Pacific (16:00 European) for the UK and Europe, on Server 1.
Players reach the race by teleporting to the Torrentrueno circuit and clicking the Kart Lobby icon to join a race about to start or create one.
Race creation: set max players and turn off 'Habilitar IA' (AI) for a player-versus-player race.
The Thunder Falls kart racing track is called Torrentrueno in the Spanish text (single-source alias for the zone name).

open: Status: article 2011 announces the run in future tense ('el evento comunitario de esta semana sera...'). No source in the pack or index confirms it took place, so live is 'unsure', not 'yes'. The critique's point is accepted.

Recurrence is null. Article 2011 says 'esta semana' (this week's community event), which hints at a weekly series, but no source states a recurrence and no second dated run exists. The pack's 'weekly' label is unconfirmed.

Article 2013 has the same PvP kart challenge, same 'esta semana' wording and server-time pairs, and the index describes it as a 'weekly community event'. Its date is not in the pack or the index, so it is not an occurrence and does not support recurrence. Its date is needed.
The two 2011 time slots are one announcement, so they are one occurrence here, not two.

Possible merge, unresolved: article 2009 (weekly winner-takes-all kart race at Thunder Falls Speedway, 'Community Event', undated in the index) describes the same track and format. The pack may be merging it with this event, or it may be a separate weekly. Not merged here; its date is needed.

Possible merge or alias, unresolved: article 2015 (weekly community kart race at the Roaring Thunder Circuit / Circuit du Tonnerre Rugissant, Americas and Europe, Server 1) may be the same track under another name. Not merged.

Article 1913 (Demolition Derby at Thunder Falls/Torrentrueno, 18 November 2010) is a different event on the same track and is excluded. Article 235 (Frost Ridge Speedway, 28 August 2009), article 1700 (Wildwood Speedway, Summer Camp Racing Week), article 2045 (Wildwood Racing Challenge), article 2048 (Hojasilvestre, 10 March 2011) are other kart events and are excluded.
Thunder Falls zone equivalence rests on article 1913 alone; the index supports it only as 'called Torrentrueno in the Spanish text'. Kept as a single-source alias, not a settled fact.
Rewards are empty. 'The winner takes the whole race' may describe the race stake or just that the winner wins; no source names a reward or pot.

Items: no client kart item (Race Kart, Kart Race Tires, Kart Race Fuel, etc.) or wiki kart page (Buccaneer Racer, Arrow Runner, Wicked Racer, Splash Zipper, USA Racer) is tied to this event by any source. None listed.
NPCs: Tamara Violetwig appears in a Kart Race Lobby video frame (video:eCjjzP3ef0E/00022.jpg), but no source ties her to this event. Not listed.
Quests: no quest answers and no wiki quest pages in the pack or index tie to this event. Empty. The wiki pages Chase Wheeler and Laurin mention Thunder Falls Speedway but not this event; not listed.
The ids check for n067 returned no output (empty), so the event id is not verified in the index.
Zones list the Torrentrueno track name; the Thunder Falls mapping is single-source (article 1913).

Its link to the weekly series is inferred from matching activity and place, not stated by any article, so it is not a weekly occurrence. Lookup on the House Party articles returns no time-of-day text for 834, 2286 or 2492, and the article summaries only say 'two server groups' or 'two times for different regions' without the times. Each needs its own event record.

YEAR: 2112's pack date 2011-04-30 comes from a relative label ('posted 2 months, 2 weeks ago'), and the article summary says the year is inferred. 2011 rests on the June 2011 capture context of 2118 and the Saturday weekday match (April 30 was a Saturday in 2011). Articles 2118 and 2119 are undated, so their claims are used only for the same event's details.

ITEMS: none. No source ties an item to this event. Locale 510210 belongs to the 2013 Best Buy event, not this one. The 1186 article's Starter Cards exclusion and 2893's SMS exclusion belong to other promos and are not attributed here.
LIVE: 'live: yes' rests on past-tense wording ('held', 'will be hosting' on Apr 30). No client, quest or video evidence was found for this event.
ZONES/NPCS/QUESTS: none. Sources only describe Station Cash bonuses; no Free Realms-specific mechanics were given.
NAME: pack name is a generic label, so the alias list keeps only forms that match this specific Apr 30 event.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

evidence.claim: Article 2806 is a pre-launch post announcing an upcoming US 7-Eleven promotion: SOE Game Cards bought at 7-Eleven and redeemed for Station Cash give double Station Cash. The quote is 'get Double Station Cash when you redeem an SOE Game Card for Station Cash', exclusive to cards bought at US 7-Eleven stores.

The promo redemption window was 12:01 AM PST 11/16/12 to 11:59 PM PST 11/18/12 (Nov 16-18, 2012), per the offer terms quote in article 2806. This is the window the article announces, not confirmation that it ran.

Article 2807 gives the offer terms: 'Get Double Station Cash when you purchase the SOE Pre-Paid Game Card from 7-Eleven and redeem for Station Cash between 11/16/12 and 11/18/12'. The offer applied to Station Cash redemption only, not membership time. The posting date is not stated; the pack's 2012-11-16 is relative to capture and is not a posting date.
Redemption for membership time does not qualify for the double Station Cash offer.

open: Live status is unsure. The only sources for the window are announcements (2806 is explicitly upcoming; 2807 is undated and its wording is imperative, not evidence the promo ran). No post-window article in the pack confirms it ran. Check the freerealms.com news archive or a Ten Ton Hammer post from Nov 2012 before setting live to yes.

Name collision: 'Double Station Cash' is reused across separate promos, none included here. Europe Oct 7-10 2011 (articleId=2294); a Dec 2011 weekend ending Dec 19 (articleId=1970); Spring Celebration Mar 29-31 (articleId=2893); a Saturday PSN-breach compensation event (tentonhammer node 97967); Walmart Oct 12-14 2012 (pack). Also, articleIds 2717/2719 put a Best Buy Station Cash promo on 17-19 Aug 2012, while the pack lists Best Buy as Aug 16-18 2013. That date conflict needs resolving; do not merge it with this event.

Possible second occurrence, not counted: articleId=2923 summary says SOE Pre-Paid Cards redeemed for Station Cash during April 27-28, 2013 earned double Station Cash at US 7-Eleven. The summary also says the body never mentions Free Realms, so it may be a site-wide or different promo. Recurring stays null until this is checked. Source: articleId=2923 summary.

Excluded as separate events: 7-Eleven Day, July 11 2013 (articleId=2945; SC500 plus a free Slurpee, not the double-SC offer); the 7-Eleven bundle of March 18 to April 19 2010 (locale:4889 Slobbersaurus-Rex and its wiki page). The pack's name match should not merge these.

tentonhammer node 74525 lists participating retailers (7-Eleven, Best Buy, Blockbuster, CVS, Rite Aid, Speedway, Target, Toys R Us, Walmart) for an unidentified promotion. It is not tied to this window by any source, so it is removed from evidence.

Client and wiki check is incomplete. The pack reports no client locale or wiki category members for this event. My own lookup across client/wiki/articles/video for 'Double Station Cash 7-Eleven' returned an FTS5 error on the hyphen, and I did not rerun it in a form that works. So no client tie is confirmed by me.

ids check: 'ids 2806 2807' does not resolve article ids. It returns locale:2806 and locale:2807 ('Chatty Baseball Cap' crit-chance strings), which are unrelated. 'ids 2923' returns locale:2923 'Postman Gear', also unrelated. No locale item is tied to this event.

No items, zones, NPCs, quests or quest answers are sourced. The 'Double Station Cash' bonus is a currency multiplier, not an item. The video frame video:e4XXSnnive0/00058.jpg is an undated card ad and was not used.

Name may be an alias problem: the article titles say '7-Eleven Double Station Cash Weekend' (2807) and 'What is New? (7-Eleven Double Station Cash Weekend)' (2806). Both use the same name, so no alias is needed beyond the pack name.

svall-day-birthday-party.title: All Day Birthday Party

evidence.claim: The 1st anniversary All Day Birthday Party ran as eight hourly parties, one per region, on Thursday April 29, 2010, 9am-5pm PDT, each doubling as an Ambassador Hide and Seek game.
The birthday party ran from the announcement until May 10, 2010, and the festivities were scheduled to end on 10 May 2010.
Parties were set up in eight zones named in English: Joyful Vale, Criqueville, Snow Hill, Misty Glade, Wugachug, Blackspore, Heather Moor and Sanctuary.
Camellia, near the great tree in Sanctuary, starts the birthday party quests, and other Sanctuary residents also give quests, including some members-only ones.
The party's cake boss Gatostein (English client name Cakenstein) must be defeated seven times during the birthday event; fireworks work against it.
Cakenstein is the result of a baking accident in Glerga's kitchen, a Robgoblin chef, when she added Mystery Meat to a bake-off recipe.
The official 1st anniversary guide lists daily activities: cake bake-off with Camellia, Flitter's invitation contest, Quills' balloon trade, Helga's feast ingredients and the Cakenstein boss fights.
Chef Jarvie in Happy Valley is part of the 1st anniversary celebration activities, per the guide.
Free Realms' 1st birthday celebration was set to begin April 29, 2010, with new in-game events and prizes to follow.
Birthday Party Crates were created for the first anniversary, contain party supplies, and were sold in the Marketplace.
Completing party quests yields birthday gifts; anniversary gifts include balloon weapons, t-shirts and illusions.

Eight party areas are named in German (Jubeltal, Sanddorf, Schneehugel, Schleierwiese, Wugachug, Pfifferdorf, Dornenwald, Freistatte) with players starting at Sanctuary (Freistatte). No source maps these German names to the English zone names.

Ambassador Hide and Seek also ran as a standalone event (articleId 212 and 220, Aug 21, 2009; articleId 2060 Snowhill). Those are separate events and are excluded.

Quest titles: the articles describe quests but give no exact in-game titles, so quests stays empty. Client quest_title 'Birthday Party! Yay!' (locale:139313) matches by name only and is not tied to 2010 by any source, so it stays out.

Activity quest references were relabelled as article ids, not quest ids. The lookup gave no source for the claim that Cakenstein becomes invulnerable when a gatolin brings it cake, and no source for articleId 1306, so that claim is dropped.
Alias 'Free Realms 1st Birthday Celebration' is kept now, sourced to tentonhammer node 83604 ('Free Realms' 1st birthday celebration'). The exact official name is not confirmed by any source.

Zones now list the eight English party zones from articleId 1267. Robgoblin Camp is kept only in activities for the Helga and Glerga quest steps (1282, 1293), not as a party zone. Happy Valley appears only in the Chef Jarvie activity (1293), not as a party zone. The German area names (articleId 2099) have no English mapping in the pack, so they are evidence only. Article 2099 has no printed date.
Chef Jarvie is listed as an NPC from articleId 1293. Her quest role is not stated beyond the guide's mention.

Cake-collecting reward from the Cakenstein boss was not confirmed in the lookup output, so it is not listed in rewards. Article 1197's unnamed rewards and the undated article 1136 coin reward stay out.

Items: Birthday Party Balloons 3-Pack (locale:14422), 4-Pack (14423), Banner (14424) and Hat (19955) match by name only. No source ties them to the 2010 party. Left out. Crate price is not in any source (wiki price blank); currency station_cash comes from the wiki's 'SC Marketplace' wording.

Ten Ton Hammer node 83604 has no posting date in the corpus, so it is used only for the alias and the preview wording, not for a date. Live status rests on articleId 1267 ('was held in the game') and 1308 ('ran on Thursday'). Preview-tense wording in 83041 and 83604 does not count on its own.
Recurring is null: only one occurrence of this event is in the pack. The anniversary itself recurs each April 29 (wiki Birthday Bash), but that is a different named event.
Kind chosen as 'community' (Community Team anniversary party). 'holiday' would also fit an anniversary, so this is a judgment call.

Article 2462 ('Verschenkt Doppel Station Cash!') is a separate German gift-purchase promotion, not part of this event. The 'Stocking Stuffer' title comes only from article 1974. Whether the 2011 German promotion is the same event under another name is not proven. The name is kept for 2010 only.
The alias 'Doppel Station Cash' is only a headline in a summary field, not a page title. Treat it as a candidate alias.

open: Wireable: not wireable as a server calendar entry. Power Hour is a per-player daily window that starts at each player's first login of the day, and no source gives a server-wide start or end. The calendar needs a per-login daily window type before this can be scheduled. Keep it out of the server calendar until that type exists. The answer format has no wireable field, so this is recorded here.

Pack problem: 'Power Hour' is a daily member coin-doubling mechanic, not a dated event with a window. live=yes means the feature was in the client and documented in 2010 notes and 2011/2013 HUD captures. It does not mean an event run. Decide whether the calendar should hold it or whether it belongs to the membership/coin system. kind=other is kept for that reason.

Activities widened per critique: article 967 says coin rewards from all activities are doubled for Members. Quests and Dungeons are the wiki's examples only. Spot the Difference is not listed as an activity: article 2907 is undated and gives a tip, not an event fact.

Critique fix 2 (occurrences/aliases): one occurrence only, 27-28 Jan 2011, Server 1. articleId=2011 and 2013 are one announcement, not two events, and the calendar must not count them twice. Not independently verified that they are not two posts of one announcement; the lookup shows identical times in both.

Critique fix 3 (wireable): the required answer format has no wireable field, so it cannot be set here. Recorded as not schedulable: store as a historical one-off (27-28 Jan 2011, Torrentrueno kart PvP race, Server 1). Do not schedule as recurring until a second dated occurrence is found.

Live status: 'live' is recorded as unsure for the calendar. The articles confirm the 27-28 Jan 2011 sessions ran. No result or end-of-event article was found, and the archive has only announcement wording.

Pack merge risk, unresolved: the English 2009 Thunder Falls Speedway weekly winner-takes-all race (articleId=2009) is NOT tied to this January 2011 Torrentrueno event. It is not used for recurrence, activities, zones or dates. Treat as a separate series or an unverified merge until a source links them.
Alias gap: the English event name in the pack ('Community Event: Kart race challenge') and the Spanish title may be the same event. Not verified beyond the same article pair.
Dates: both article posting dates are null in the pack. The year 2011 comes from the Spanish date text in the quotes. Only one dated occurrence exists.
UK/Europe time: the quoted 16:00 European figure does not match 09:00 Pacific under standard January offsets (09:00 PST is 17:00 GMT and 18:00 CET). Not used as a converted value.
Rewards: 'the winner takes the whole race' implies a pot, but no source says what it is (coins, Station Cash or nothing). Rewards left empty.

Items: client kart items (Race Kart locale:5101173, Kart Race Tires locale:67585, Kart Race Fuel locale:67586, Kart Race Lobby locale:3052) and Kart Racer quests (locale 3497-3582) are general kart content. No source ties them to this event, so none are listed.
Quests: no quest answer in the pack mentions this event, and no client quest was tied to it by a source.
NPCs: no NPC is named in any source for this event.

Other events: lookup matched Demolition Derby (18 Nov 2010, articleId=1913, same Thunder Falls track, Server 1), Fishing Derby, Stampede, Story Time and Lot Racing. Only the Demolition Derby is at the same track, and it is a separate event, not this one.

evidence.claim: Article 1910 announces a Demolition Derby Day at Thunder Falls Speedway on Server 1, with a U.S./Latin America session on Thursday November 18, 2010 at 3pm Pacific. The quote is 'Thursday November 18th, 2010 3pm Pacific Time (U.S. and Latin America) Server 1'.

Article 1910 gives a UK/Europe session on Friday November 19, 2010 at 9:00am Pacific on Server 1. The quote is 'Friday November 19th, 2010 9:00am Pacific Time / 4:00pm GMT (UK and Europe) Server 1'. The GMT figure conflicts with Pacific under PST (9:00am Pacific is 5:00pm GMT), so only the Pacific time is used.

The event is labelled 'Community Event' in client text: 'Scheduled: Community Event: Demolition Derby'. This is the source for kind 'community'. Article 1910's 'community event post' wording comes from the pack summary, not a quote from the article, so it is not used as the label source.
Client text ties the event to Thunder Falls and Server 1: 'Meet at the Thunder Falls Demolition Derby track ... Enter the lobby to find a match. SERVER 1'.
Article 1910 places the event at Thunder Falls Speedway: 'Head to the Thunder Falls Speedway and get ready to crash some karts!'.
Article 1910 says players learn to drive karts from Crash Davis, who gives the equipment and training to become demolition derby drivers. The equipment is not named in any source.
Article 1910 says players enter via the demo derby turnstile and the 'Demo Derby Lobby' to find a match.
Article 1910 says events are found through the Game Guide calendar.

Crash Davis is listed as a derby trainer at Thunder Falls Speedway on the wiki, and client dialog (locale:116904) sends players to him for derby driver training. Both are job-trainer facts, not specific to this event.
evidence.source: Demolition Derby Driver (wiki, Trainers list); locale:116904

evidence.claim: Only one article in the pack names this event, so no recurrence is sourced.

open: event: 'Demolition Derby Day' is sourced only by article 1910 for the announcement. The kind label comes from locale:6674, which matches the client's 'Community Event: Demolition Derby'. That label is the same as the 'Demolition Derby' job, minigame and tutorial name, so do not merge them. This entry covers only the scheduled community event.

event.aliases: 'Demolition Derby' comes from the client event label (locale:6674). 'Demo Derby' comes from article 1910 ('demo derby turnstile'). Both names are shared with the job, so treat them as weak aliases.
kind: 'community' is supported by client label locale:6674. Article 1910 is an announcement post; the 'community event post' wording is from the pack summary, not a quote.

live: 'unsure'. Article 1910 has no article date in the pack. The sessions on Nov 18-19 2010 are stated, but no source confirms they ran as announced. Treat as unconfirmed until an article date or a post-event report is found.

occurrences: two sessions are listed, both from article 1910 on Server 1 in 2010. They are two sessions of one event, not recurrences. The Nov 19 GMT figure is a source inconsistency and is not used. The Nov 18 session has no GMT figure in the article.
recurring: null. Two sessions in one announcement do not make a recurrence, and no article says it recurs.
zones: Thunder Falls Speedway is sourced by article 1910 and locale:6678. The 'Demo Derby Lobby' is named in the article but its zone or sub-zone is not confirmed, so it is not listed as a zone.

npcs: Crash Davis is tied to the event by article 1910 (fact:npc). The wiki places him at Thunder Falls Speedway as a trainer, but that is job-trainer info, not event-specific. Burt 'Wrecking' Crewe, Rip Ringa and Mad Jack appear in the wiki as trainers at other tracks and are not tied to this event. 'Demolition Derby Trainer' (locale:20094) is not tied to this event.

quests: none tied to this event. 'Demolition Derby Tutorial' (locale:117325) and the dialog at locale:116904 are job-tutorial text. 'Snow Day: Frost Ridge Demo Derby' (locale:31359) and '12 Days 2013 - Day 11: Snowhill Demo Derby' (locale:441194, 441195, 441119, 441117) are different events and are excluded.
activities: learn to drive karts from Crash Davis (article 1910); enter the demo derby lobby and find a match at Thunder Falls (article 1910, locale:6678).

items: none. No source ties any item to this event. Demolition Derby Sticker (locale:442139, 442149), Demolition Derby Equipment (locale:5102703), Demo Derby Kart (locale:3723) and the Crash Cup weapon are not tied to this event. The equipment Crash Davis gives is not named in any source. Items are left empty.
rewards: none sourced. The article lists none.
evidence_gap: the pack has no price or currency for this event, which is consistent with a free community event but is not confirmed.

pack_merge_risk: article 188 (Aug 7, 2009, 2pm-4pm Pacific, all servers, Wildwood Speedway, 'Community Team' event with a demolition derby) is a separate event at a different track, but its format is similar and it may be an earlier run of the same series. Do not merge it into this entry without an article or client source. The weekly kart race 'Community Event: Thunder Falls Racing Challenge' (locale:2787, article 2009 on Jan 27-28, 2011) is also a separate event at the same track. The Frost Ridge and Snowhill derby quests are separate events and are excluded.

Halloween Harry: Sanctuary (about 30 client lines, article 1864) versus Pixiewood (locale 436401, 416800). Both appear in client text; not resolved.
Year-count conflict: articleId=2949 says 'Fourth Annual' for 2013, while 2009 'First Annual' and 2010 'second annual' imply 2013 is the fifth. Wording kept as quoted.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

Sunstone Valley was a new area of Free Realms that the webcast was to present.

Sunstone Valley later opened as Free Realms' first expansion zone, with roughly 50 quests. The article is undated in the lookup, so its order relative to the 30 August 2012 announcement is not established.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

Zando is the only Free Realms item tied to this event by a source. Article 870 and node 79393 say 'items' priced at 500 SC without naming them, and the wiki category membership in the pack is empty, so other Free Realms items under this promotion are unverified.
Recipient wording differs: the articles say 'Haiti relief' or 'Haiti Relief and Development Effort', and Ten Ton Hammer names the American Red Cross. Both are kept in evidence.
