Free Agents receive access to member content at no additional charge.
Sony Online Entertainment would announce Free Agent recruiting on the Free Realms What's New web page, via an ad banner or news feed.
The page was captured March 2009, before the April 2009 launch, per the article summary; the pack gives date null.

open: Answer object: event {name: "Free Agents", aliases: ["Free Realms Free Agents"]}; kind: "community" (low confidence, a sign-up feedback and promotion program, not an event with a date); live: "no" (pre-launch plan, only source is the March 2009 FAQ page); occurrences: [] (no dated occurrence in any source; the only article has date null and describes a plan); recurring: null; zones, npcs, quests, activities, items, rewards: [] (no source ties any of these to the program; the lookups returned no client, wiki or quest hits for Free Agents).
No wiki page, wiki category member or quest answer mentions Free Agents. The pack's wiki_category_members is empty, so the category-based item and NPC lists cannot be filled.

No article or client string shows an actual Free Agent recruitment round, selection, or a live period after the April 2009 launch. Whether the program ran after launch, and when, is unknown. A follow-up search of the articles for later What's New or news posts about Free Agents is needed.

The pack's single article is an FAQ with no date, so the pack cannot give a year for any occurrence. The quote 'Free Agents get member content at no additional charge' is from the article summary; the exact wording is 'access to member content'.
Lookups for 'recruiting', 'special access' and 'recruitment' matched only unrelated quest dialogs, wiki guild pages and chat text. These are not Free Agent sources and were not used.

Possible alias or merge issue: the pack's names_seen lists only 'Free Agents'. Other Free Realms recruiting or beta-tester programs may share the same vocabulary; this pack does not show whether any were merged under this name.
The event needs a checked-in source for its date, status and any run after launch before the events calendar can list it. Until then it should be marked as a pre-launch plan, not a live event.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

svseaside-launch-pad-leap.title: Seaside Launch Pad Leap

event.name: Seaside Launch Pad Leap
aliases: Community Event: Seaside Launch Pad Leap

occurrences.when: Friday January 29, 2010 (3pm Pacific US/LatAm; 9am Pacific UK/EU), Server 1, meet on the Seaside beach. Announced in article 906; held status not confirmed by that article.

activities: Meet up on the Seaside beach and bounce on the launch pads together, as a group, to see how many players can bounce at once (goal about 30 players).

evidence.claim: Article 906 announces a community event called Seaside Launch Pad Leap on Server 1 in Seaside, where players meet on the beach to bounce on launch pads together.

Article 906 gives the start times as 3pm Pacific (U.S. and Latin America) and 9:00am Pacific (UK and Europe), both on Server 1. The article's GMT figure for UK/Europe (6pm) does not match 9am Pacific (about 5pm GMT in January), so only the Pacific times are used.

Article 906 quote is future tense ('Meet up on the beach and we'll see how many people we can get bouncing at once'), so the article reads as a pre-event announcement. Its summary also reads as an announcement and gives no posting date (relative capture only).
Client NPC dialog 'Bring a swimsuit and your jumping shoes, it's a Launchpad Leap Party in Seaside!' ties the Seaside launch pad event to the client text; the speaker is not identified.

open: Live status is unsure. Article 906 is a pre-event announcement by its quote and summary. Its fact text says the event 'was held' on Friday January 29, 2010, but no fetched text in the pack confirms that. Do not count it as a held event until a post-event source is found.
The January 29, 2010 date comes from the fact text for article 906. The article's own date is null in the pack, so the year and day are not independently verified from the article body.

Separate events, not aliases. Article 1254 covers Lakeshore Launch Pad Leap (Thursday April 15, 2010, Lakeshore dock, Server 1; US/LatAm 3pm Pacific and UK/EU 9am Pacific; held). It is a different town and is not counted here. Client locale 6538 names 'Community Event: Lakeshore Launch Pad Leap'. Article 1888 covers Launch Pad Party (Thursday November 4, 2010, US/LatAm 3pm Pacific; Friday November 5, 2010, UK/EU 9am Pacific; Seaside launchpads, Server 1; held). The pack does not say these are one series, so the alias 'Launch Pad Party' is not claimed for this event.

The wiki Community Events page describes a Launch Pad Party as an event where players jumped on the Seaside launch pads. It supports a Launch Pad Party in Seaside, but it does not link that event to the Seaside Launch Pad Leap article 906. The wiki category member list for this event is empty.

Recurring is null. The pack contains no source that says the Seaside Leap recurs. Launch Pad Party (Nov 2010) and Lakeshore Leap (Apr 2010) are separate events and do not show a yearly or weekly cadence for this one.
Quest title 'Seaside Launchpad Leap' (locale 7038) is an unverified title match with no steps, date or NPC in the pack. Not listed under quests.
Snowhill 'Snow Day: Launch Pad Leap' (locale 31301) has no dated article in the pack. Not counted and not listed in zones.
No NPC is tied to the event. Locale 7117 has no speaker name.

Items are empty. The wiki Items list shows Medium and Large Launch Pad as furniture-style entries, but no source ties them to this event. Small Launch Pad (locale 6178) has no source describing it, so its classification is unverified.
No rewards are tied to the event by any source in the pack.
Locale 426819 ('Launch Pad Leap') is an ability/mechanic name, not a dated event, and is not used as evidence of an occurrence.

open: Not an event. This is a one-off server maintenance notice, so the event name, kind and recurrence are a poor fit for the events calendar. Confirm whether the calendar should hold maintenance windows at all, or only ran-as-live events.

live is unsure: the only source is a pre-event notice in future tense. Nothing confirms the maintenance happened, when it ended, or whether it was extended. A later article or forum post confirming it is needed.
No items, NPCs, zones, quests, activities or rewards. The article is explicitly content-free ('gives no patch contents'), and the wiki category and quest answers are empty.

The pack's name is the article title, 'Server maintenance, July 28, 2010'. It has no separate event name, so aliases is empty. It may be one of several maintenance notices merged under the generic title, but nothing in the pack shows that.

evidence.claim: Event is a limited-time 5M celebration for the 5,000,000th registered Free Realms player. Players could log in daily to spin a special 5M Party Wheel.
Event window was September 16 to September 23, 2009. Players had to log in to Free Realms during that window.
The article lists the event's virtual rewards as one Party Crate, one Silly String can, three Party Poppers and one Grab Bag.
Client item 407352 is named exactly 'Party Crate'. The article's reward list names the Party Crate, so the item is tied to the event through the article.
Client item 408149 'Silly String Can' carries the note 'Used for 5M item: Silly String Can', tying it to the 5M event. This matches the article's reward list.

Party Popper is in the article's reward list. Client note 407421 'Used for 5M item: Party Popper' is flagged as placeholder sample text, so it is not used as evidence. No client item id is confirmed for the Party Popper reward.
Grab Bag is in the article's reward list. Client names 'Grab Bag' (141315) and 'Grab Bags' (67549) exist, but no source says which is the event reward, so it is not in the item list.
Client id 407350 'Spawn 5M GM Crate' is flagged FLAG dev_note as an internal GM spawn label. Nothing ties it to 407348 or to the player rewards, so it is excluded.
Client item 407348 '5M GM Crate' carries only its name. No source ties it to this event as a player reward, so it is excluded.
Client item 156744 '5 Million Party Pack' exists and its name carries the 5 Million number. No source links it to the article's rewards, so it is excluded.
The 1M Party bash (Friday May 15, 2009, 5pm PT, Snowhill, for one million registered users within 17 days of launch) is a separate, earlier celebration and is not part of this event.
evidence.source: wiki page 'Bruce' (lookup text for the 1M Party); corroborated by http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=113 (Snowhill party, 1,000,000 registered players, May 15, 2009)

open: Only one occurrence (2009, Sep 16-23). Recurring is null because nothing says it recurs.
The article date 2009-09-16 is inferred from the capture date and a relative 'posted 6 days, 3 hours ago' stamp. The window dates themselves are stated in the article.
Live is 'yes' because the article says it ran during the window, which closed 2009-09-23. Confirm whether the calendar needs an explicit ended flag.
Kind is 'promotion' (daily login wheel for free rewards). 'community' (milestone celebration) could also fit. Pick one for the calendar.
No prices or currency are given. Rewards are virtual prizes from the wheel, so currency is 'reward' with price null.
Zones, NPCs and quests: no source in the pack or lookup ties any of these to this event. Left empty.
Grab Bag reward is unresolved. The article names it, but the client has 141315 'Grab Bag' and 67549 'Grab Bags' with no event tie. Not in the item list. Needs a human check.
Party Popper reward has no confirmed client item id. Client 407421 is placeholder text, so the item is listed by article name only.
Item 156744 '5 Million Party Pack' is not tied to the article's rewards. It may or may not equal the Party Crate. It is excluded. Confirm if needed.
407348 '5M GM Crate' and 407350 'Spawn 5M GM Crate' are GM-side items with no source tying them to player rewards. 407350 is an internal dev_note label. Both excluded.
Aliases: '5M Party Wheel' is the same event by the article title. The pack does not merge it with the 1M Party bash (May 2009), which is a separate event. The pack may also miss other aliases.
The 1M Party wiki citation is the lookup entry for wiki page 'Bruce', which holds the 1M Party text. The page title looks odd, so the article 113 link is the more reliable corroboration.
Video frames were not searched. Wiki category members and quest answers were empty in the pack.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

open: MERGE: the pack merges several years under one name. Split by year: 2010 (articles 1261, 1267, 1268, 1308; pre-launch decorations 83041), 2011 (2107, 2099, 2094, 2093), 2012 (2580, wiki news 2012), 2013 (2924). Treat as one recurring event with per-year occurrences.
ALIAS: 'Birthday Bash' is the 2012+ name (wiki category and articles). Added as alias.

DATE CONFLICT: the anniversary is April 28 in the 2009 launch post (2109), the 2011 and 2012 articles (2107, 2098, 2580) and TenTonHammer 83041 (2010). It is April 29 in Free Realms' 2010 articles (1267, 1268, 1308, 1197), TenTonHammer 83604, the 2013 article (2924) and the wiki Birthday Bash category. Recorded per year as the article states; the conflict stands.

PRE-LAUNCH 2010: decorations were to appear in game from mid-April 2010 (TenTonHammer 83041). This is a plan, so it is a separate pre-launch entry and not a live occurrence. The live party window starts on the posting day, which the articles do not give.
2010 YEAR: closed. Article 1267 states the first anniversary fell on April 29, 2010 directly, so the year is not inferred from 1261.
2010 START: the posting day is not stated in the articles (1261 date null). Start is 'posting day' only.

2011 WEBCAST DATE: article 2094 gives Thursday at 4:00 pm US Pacific time (time confirmed). Article 2093 gives Thursday 2 April 2011 and article 2098 gives Thursday April 21 (20:00 Brasilia), so the date conflicts and is left open. The time is not in 2093 or 2098, so it is cited to 2094 alone.

ZONES: article 1261 says eight areas but names none; article 1308 says hourly in different regions, also unnamed. Sanctuary is tied by Camellia (wiki) and 2924. Shrouded Glade, Seaside, Snowhill, Merry Vale, Sanctuary and Wugachug come from the six cake items (locale 9392-9397), which are name-only; no article ties them to party areas. Blackspore Swamp and Briarwood come from undated wiki T-shirt pages. Queensfields and Sacred Grove are removed from zones: they are Cakenstein battle locations (articles 1282, 2580 per the pack, not re-run), not party areas.
PRICES: no source gives a price for any party item. Wiki Birthday Crates says 'sell for .' with the number blank. Crate currency station_cash rests only on the wiki's SC Marketplace mention.

BALLOON WEAPONS: currency set to reward because article 2106 gives them as quest presents. The wiki also lists them under Coin Shop Weapons, Prize Wheel Weapons and Marketplace Items, so they are also sold; no price is given.
PARTY CRASHER: a power attack shared by all Birthday Bash weapons (wiki Category:Party Crasher), not a reward. The schema has no abilities field, so it is recorded here and removed from rewards.

ANNIVERSARY FIREWORK: removed from items and rewards. Video C3fysVLxrMg/00540 shows it beside a Birthday Party Crate, but the pack's other frames show it in unrelated contexts, and the only firework article (136) concerns a different item. Unconfirmed; no year, no price.
BIRTHDAY CAKE HAT (2012 login reward): removed. The lookup for 'birthday cake login hat' returned no matches, and the 2580 summary describes the bake-off and Cakenstein, not a login hat. Unconfirmed.

NAME-ONLY LOCALE ITEMS: Birthday Party Banner (locale 14424), Birthday Party Hat (19955) and Birthday Party Balloons 3-Pack (14422) exist in the client (ids check), but no dated or event-specific source ties them to the event. Unconfirmed candidates, removed from items. The six Birthday Cake Samples items (9392-9397) are listed as name-only candidates with currency null.

NPCS: Camellia is confirmed by the wiki page only (year unknown). Cakenstein is a boss creature, not an NPC. Queen Valerian (2012), Glerga, Commander Kiggle and General Glowlight come from the pack and were not re-run. Bud Grimyfoot appears only in video frames with no tie, so he is left out.

QUEST TITLES: 'Birthday Cake Bake-off' is read from wiki Camellia 'Quest:[Birthday] Cake Bake-off'. The brackets mark the matched query word in the lookup output, not a title change. 'A Piece of Cake' and 'Undelivered Confections' also come only from that wiki page. 'Cakenstein Attacks!' is confirmed in the minigame frame. Quests from article 1282 and the Glerga quests have no exact title in the pack.
NAME VARIANT: article text says 'Birthday Crates' and locale 5664 says 'Birthday Party Crate'. Both are recorded.

BIRTHDAY HIDE AND SEEK (locale 6540, Community Event) and the 1197 all-day community party: the 2010 hourly party is now tied to 2010 by article 1308. Hide and Seek has no year and is not tied to this event, so it is left out of activities.

2012 END DATE (May 24) and 2013 details: May 24 is from the pack and was not re-run. Article 2924 confirms only the Ambassadors dancing and the Sanctuary area, so the 2013 entry has no further activities.
LIVE: yes for 2010-2012 (dated articles). 2013 is a brief post. The 2010 pre-launch decorations are a preview and are not counted as live.

evidence.claim: The client names the event 'Community Event: Memorial Caverns Pool Party' (locale 9108), which ties the name to the Memorial Caverns and to a community event category.

A community Memorial Caverns pool party was held in the pools below the Memorial Caverns, hosted by the Community Team, with high dives, dancing, silly string fights and swimming on Server 1. Its US/Latin America session was Thursday January 20th, 2011 at 3pm Pacific Time, and its UK/Europe session was Friday January 21st, 2011 at 9:00am Pacific Time, both on Server 1.

The French announcement gives the same sessions: Thursday 20 January 2011 at 3pm Pacific for US and Latin America, and Friday 21 January 2011 at 18:00 CET for UK and Europe, on Server 1. It adds duels to the activities. The article's own gloss reads 4:00 GMT for 18:00 CET, which conflicts with the Pacific time (see open).

The Spanish announcement gives the same dated sessions: Thursday 20 January 2011 at 15:00 Pacific Time (US and Latin America) and Friday 21 January 2011 at 09:00 Pacific Time (UK and Europe), on Server 1. It describes a pool party with dancing, confetti cannons and swimming in the pools beneath the Caverns of Memory. Its '16:00 European Time' gloss conflicts with 9am Pacific (see open).

Article 2003 places the Caverns of Memory in the depths of the Sanctuary caves, reached through the atlas and the Forgotten Caves battle. Its dates, server, community-team host and activities match the Memorial Caverns pool party, which supports treating Caverns of Memory as an alias. The article does not name Memorial Caverns, so the link rests on matching details rather than an explicit name.

The pack's 'Memorial Caverns collection updates' is an undated location note, not an event. Article 144 says only that collection updates are available inside Memorial Caverns. It is listed in open, not as this event's identity.
Memorial Caverns is a Sanctuary museum on Pixie and Sanctuary history, located north of the World Tree.

open: Time conflict in the sources. 9am Pacific in January (PST, UTC-8) is 17:00 GMT, which equals 18:00 CET. The recorded time for the UK/Europe session is 17:00 GMT = 18:00 CET = 9am Pacific. The sources' '4pm GMT' (articleId 2002) and '4:00 GMT' beside 18:00 CET (articleId 2007) conflict with their own Pacific and CET times, and articleId 2003's '16:00 European Time' also conflicts with 9am Pacific. The Jan 20 US/LatAm session (3pm Pacific = 23:00 GMT) is consistent.

The pack name 'Memorial Caverns collection updates' merges two things. The one-line collection-updates note (articleId 144, undated) is not an event. The event is the Memorial Caverns Pool Party (articleIds 2002, 2003, 2007), and the event name and aliases are the pool party.

The Caverns of Memory alias rests on matching details (same Jan 20/21 2011 sessions, Server 1, community team, dancing and swimming), not on an explicit name match, since articleId 2003 never names Memorial Caverns.

The pack's article dates are null. The dates above come from the article text. Article 2007 gives no publication date; the store's 'four and a half months before a June 2011 capture' remark is a capture-date note, not a publication date, so no publication date is stated.
Only one occurrence (January 2011, both sessions) is sourced. Nothing says it recurred, so recurring is null.

Live is 'yes' for the January 2011 sessions only, based on announcement text ('was held' in articles 2002 and 2007). The announcements do not confirm attendance, and a pre-launch preview would not count.

No item, price, currency, NPC, quest or reward is tied to the pool party by any source. The 'Memorial Caverns Explorer's ...' clothing and backpacks (locale 29150, 30259, 30996, 29388) and the Looking for Volunteers and tour quests are named after the place, not the event, and are excluded.

Unresolved neighbour, not a settled exclusion: the wiki Items page lists '[VIP] Party [Pool]', and video frames (vY6GXmnE6eM/00016.jpg at Adventurer 20 and WSpXvhq_VCY/00256.jpg, 00258.jpg) show 'VIP [Party] [Pool]' with 'Buy now and save! Time Left: 17 Hours'. A 'Party Pool' place also exists (locale 6633/6634). No source ties these to the January 2011 pool party. They may be a later or separate store or housing event, and this answer does not assert which.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

ALIASES: 'Reto Futbolístico' and 'Evento Comunitario: Reto Futbolístico' are the article titles of articleId 1622 (accents as in the source title). 'Sports Week' and 'Semana Deportiva' are withdrawn from this event's aliases (they belong to the parent week). 'Summer Camp soccer event 2010' is a descriptive label, not a source name, and is removed.

DATE GAP for the week: articles 1596, 1601 and 1622 carry no date in the index. The week's exact dates are unknown, so no week occurrence can be added until a dated source turns up. The only dated occurrence is the scheduled July 8-9 2010 session from articleId 1621.

LIVE STATUS: live is 'unsure'. Only one dated occurrence exists, announced in articleId 1621. The sources show a scheduled time, not that the event took place, that it recurs, or that it is live now. Attendance and occurrence are unconfirmed.
ZONES: Greenwood Forest (Chatty's camp, articleId 1510) is removed. Articles 1510 and 1498 place the Summer Camp season camps there, not this event.
ACTIVITIES: the Sports Week challenge and house party (articleId 1596, 1601) are week-level and are removed from this event. The three activities above are tied to this event only by articleId 1622.

UNVERIFIED SEASON CLAIMS: earlier Ten Ton Hammer claims (13 weekly themes, season release June 7 2010, 14 camp land quests), articleId 1624 (Arts and Crafts Week), and articleIds 1661 and 1780 are removed. They could not be re-verified and are season context, not facts about this event.

NOT TIED, NOT IN ITEMS: locale:5630 'Soccer Ball' (item) and locale:402749 'Soccer: Snowhill' (place) exist, but no source ties them to this event. Left out. The 'Zona de Juego' ball is an in-game interaction object from articleId 1622, not a priced item, so it is listed under activities.
NOT TIED, NOT IN NPCS: locale:410136 'Fred Futbol' exists, but the sources tie him to the Soccer Star job, not this event.

NOT TIED, NOT IN QUESTS: locale:31340 'Soccer Saturday', locale:441714 'Jojo's Mojo' and locale:441718 'Jojo's Dojo' exist, but no source ties them to this event. locale:402750 'Soccer: Briarwood' also exists and is unlinked.
REWARDS: no source states a reward for this event. Left empty.
WIKI: the pack has no wiki category pages for this event, so no wiki source is cited. A lookup for 'Semana Deportiva' and 'Sports Week' returned no wiki page tied to this event.

evidence.claim: The Double Member Discount Event ran from September 1, 2010 at 11:59am PDT to September 8, 2010 at 11:59am PDT and was limited to Members.
During the event, Members got 20% off Station Cash marketplace purchases, up from the normal 10%.
The event is a limited-time SOE news post, so it is a promotion (a discount), not a holiday, theme or update.
The normal Member discount on Station Cash marketplace items is 10%, and the Membership page lists it as a standing benefit.
No wiki page, quest or client string names the Double Member Discount Event itself. The wiki hits for Member discount show the standing 10% benefit, not this event.
evidence.source: wiki lookup: Archer Power Bow, Upshot Archer Quiver, Athletic Shades, Membership

open: The event's year and dates come from one article (articleId=1782). The Sept 1-8 2010 dates are given in the article text.

live is set to 'yes' because the article is a live SOE news post that states the dates. It is not a pre-launch preview. Only one live source was found, so this is not corroborated by a second article.
recurring is null. Only one occurrence is attested. No article says it recurs.

Pack alias risk: the event is probably not the same as the 30% Members Only weekend promotion in locale:1735 and locale:1738 ('This weekend members save big by getting 30% off all Station Cash items'), nor the 'Super Fan Holidays' triple member discount in articleId=1933 (30% off Station Cash). items is empty. The article applies the discount to all Station Cash marketplace purchases, not to a named item list. svarts-and-crafts-week.title: Arts and Crafts Week

event.name: Arts and Crafts Week
aliases: Summer Camp - Arts and Crafts Week

activities: Blacksmiths and Cooks create new items from raw materials (metals from mining, food from harvesting)
Dance to boombox music
Build block sculptures at houses

items.name: Merri's Marinated Mystery Meat
items.source: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=1624 (cited as the example cooking item for the week)

evidence.claim: Arts and Crafts Week is a weekly theme of the Summer Camp community event season; each week celebrates a different theme and this week's theme was Arts and Crafts Week.
During the week, Blacksmiths and Cooks create brand new items from raw materials; raw materials come from mining metals or harvesting food.
Players could dance to boombox music and build block sculptures at their houses during the week.
Merri's Marinated Mystery Meat is the example cooking item referenced for Arts and Crafts Week.
The article is a live-game community event post, not a pre-launch preview; it describes the week in past tense ('this week's theme was').

Summer Camp 2010 season ended with Pet Week as its final theme, and the last Summer Camp event was the Pet Parade on Sept 2-3, 2010. This places the season in 2010, but not the Arts and Crafts week itself.
Locale lookup for 'Arts and Crafts' returned no matches, so the client does not name this event.

open: Date unresolved: article 1624 has no absolute date (only '1 week, 5 days ago'), so no year or week can be stated from its own text. Season year 2010 comes from article 1775 (Pet Week, final theme of the 2010 Summer Camp season). Whether Arts and Crafts Week fell in 2010 is not stated; occurrences left empty. Needs a dated source or a second occurrence.
Recurring is unknown: one undated occurrence only. Summer Camp is a season with weekly themes, so the theme may recur in other seasons; no source says so.

Pack naming: 'Arts and Crafts Week' is one weekly theme inside the 'Summer Camp' season, not the whole event. The pack may be merging the season and a theme week under one name. Summer Camp (season) is listed here as context only, not as an alias.

Items: the boombox items (Boombox, Chiller Boombox, Totem Boombox etc.) and the wiki boombox category are NOT tied to Arts and Crafts Week by any source. Article 1624 names boomboxes only as an activity. Left out of items. Merri's Marinated Mystery Meat is tied only as an example cited in the article, price unknown.
Wiki category members are empty and quest answers mentioning the event are empty. No NPCs, zones, or quests found for this event.

Live status: article 1624 is written as a past live event, but it also describes an 'expected in-game event schedule'. Marked live 'yes' with moderate confidence; the article date is unknown, so this is not confirmed against a dated post.
Locale: no client string matches 'Arts and Crafts'. Boombox locale ids (6489, 92312, 151365, 5101167) exist but are not tied to this event; the client does not confirm any item for it.

Speed record holder, race timing rules and whether the course is still in the live game are not in any source.

evidence.claim: Crafting Week is one weekly theme inside the Summer Camp community event season, not a separate event. Article 1624 says 'Summer Camp is a community event season in which each week celebrates a different theme; this week's theme was Arts and Crafts Week.'
Article 1628 says Summer Camp was a multi-week community event and the week covered was Crafting Week (Semana de Artesanias).
Summer Camp ran in summer 2010 with themed events for 13 weeks beginning the week of the announcement.
Free Realms released its virtual Summer Camp on June 7, 2010.
Summer Camp added 14 new camp-land quests along with daily questlines and events.
During Arts and Crafts Week, Blacksmiths and Cooks create new items from raw materials (metal mined or food harvested), players dance to boombox music and build block sculptures at their houses.
Crafting Week activities included blacksmiths and cooks making items from pure materials from mining and food harvesting, plus radio-cassette music, dancing and block sculptures at home.
Merri's Marinated Mystery Meat is the cooking item used as the example dish for Arts and Crafts Week.
A printable Summer Camp Activity Calendar was released each week, with a new one each week.
Chatty created the summer camp deep inside Greenwood Forest, reached through a newly activated Warpstone.
Jojo is the chugawug at Summer Camp whose quests Jojo's Mojo and Jojo's Dojo are client-named with Summer Camp.

Client quest titles naming Summer Camp: Jojo's Mojo (locale:441714), Jojo's Dojo (locale:441718), Chatty's Summer Camp Party (locale:7037), Robbie's Summer Camp Party (locale:7039). The place name Summer Camp is locale:442124.
Article 1780 calls the Pet Parade the last Summer Camp event.

open: The pack title 'Crafting Week' is a week theme inside the Summer Camp season, not the event name. The pack merges a sub-theme with the event, so the event should be recorded as Summer Camp (2010) with Arts and Crafts / Crafting Week as one week.

Exact dates of the Crafting Week (Arts and Crafts Week) itself are not in the pack or the lookup. Article 1627 is dated only by a relative 'Posted 10 months, 3 weeks ago' stamp and 1624 and 1628 are undated. The week can be placed only within the 13-week 2010 season, so the month and days are unknown.
Year 2010 rests on Ten Ton Hammer node 85170 and node 86237, which describe the summer 2010 Summer Camp season. The articles themselves give no year.

Article 1628 gives an expected in-game schedule (Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, Pacific Time). That reads as a pre-launch or plan wording, so the weekday schedule is not confirmed as live. Article 1624 says 'this week's theme was' and reads as live, so live is set to yes for the season.
No prices, currencies or reward lists for Crafting Week items are in any source. Merri's Marinated Mystery Meat has price null and currency null.

Only locale quest titles tie to Summer Camp. None is confirmed to belong to the Crafting Week week itself. The quest answers pack is empty. Robbie is named only in a quest title, so he is not confirmed as an NPC. No rewards are sourced.
The Pet Parade and other Summer Camp themed weeks are separate weeks of the same season and are not part of this pack's Crafting Week.
Wiki category members and quest answers for this event are empty, so the item list is limited to what articles 1624 and 1627 name.

open: Pack merge: the input pack is titled 'Trading Card Game events' and merges several things. Only the Snow Days JCC tournaments have a dated source here. Not included: (a) the daily JCC community events (article 718 summary mentions 15:00 Pacific, but no date tie to this object); (b) the weekly PvP community event (article 641, undated); (c) the standing TCG minigame (articles 640, 69, unchecked); (d) the Halloween TCG promo (articles 1861, 1857, 1860, conflicting rewards, undated); (e) the Rumbledome! card set (article 2877, a set launch); (f) Card Duelist: Snowhill is Melting (locale 436538), no tie to a TCG event run.

The pack's only fact (article 1593, Spanish Summer Camp / Fashion Week post) is undated, is a preview ('se espera' = expected), and belongs to Summer Camp, not Snow Days. It is excluded. Its 'daily JCC events' wording cannot be tied to this object.
Article 705 (English Snow Days post) is dropped: it was not re-read and the lookup index did not return it. Article 770 and 771 (all-day wording) are undated and are not cited.

Recurrence: the Snow Days name recurs in other sources (articles 892, 828, 1953, 2428; 2428 places Snow Days 2011 live during a community webcast). I did not re-read these in this pass, and they are not tied to the JCC tournaments, so recurring stays null. The JCC tournament part is sourced only for 2009.

Items and rewards: none claimed. The wiki category 'Trading Card Game' mixes unrelated items (Baron von Darkcheat, Abominable Snowman, Banana Suit, Golden Santa Suit, etc.), so it does not tie any item to this event. TCG-looking members (Drake, Hip Hop Boombox, Gloam Clone, Chiller Boombox, Chrome Drake, Card Shark Trilby, Card Champion's Case) are unverified.
NPCs: Sam Potts (Card Duelist trainer) excluded; her location conflicts across articles 381 and 2734 and wiki, unresolved.

evidence.claim: Pet Week was the final weekly theme of the 2010 Summer Camp season, featuring pet showing and mount riding.

Pet Parade started in Crossroads, marched to the area near the Sanctuary warpstone, was held on Server 1 on September 2 and 3, 2010 (US/LatAm and UK/Europe times), and the event was the last Summer Camp event. Confirmed by a second lookup of the article summary; the exact session times and the 'biggest yet' quote were not confirmed and are omitted.
Summer Camp was a 13-week virtual themed event beginning with its June 2010 announcement.
Summer Camp was released on June 7, 2010.
The client has a Community Event named 'Pet Parade' (locale 31293). Name-only tie; it does not place Pet Week.

open: Pet Week's own dates are not stated in any source. articleId 1775 is a pre-launch preview ('We are going to end the season with this week's theme'), so the Pet Week theme itself is not confirmed as live; the Sept 2-3 2010 parade dates are the only dated, sourced occurrences. Recheck the publication date of 1775 and 1780 (both show no absolute date in the pack).

Pet Week and Pet Parade are merged in the pack's name. Pet Week (theme, articleId 1775) is treated as the parent; the Pet Parade (articleId 1780) is its child activity. Do not treat the parade as covering other parades.

Other parades share the name 'Pet Parade' and are separate events: articleId 516 (costume parade to Blackspore, Oct 23 2009), articleId 877 (Dress Up Your Pet Day, Wugachug to Sanctuary) and articleId 889 (costume parade after home showcase, Wugachug to Sanctuary). Locale 31294 gives Blackspore as location, conflicting with the 2010 route; not used.
Session times (3pm Pacific Thursday; 9am Pacific / 4pm GMT Friday) were not confirmed in the lookup; omitted.
The 'biggest yet' quote from articleId 1780 was not confirmed; only the 'last Summer Camp event' fact is supported.
Summer Camp season end is not stated in any source; the 13-week run is an inference and must not set an end date.

No items, NPCs or quests are tied to Pet Week. Pet Pals pets (e.g. Marshmallow) and Summer Camp Jojo quests are season-level and not tied to Pet Week. The expected in-game and TCG event schedule for Pet Week (articleId 1775) is not in the pack.

Pet Week is the parent weekly theme of article 1775, not an alias of this event. It is removed from aliases. The schema has no parent-theme field, so it is recorded here: parent theme = Pet Week, the final weekly theme of the 2010 Summer Camp season.

Alias 'Community Event: Pet Parade' (locale 31293) is dropped as ambiguous. Locale 31294 uses the same name for a Blackspore parade (SERVER 1). Only 'Pet Parade' is kept, and it is also generic, so the Sanctuary route should be matched by article 1780 rather than by name.

No items, NPCs, quests, prices or rewards are tied to this event: the wiki category is empty, quest answers are empty, and the video frames show Sanctuary without a parade link.
recurring is null: only one occurrence of this route is found, and no article says it recurs.

The 2010 first run is dated Thursday 7 October 2010 at 3pm Pacific Time (U.S. and Latin America) on Server 1. In UTC that is 22:00 (October 2010 Pacific time was UTC-7).

A second run is dated Friday 8 October 2010 at 9:00am Pacific Time, stated in the article as 4:00pm GMT for UK and Europe, on Server 1. 9:00 PDT equals 16:00 UTC, so the GMT figure is consistent with the Pacific time. Article 1849's '16:00 European Time' wording is ambiguous and is not used as a UTC value.

The ghost pet for the party came from the Blackspore Pet Adoption Center.
The Blackspore Pet Adoption Center is run by Vusala and its pets are all ghosts. This is a general place article, not a party source.

The client names the event 'Ghostly Pet Party' (locale:14561) and its objective reads 'Bring your ghost pet and your favorite Halloween costume to this Blackspore bash!' (locale:14565, a quest_objective string).
The wiki Community Events page lists the Ghostly Pet Party as an event in Blackspore Swamp during Super Spooktacular, and says it is very similar to the Pet Party but themed around ghost pets.

Super Spooktacular is the parent Halloween holiday: 2009 (scheduled Oct 14 to Nov 11, 2009), 2010 (second year, October 2010 billed as Super Spooktacular month), 2013 (fourth annual, Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2013).

Article 1845 says October 2010 was Super Spooktacular month, with spooky community events planned every Thursday afternoon and Friday morning. This is month-level context only; it does not name the party as recurring.
The Super Spooktacular wiki category lists the parent holiday and its seasonal items. No item in that category is tied to the Ghostly Pet Party by any source, so items is empty.

open: Name and aliases: display name is the pack's Spanish title 'Ghost Pet Party (Fiesta para Mascotas Fantasma)'. Aliases: 'Ghostly Pet Party' (locale:14561, wiki Community Events, article 1845), 'Ghost Pet Party' (English-language fact text in articles 1849 and 1850), and 'Fiesta para Mascotas Fantasma' (Spanish article titles). Do not add 'Sporeshade' as an alias without a source that says so.

Do not merge: the wiki Community Events page calls the plain Pet Party a separate, similar event. Only the Ghostly/Ghost Pet Party, Blackspore Swamp, Super Spooktacular 2010 is in scope. Locale 4549 'Pet Party Favor' belongs to the plain Pet Party and is not used here.

Live status is 'unsure'. Article 1845 is a week-of notice and its fact text says 'ran on', but the sentence source is not clearly past tense. Articles 1849 and 1850 are forward-looking announcements. No source confirms the runs happened. Set live to 'yes' only if a post-event article is found.

Recurrence is unproven. Only the 2010 runs are sourced. The Thursday/Friday rhythm in article 1845 is month-level context for community events generally. Recurring stays null until a second year's article names this party.

Location conflict: article 1850 (English text) and the wiki-derived pack say Sporeshade swamp. Article 1845 and the wiki say Blackspore Swamp. Article 1850's Spanish quote says 'Pantano de Esporaumbria'. Blackspore is the canonical name here. Sporeshade is likely a translation of the same place but no source states it.

Quests: empty. Locale 14565 is a quest_objective string tagged with the party name, but its quest title is not in the pack and no quest title in the client matches it (locale 14563 'Trick or Treat in Sanctuary' is a different event). Record it as a known objective with unknown quest title. Do not create a quest record until a quest id is found.
NPCs: none are tied to the party by any source. The Super Spooktacular wiki NPC names are left out.

Rewards and prices: no source gives any reward or price for the party. Items, rewards and price fields are unknown. The wiki pages with Super Spooktacular seasonal items are not tied to this party by any source.

Activities: the sourced ones are bringing a ghost pet and wearing a costume (article 1845). Locale 6619 ('dance away the afternoon in the graveyard of Blackspore') is not tied to the party by any source and is left out.
Article dates are null in the pack. The 2010 year and the day/month come from the article text, not from a posting date.
Server 1 is the only server named for the party, from articles 1845, 1849 and 1850. No source says it ran on other servers.

Time zones: 2010 October Pacific time was UTC-7 (PDT), so 3pm PDT = 22:00 UTC and 9am PDT = 16:00 UTC. Article 1845's '4:00pm GMT' matches 9am PDT. Article 1849's '16:00 European Time' is ambiguous (UK was on BST in October 2010), so it is not used as a UTC value.

thumb|350px

The Super Spooktacular is an annual event during the month of October in celebration of Halloween. The event features many objectives such as: stopping the Pumpkin Prince, Trick-or-Treat, ghost hunting, etc.

Questline
Starting in Sanctuary
Since Halloween Harry is used in so many of these quests, he now has his own quick-click transport icon on the game Atlas during the event!

wiki_page.title: Super Spooktacular
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px

The Super Spooktacular is an annual event during the month of October in celebration of Halloween. The event features many objectives such as: stopping the Pumpkin Prince, Trick-or-Treat, ghost hunting, etc.

Questline
Starting in Sanctuary
Since Halloween Harry is used in so many of these quests, he now has his own quick-click transport icon on the game Atlas during the event!

 Trick-or-Treat from Halloween Harry in Pixiewood Hills (repeatable once per day)
 Bag Snatchers from Halloween Harry
 Candy Gram from Halloween Harry
 A Formal Report from Halloween Harry
 A Trip to the Swamp from Greyli Dustywings in Queensfields
 Spectral Spectacles from Greyli Dustywings 
 A Ghostly Discovery from Lucinda in Blackspore Swamp 
 Guardians of the Tomb from Lord William IV in Blackspore Swamp 
 Sealed with a Signet from Lord William IV 
 The Pumpkin Prince from Lucinda 

 Spooky Hide 'n Seek from Tabitha in Pixiewood Hills (must complete the above series first, repeatable once per day)
 Ghostly Games from Hector in Pixiewood Hills (must complete the above series first, repeatable once per day)
 Halloween Fanatic from Halloween Harry (must complete the Trick-or-Treat quest three times first)
 The Great Scare from Ghost Hunter in Pixiewood Hills

Zelda location conflict: articles 1857, 1862 and 1878 put Madam Zelda in Blackspore; summaries of 1866 and 1867 place her in Esporaumbria/Shadowbrook (Shadowmoor). No source supports Shadowmoor as a dance-off zone, so it is omitted. Zelda may have moved between seasons, or the articles may come from different years.

evidence.claim: Seaside beach party announced for Friday August 14, 2009, 1pm-3pm PDT, Server 1, hosted by Community Ambassadors.

Article event fact: a community beach party in Seaside 'was held on Friday March 5, 2010' at 3pm Pacific (US/LatAm) and 9:00am Pacific / 5:00pm UTC (UK/Europe), Server 1. The article summary is an announcement with dancing, crabs, fireworks, collection trading and trivia.
Article event fact: 'A community Luau Beach Party took place in Seaside' with dancing, crab transformations, fireworks and collection trading. Summary dates it to late March 2011 on Server 1.
Client text 'Beach Party Luau' and a party on the beach below the Abandoned Dojo in Seaside, wear beach gear and hula outfits, play in the water.
Article 1136 summary describes a Seaside Beach Luau where pets could swim, with beach fashions and Hula Outfits available. It is undated in the pack.

open: Name merge is unproven. 'Seaside Beach Party' (2009, 2010), 'Luau Beach Party' (2011, article 2062) and 'Beach Party Luau' (locale:5525) are treated as one event on content similarity alone. A separate event is possible.
Held status: 2009 is announcement-only (article 194). 2010 has a held-tense event fact (article 1092) but an announcement summary, with no second source. 2011 has a 'took place' fact (article 2062).
2011 has no exact day or time in the retrievable text. Do not schedule it as a timed event.

Article 1136 (Seaside Beach Luau with pet swimming and Hula Outfits) is undated. It may be an additional occurrence, but it cannot be placed in time. Its pet-swim activity is not attributed to this event.

Tiger the Party Animal, the quest 'A Luau' (locale:422865, wiki Quest:A Luau) and the Party favor (locale:422866) are general luau-party content. No source ties them to Seaside, so they are excluded here.
Luau Party Ticket (wiki; locale:5102399) starts a party in the buyer's current zone, so it is not Seaside-specific and is excluded.
Beach outfit and Hula Outfit prices are not stated in any source.
Playa Azul luau articles (2064, 2065) use similar session times under another location name. Unresolved; they may be the same event or a separate one.
'Back to School Beach Party' (locales 436158, 436159), 'Party for Pets' and 'Winter Party' are separate events and are not merged.
Pixiewood Hills is where outfits can be obtained, not an event zone.

evidence.claim: Event is the Vampires vs. Werewolves Dance-off, a contest inside the Super Spooktacular holiday. Players pick a side via Madam Zelda, then wear team costumes and join the dance-off when the in-game kick-off fires.
The side with the most fans wins the competition and can get a piece of special cake from the Pumpkin Prince.

Super Spooktacular ran October 13 to November 23, 2011. The Vampires and Werewolves compete in a Dance Off for the Pumpkin Prince near Bone Bog Cemetery, and Boy and Girl Team Werewolf and Team Vampire outfits were sold in the Marketplace.

2013 live occurrence: Game Update 115 (dated 10/15/2013, Spooktacular section) says the Grey Werewolf Outfit now qualifies as a Werewolf outfit for the dance-off. Game Update 116 (Weekly Update 10/22/13) repeats it. The Super Spooktacular wiki page lists Grey Werewolf Outfit introduced in the Station Cash Marketplace in Week #2 (10/8/13) and Week #3 (10/15/13).
evidence.source: wiki: Template:News; wiki: User blog:Soe amnerys/Weekly Update - 10/22/13; wiki: Super Spooktacular

evidence.claim: The 2012 occurrence rests on one guild wiki page (Eternal Purebloods) with no month or day. It is weak.
Reward split by winner: a Vampire Cake Slice if Vampires win, a Werewolf Cake Slice if Werewolves win.
evidence.source: wiki: Super Spooktacular; locale:6628 (item - Vampire Cake Slice); locale:7336 (item - Werewolf Cake Slice)

evidence.claim: Dance-off kick-off announcement in Blackspore: the Vampires vs Werewolves Dance-off is about to kick off in Blackspore.
Pre-launch phase: Madam Zelda side-pick and buy-in lines. Join Team Vampire (costume required), join Team Werewolf, and wait for the dance-off to be announced.

Pre-launch phase: sabotage quests. Help the vampires sabotage the werewolves' dance practice (Pre-Emptive Bite). Ed Sullenfangs' version of the same objective is a near-identical duplicate, flagged in the client.

Dance practice battle quests. Werewolf Dance Practice: title locale 432022 (quest_title 'Pixie Woods Werewolf Dance Practice'), objective locale 432023 (defeat Jake Blackforest). Vampire Dance Practice: title locale 432024 (quest_title 'Pixie Woods Vampire Dance Practice'), objective locale 432025 (defeat Ed Sullenfangs).
Quest Another One Bites the Muck: join the vampires in the dance-off. A vampire outfit is required for moves to count.

Judging: the Pumpkin Prince offered a special prize to the scariest monster and the team with the scariest dance wins. Article 1867 says he judges the contest himself, while article 1862 says the side with the most fans wins. Both are reported.
Dance-off reward items from the wiki dance-off page: Team Vampire items (Bat, Team Vampire T-Shirt, Vampire Outfit, Vampire Fangs) and the battle reward cake slices.
evidence.source: wiki: Vampires vs. Werewolves Dance-off; wiki: Vampire Dance Practice; wiki: Werewolf Dance Practice

evidence.claim: Dance-off is located just outside the gates of Bone Bog Cemetery in Blackspore and is hosted by the Pumpkin Prince. The dance practice battles start by clicking a vampire or werewolf in the Sinking Graveyard in Blackspore Swamp and are spawned only during Super Spooktacular.
evidence.source: wiki: Blackspore Swamp; wiki: Vampire Dance Practice; wiki: Werewolf Dance Practice

evidence.claim: Neighbouring internal dance-off labels (xmas 01-04, totem 01, chicken 01-05, slide 01-03; locales 432335-432365) are FLAG dev_note internal labels, not this event. Locales 432336, 432338 and 432340 do not exist.
evidence.source: locale:432335; locale:432337; locale:432339; locale:432355; ids check

open: Pack title 'Dance-off reward' names the reward, not the event. The pack merges the Vampires vs. Werewolves Dance-off with the Super Spooktacular holiday. Holiday store items (Fog Machine, Super Spooktacular Parachute, Eyeball mount, Flaming Skull Wobblehead, Super Spooktacular 2009 Member Pack) are not tied to the dance-off and are excluded.
Pumpkin Prince's Treasure (locale 432069), Pumpkin Prince Card (9919) and Pumpkin Prince Bundle (9921) are not tied to the dance-off in any source and are excluded.

Internal dance-off labels xmas 01-04, totem 01, chicken 01-05 and slide 01-03 (locales 432335-432365, FLAG dev_note) are a separate internal system. They are not aliases of Vampires vs Werewolves. Review the alias in the events calendar.
Vampires vs. Werewolves Costume Party (locale 14568) is a dialog label, not a confirmed quest title, so it is not listed under quests. It may be an alias. Not confirmed.
Madam Zelda's side-pick quest title is not in the pack. Only objective text (locales 432288, 432293) is present, so it is not listed.

2010 is not confirmed for the dance-off. Article 1862 has no date in the pack and article 1854 is undated. Article 1845 dates October 2010 Super Spooktacular and 1860 calls it the second year, but nothing ties the dance-off to 2010.

2012 occurrence is weak (guild wiki only). The 2011 article 2304 and the 2013 wiki news (Game Update 115, 10/15/2013; Game Update 116, 10/22/13) are the dated occurrences. The yearly recurrence of the dance-off itself is inferred from the Spooktacular being yearly, not stated by any article.
Live is 'yes' with moderate confidence. The 2011 and 2013 dated sources show the event and dance-off running. No post-run article confirms the 2011 or 2013 result. Video frames carry no dates.

Phase split. Pre-launch covers Madam Zelda side-pick, costume buy-in, and sabotage/dance-practice quests (Pre-Emptive Bite; the Pixie Woods dance practice quests). Live covers the in-game kick-off announcement (locale 5197) and the judged dance-off. The kick-off has no clock time in any source, so the live start is open. A wiki line says there is a world-wide announcement every 15 minutes, but it is not tied to the dance-off start. Not used.

Location conflict. Wiki places the dance-off at Bone Bog Cemetery, client text (5197) and video place the kick-off in Blackspore, and wiki dance practice battles are in the Sinking Graveyard of Blackspore Swamp. Pixie Woods appears only in quest_title prefixes (locales 432022, 432024). It is not confirmed as a location and is excluded from zones.

Team Werewolf item list is truncated in the wiki snippet. Only Team Vampire items are listed. No prices or currencies for any dance-off item appear in the pack, so price is null. Grey Werewolf Outfit is listed as station_cash only because the wiki places it in the Station Cash Marketplace; the price value itself is not in the pack.
Pre-Emptive Bite is named from the video quest text and locale objective label. Its exact title is not confirmed in a quest_title row.

wireable is false. The dance-off has no fixed start time and the recurrence is inferred. The calendar could hold the 2011-10-13 to 2011-11-23 Spooktacular window and the 2013 dated sources as a historical record, but could not schedule the dance-off itself until a dated start or announcement schedule is sourced.

Article 1867 is Spanish. Its statements are translated, not quoted verbatim. Article 1867 says the Pumpkin Prince judges the contest himself, while 1862 says the side with the most fans wins. Both are reported.

aliases: Harry Halloween (pack name, reversed token order of Halloween Harry)

event_answer.recurring: yearly in October to November. quests: Return to Halloween Harry in Sanctuary
activities: Trick-or-Treat: players collect treats with the /scare command, and Harry starts the activity (article 1860 summary; article 1854). Players return each day.
Daily Halloween quests offered from a list of NPCs including Ruby, Vladamir and Halloween Harry (article 1857).
Pumpkin Prince fights (article 1857 summary names the Pumpkin Prince; article 1854).

Ghost Pet Party: a community event run under the festival name, not Harry's trick-or-treat. Runs on Server 1 on Thursday 7 October 2010 at 15:00 Pacific and Friday 8 October 2010 at 09:00 Pacific (articles 1849, 1850). Linked here as an in-festival sub-event, kept out of the occurrences above. The wiki Community Events page says it took place during Super Spooktacular; that wiki line was not re-read in this pass.

evidence.claim: Event is the Super Spooktacular Halloween festival. Halloween Harry (client name, locale:415047; wiki page Halloween Harry) runs its trick-or-treat activity and sends players on Halloween quests. The pack's 'Harry Halloween' is the same NPC with the name tokens reversed.

Edition count: article 1861 says 'second annual' and 1860 says 'second year'. Article 1870 calls a Sanctuary party the 'second anniversary of the Super Spooktacular edition'. The 2009 first run is consistent with the client item 'Super Spooktacular 2009 Member Pack' (locale:156839, name only, used as precedent and not as an item of this event). Article 2304 gives the 2011 window.
2011 live window: October 13, 2011 to November 23, 2011.
Pre-launch: the October 6, 2011 webcast discussed the Spooktacular event (a plan before the live run, not a live event).
Trick-or-Treat mechanic: players collect treats with /scare in Pixiewood, and Harry starts it. Players can return each day.
Daily Halloween quests are offered from a list of NPCs including Ruby, Vladamir and Halloween Harry.

Harry's location: 2010 articles put him on the road to Pixiewood. Client and wiki data put him in Sanctuary during the event ('Return to Halloween Harry in Sanctuary', locale:415943; 'Speak to Halloween Harry' tagged Sanctuary, locale:416853; wiki page Halloween Harry).
evidence.source: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=1860; locale:415943; locale:416853; wiki page Halloween Harry

evidence.claim: Quest titles confirmed in the client: Bag Snatchers (locale:415303), Candy Gram (locale:415311), Delicious Goo'd Candy (locale:416791), Return to Halloween Harry in Sanctuary (locale:415943).

A Trip to the Swamp: the title is confirmed in the client (locale:415319), but the dialog and objective text (locale:415317, 415318, 415320) names General Glowlight, Ethan, Blackspore and Greyli Dustywings with no Halloween wording. The event tie is wiki-only (wiki page Super Spooktacular lists it from Greyli Dustywings in Queensfields). Kept in quests with the tie marked as wiki-only.
evidence.source: locale:415319; locale:415317; locale:415318; locale:415320; wiki page Super Spooktacular

evidence.claim: Guard Hardin speaks the Bag Snatchers dialog, 'We've had reports of bag snatchers here in Sanctuary' (locale:415689).
Fog Machine is tied to the event by the wiki (available during Super Spooktacular; store copy 'unique Spooktacular house item'). Price 8999 coins is from an undated store frame.
evidence.source: wiki page Super Spooktacular; wiki page Fog Machine; video:1TNyzyI62nc/00252; video:1TNyzyI62nc/00254

evidence.claim: Ghost Pet Party: Thursday 7 October 2010 at 15:00 Pacific, and Friday 8 October 2010 at 09:00 Pacific, on Server 1. Kept as a linked in-festival community event, separate from Harry's trick-or-treat occurrence.
How Rude! is not confirmed as a live quest title. The client hits are dev-flagged or QA strings (locale:415641, locale:415271), and the wiki lists it for Ruby in Pixiewood Hills.
evidence.source: wiki page Super Spooktacular; locale:415641 (FLAG); locale:415271 (FLAG)

evidence.claim: Super Spooktacular Parachute (899 station_cash) is tied by the wiki to the 2013 event (week 3, 10/15/13). It is not part of the 2010 or 2011 runs and is removed from this event's items.
evidence.source: wiki page Super Spooktacular; wiki page Super Spooktacular Parachute; video:1TNyzyI62nc/00122; locale:5102560

open: Name: the pack says 'Harry Halloween'. Client and wiki say 'Halloween Harry'. Article 1857 is French and calls it 'Super Fantomastique', which is an alias the pack misses. The articles tokenise the name as [Harry] [Halloween].

Pack may merge two events. The annual Super Spooktacular (Harry trick-or-treat) is kept separate from the Oct 2010 Ghost Pet Party community event (articles 1849, 1850). Ghost Pet Party is an in-festival sub-event, linked but not an occurrence.

2010 year is inferred from article 1860 (undated, with only a 2011-06-04 capture note) and from the 'second annual' wording of 1861 and 1857. 2009 is the first run, inferred from locale:156839, and is not an occurrence because no article gives its dates.
Pre-launch row: the October 6, 2011 webcast (article 2300) is a plan, not a live run, and is kept separate from the Oct 13 to Nov 23, 2011 window (article 2304).

Undated store items held out of the scheduled item list until a year is confirmed. Eyeball mount (134 station_cash, video:1TNyzyI62nc/00152, 'creepy Spooktacular eyeball mount') and Flaming Skull Wobblehead (89 station_cash, video:1TNyzyI62nc/00132, 'your spooktacular noggin') are Spooktacular-named store listings with no date. They are candidates, not confirmed event items.

Ghost Hunter, Greyli Dustywings and Madam Zelda are not confirmed as NPCs for this event in the client. Madam Zelda comes from article 1861, which is truncated. Greyli and Ghost Hunter ties are wiki-only. Queensfields and Blackspore appear only through the A Trip to the Swamp wiki tie and client dialog, so they are not listed as zones.

Ghost Pet Party's wiki 'took place during Super Spooktacular' line is from the earlier pass and was not re-read here. Extra Ghost Pet Party dates Oct 14, 15 and 21 are unconfirmed. Only Oct 7 and Oct 8 2010 were read.

'Trick-or-Treat' is listed as an activity, not a quest. A Formal Report and Halloween Fanatic appear on the wiki but have no client id, so they are not in quests. Goo'd Candy minigame details (Candy Bag, Ectoplasmic Goo) were not re-checked in this pass and are left out of activities.
Article 2304 (2011 window) was checked via lookup for its date quote, but its full text was not re-read in this pass. The 2011 year and window rest on the quoted date in the lookup excerpt.
Spanish and French articles are only partly read. The Spooktacular Parachute is excluded (2013), and its store price is not used.

The Super Spooktacular is an annual event during the month of October in celebration of Halloween. The event features many objectives such as: stopping the Pumpkin Prince, Trick-or-Treat, ghost hunting, etc.

evidence.claim: The SOE Super Fan Holidays sale started at 18h CET on 29 November 2010 (equal to 09:00 Pacific on 29 Nov).

The end instant conflicts across sources. Article 1938 says 18h CET on 3 December 2010 (equal to 09:00 Pacific on 3 Dec). Articles 1939 and 1940 say 18:00 Pacific Time on 3 December 2010. Article 1933 (summary) says 6pm PST on 3 December 2010. The 18:00 Pacific end is 03:00 CET on 4 December. This is an open conflict, not one window.
Free Realms members got an extra discount on Station Cash items during the sale: all Station Cash items 30% off for members, described as a triple discount.
Dragon mounts were reduced by 30% for members during the Super Fan Holidays sale.
The Super Fan Days promotion ran Wednesday 3 Nov to Tuesday 9 Nov 2010, with 50% off Station Cash purchases of 2000 or more. It is a separate event and is excluded from this record.
Client locale 432670 reads 'Super Fan Discount!'. It names a Super Fan discount but not Holidays, so it is not tied to this event.

open: Wireable is false until the end instant is settled. End conflict: 18h CET 3 Dec 2010 (article 1938, = 09:00 PST 3 Dec) vs 18:00 PST/Pacific 3 Dec 2010 (articles 1939, 1940, 1933). Start instant is consistent across all four.
Station Cash pack discounts of 25% off 5,000 and 35% off 10,000 were removed. The lookup did not find them in articles 1938 or 1939, so they are unverified.
Base Station Cash prices are not stated, so the Dragon mount price is null. Only the 30% member discount is sourced.
Article 1938 has no absolute posting date (date null). The year 2010 comes from the quoted sale dates. Article 1933 is marked late-November 2010 by its summary, not a stated post date.
Pack merges names: 'Super Fan' is a family brand. 'Super Fan Days' (3-9 Nov 2010) and 'Super Fan Summer Sizzle' (last day 18 Aug 2011, article 2218) are separate events and are excluded.
Aliases seen: 'Les Super Fan Holidays' (pack title, French form), 'Super Fan Holidays sale', 'SOE Super Fan Holidays'. An alias check on the FTS lookup did not find more.
Only one occurrence (2010). Recurrence is unknown and no article says it recurs, so recurring is null.
No zones, NPCs, quests or wiki category members are tied to this event in the pack or lookup. Those fields are empty.
Live is 'yes' for the 2010 run only, based on articles that describe a completed sale window. No pre-launch preview is in the pack.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

Wireable: no. Hold as a sub-activity of the Super Spooktacular holiday entry until that entry is built and its dates are sourced.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

Max players and AI disabled from the earlier answer are dropped: no lookup result confirms them.

Client quests 'Kart Racer: Thunder Falls Sprint Challenge' (locale 3533) and 'Endurance Challenge' (3542) are not tied to this event. Wiki pages 'Chase Wheeler' and 'Kart Driver' mention Thunder Falls kart quests, but no source ties them to it. Client NPC dialog 'Do you wanna go fast? Head to Thunder Falls and drive against the best!' (locale 31494) and 'Thunder Falls Speedway' NPC dialog (locale 116815) name the track, not this event.
Client names 'Thunder Falls Speedway' (locale 3606) and 'Kart Racing at Thunder Falls!' (locale 3244) name the track, not this event.
Video frame kNZtSg_Qrsw/00122.jpg shows a Thunder Falls Speedway kart minigame with a '1ST PLACE' result. It is not tied to this event by a source, so it is not evidence here.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

evidence.claim: Event is the SOE Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief fundraiser in Free Realms, where Cherry Blossom items were sold in the in-game marketplace and SOE donated $10 per item.
Initial sale window was Friday March 25 through Monday March 28 (2011); the article quote gives the days and the 2011 year is stated in the fact text for the same window.
The promotion was extended through April 1st.
A Cherry Blossom item was sold in the in-game catalog as part of the relief promotion, available until April 1.
Cherry Blossom Tree could be bought for 500 Station Cash as support for Japan earthquake relief.
Item name Cherry Blossom Tree, with the description and the $10 donation text, is in the client.
Client text: for every Cherry Blossom Tree purchased, SOE donates 10 dollars to the Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort.
Client description: a cherry blossom tree purchased to show support for the earthquake relief effort in Japan.
Cherry Blossom items could be displayed in player in-game homes, where applicable.

Article 2066 is a pre-launch announcement (players will be invited to purchase); the live run is supported by the later extension and sold-item articles 2072 and 2076, which the pack did not include and I found by lookup.

open: Year: the pack's own date for article 2066 is null. The 2011 year and March 25-28 window come from fact text in article 2068 and the article summaries (capture 2011-04-02); the March 25 2011 Friday and March 28 2011 Monday weekdays are consistent with that year.
Extension end: articles 2072 and 2076 say through April 1, 2011. No article confirms the sale actually ended on April 1, so the window end is announced, not verified.

Donation recipient: the article text names the American Red Cross, but client strings (locale:434305) say the Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort. The same donation is described both ways; this is a naming difference, not a second event.

Aliases: the pack names only the fundraiser. Aliases I found: 'Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort', 'Japan Earthquake & Tsunami Relief', 'Japan earthquake relief promotion' (articleId 2072), 'Cherry Blossom Tree promotion'. The pack did not merge any second event here.
Only the Cherry Blossom Tree is named in any source. Other 'Cherry Blossom items' sold in the catalog are unnamed (price and names not in the pack or the lookup), so they are not listed as items.

Client locale:434534 (moment of silence at 7:00 p.m. PDT on Server 1 for the Japan earthquake and tsunami) names the disaster but not this fundraiser, and no article ties that moment to the sale window. Not listed as an activity; needs an article to confirm.
Client locale:7788 'Bamboo and cherry blossom combat outfit' is not tied to this event by any source, so it is excluded.
Zones and NPCs: none named in any source. Player homes are where the items could be displayed (article 2066 and 2068), not a zone.
Quests: none. The evidence pack has no quest answers and the lookup found no quest linked to this event.
Live status: 'yes' rests on articles 2072 and 2076 describing a sale in the catalog. Article 2066 alone is a plan. Confidence 0.8 reflects that no post-window sales report was found.
Wiki category: empty in the pack, and the lookup found no wiki page for the event, so no wiki confirmation exists.

The Spring Chicken Pack was described as returning from the Spring Fever promotion. It was sold for 500 Station Cash (2000 SC value) in its own window, May 27-30, 2011 (7:00 AM PDT Friday to 11:59 PM PDT Monday). That window is a separate occurrence and is not a Spring Fever window.

Its May 27-30, 2011 sale window is recorded here as a separate occurrence, not a Spring Fever occurrence: source http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=2146. Year 2011 is stated in that article for the pack's window only. Spring Fever's own occurrence stays year null.

Year for the Spring Fever April 22-25 window is unresolved. Article 2103 suggests a post around May 2011, after the window it announces, which does not confirm April 2011. 2011 is a candidate only. The capture date in article 2105's summary (2011-06-04) suggests 2011 but is not stated in the article text.

wireable is false. The only timed fact is an SC double window with no confirmed year. No quests, NPCs or item windows are tied to this event. Set wireable only after the year is accepted and the Chicken Pack tie is settled.
The critique's pass is false and wireable is false, so no pass field is returned; the calendar lens fails on the merged activity, which is now fixed.
The Spring Chicken Pack tie to Spring Fever rests only on article 2146's 'returning from the Spring Fever promotion' wording. It is kept as an item note, not as a Spring Fever occurrence or activity.

Article 2146's contents list (Spring Chicken Costume, Spring Chicken Pet, Spring Chick Pet Pal, 20 chick and chicken house items) describes the pack, not confirmed Spring Fever rewards. Rewards is left empty. The article list may be truncated in the lookup text, so the full item list is not confirmed.

Article 2557 gives a separate spring double-SC window, April 6-8, 2012, described as 'A Spring special' and not naming Spring Fever. It is excluded from occurrences and kept as a separate candidate. The 2011 and 2012 spring windows do not establish a recurring pattern, so recurring is null.
Locale 432670 ('Super Fan Discount!', type other, no description) exists and is not flagged. It is uncited because its label alone does not tie to Spring Fever.
The event is an SOE-wide cross-promo, and Free Realms only participated. Whether it belongs in the Free Realms calendar is a design call.
Other spring-themed items named in article 2103 are not identified and are not in items.

Aliases are inferred from titles and may match other SOE spring promotions. The pack may merge the 2011 Spring Fever promotion with other SOE spring windows, and it does not show whether the Chicken Pack's May 2011 window is the same event.
