summary: This is a Portuguese-language SOE site-wide promotion post, not a Free Realms article. Free Realms appears only as one of several participating SOE games in a Station Cash double-purchase event held April 22-25; it gives no quests, items or mechanics. The year (http://www.freerealms.com/article/detail.action?articleId=2105)

evidence.claim: Super Fan Spring Fever was an SOE cross-game promotion. Free Realms was one of the participating games, alongside EverQuest, EverQuest II, Star Wars Galaxies and Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures.
The Station Cash double window ran April 22 to April 25, with Station Cash purchases doubled. SMS Station Cash purchases were excluded.
The same April 22-25 double Station Cash window is listed for Free Realms as a participating game in the SOE Super Fan Spring Fever promotion.

Article 2103 gives the window as April 22-25 with no year. It says the post was made about 1 month 1 week before a June 2011 capture, which places the posting around late April to early May 2011. That is a relative date and does not confirm the year of the window, so year is set to null.

Article 2146 is a separate occurrence. The Memorial Day and Spring Chicken pack promotion ran from 7:00 AM PDT Friday May 27 to 11:59 PM PDT Monday May 30, 2011, with the year stated. It is not part of the April 22-25 window and is not listed as an occurrence of this event.
Article 2146 says the Spring Chicken Pack was returning from the Spring Fever promotion. That wording gives no April date, so it is not used to link the 'Spring Fever' alias to the April window.
Article 2557 (April 6-8, 2012, two times SC) and article 2893 (March 29-31, Spring Celebration double SC) are other spring promotions. They are not occurrences of this event.
The client text for the Spring Chicken Pack names the pack and its contents but does not date it to April or tie it to the April window.
No item is tied to the April 22-25 window by any source, so the item list is empty. The Spring Chicken items belong to the May 2011 occurrence only.

open: Year of the April 22-25 window is not stated on any page. Article 2103's relative date (about 1 month 1 week before a June 2011 capture) only suggests 2011, so year is null. Wire only after a dated source confirms the year. wireable stays false.

Name issue: the pack title is the Spanish page title, and the English name in articles 2103 and 2105 is 'Super Fan Spring Fever'. The pack may merge two events under one name, the April 22-25 Station Cash double and the May 27-30 Memorial Day / Spring Chicken pack. Keep them as separate events.

'Spring Fever' is removed from aliases because it is ambiguous. Articles 2557 and 2893 use the same wording for other spring promotions, and article 2146 gives no April date. It can be mentioned only as an ambiguous term.

Spring Chicken Pack, Spring Chicken Costume (locale 435322), Spring Chicken pet (locale 435323), Spring Chicken Pet Pal (locale 435320) and the pack item (locale 435357) belong to the May 27-30, 2011 occurrence. They are not items of this event. Article 2146 is their only dated source, and it gives no April date.
Live status is 'no'. The April window is a past promotion and its year is unconfirmed. Recurring is null because only one April occurrence is confirmed.

No zones, NPCs, quests or activity-specific rewards are sourced. No wiki category members or quest answers mention this event. Article 2102 and 2105 are cross-game SOE promotion pages, not Free Realms updates, so they support participation and the discount terms only.
Locale 432670 'Super Fan Discount!' contains 'Super Fan' but no source ties it to this spring event, so it is not listed.

evidence.claim: Super Fan Spring Fever was an SOE cross-game promotion in which Station Cash purchases were doubled from April 22 to April 25, with SMS Station Cash purchases excluded.
The Portuguese post (titled as SOE Super Fan Spring Fever) also gives the April 22-25 double Station Cash window and lists Free Realms among the participating SOE games.

Free Realms was one of six SOE games named as included in the promotion, alongside EverQuest, EverQuest II, EverQuest II Extended, Star Wars Galaxies and Clone Wars Adventures. The article 2102 quote naming Free Realms in the participating list is Spanish text: 'Estaran participando EverQuest, EverQuest II, EverQuest II extendido, Free Realms'.
Super Fan Spring Fever gave selected games spring-themed special items or items on sale; Free Realms was one of the selected games. No Free Realms item is named in this article.
Article 2103 gives no year. It says the post was made about 1 month 1 week before its June 2011 capture date, so the year is not stated in any source.

The Spring Chicken Pack was described as returning from the Spring Fever promotion. Its contents were a Spring Chicken Costume, Spring Chicken Pet, Spring Chick Pet Pal, and 20 each of chicks and chickens.

The 500 Station Cash price of the Spring Chicken Pack belongs to a separate Memorial Day and Spring Chicken pack promotion, which ran from 7:00 AM PDT Friday May 27 to 11:59 PM PDT Monday May 30, 2011. It is not part of the April 22-25 Spring Fever window, so the Spring Fever item price is left null.

open: Year not stated. No article in the pack states a year for Super Fan Spring Fever. Article 2103's posting time relative to its June 2011 capture suggests 2011, but that is an inference, not a stated date. occurrences is therefore empty, and the calendar cannot schedule it until a year is confirmed.

Critique fix applied to evidence[1]: the claim that article 2101 gives the April 22-25 window and participating-games list is dropped. Lookup did not return any 2101 article fact (locale:2101 is a quest objective, not an article). The window and Spanish participation list are now cited to 2102.

Critique fix applied to evidence[5] and the item price: the 500 SC price is attributed to the Memorial Day sale (May 27-30, 2011) in article 2146, not to Spring Fever. The item price is null and currency is null.
Wireable is false. The event has a month-day window and no year, and the only dated item sale belongs to a different promotion.

Possible confusion, not included: articles 2118 and 2119 describe a one-day double Station Cash on Saturday April 30 across the SOE lineup, a separate event. Article 2557 describes a spring double-SC window on April 6-8, 2012 with the year stated in its text. Treat both as separate unless a source ties them.
Pack name 'Super Fan' is an SOE umbrella. Other Super Fan events (Super Fan Days Nov 3-9 2010, Summer Sizzle Aug 2011) are separate and are not included.
Live status is unsure, not no. The event is past, but it has no dated occurrence, so the pack cannot say whether it is due to run again.

No zones, NPCs or quests are tied to this promotion by any source. The pack's quest_answers list is empty. The client text at locale:435358 names the pack's contents but not Spring Fever, so it is not cited.

The Spring Chicken Pack item is tied to the event only by the 'returning from the Spring Fever promotion' wording in article 2146. Its contents are listed as evidence, not as rewards, because the article does not say they were rewards of the Spring Fever promotion.
The pack's fact quote is truncated Spanish text, so it was not used as a date source. Article 2102 was used for the window instead.

Cherry Blossom items could be placed or displayed in player in-game homes.

Client text: for every Cherry Blossom Tree purchased, SOE will donate 10 dollars to the Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort.

Its date is unknown and no source ties it to a day inside the March 25 to April 1, 2011 sale window, so it is not merged into the sale. Recurrence is unknown; no second occurrence is shown.

Only one sale occurrence (2011). Base sale dates are from article 2068 and 2070. Extension end date April 1 is from article 2072 and 2076, but the extension post date is approximate (about 2011-03-29, not shown in source). No second run is shown, so recurring is null.

The 2011 second-birthday party post is dated April 21, 2011 and lists eight areas: Merry Vale, Seaside, Snowhill, Shrouded Glade, Wugachug, Blackspore, Briarwood, Sanctuary.
The 2012 Bash ran through May 24, 2012 as the third anniversary celebration.

The 4th-anniversary post is dated April 29, 2013 and invites players to the Birthday Bash area in Sanctuary for dancing with the Ambassadors.

Cakenstein is defeated with fireworks.

open: The evidence pack is mislabeled: its title and alias 'Service interruption' name the outage (cause) rather than the event. Year 2011 is not in the article 2112 quote itself; it comes from the pack's summary of 2119 ('roughly late April 2011'), the TTH 97967 coverage and the April 21, 2011 intrusion date (TTH 97837). Article 2119 has date null. Confirm the year from the article page.

Cause conflict: TTH 97967 calls the interruption a PlayStation Network security breach; TTH 97837 says an external intrusion on SOE's system on April 21, 2011. These may be the same incident, but the sources do not say so directly.

Eligible transaction detail is truncated in the 2112 summary ('Game cards of eligible types can be redeemed for...'). The exact qualifying purchases and the multiplier scope are unverified; the 'double Station Cash' wording is from the 2112 quote and the summaries.
Live status is inferred: article 2112 says the promotion was 'held' and TTH 97967 says SOE 'offered' it. No post-event confirmation was found, so live is 'yes' at moderate confidence.
No items, NPCs, quests or zones are tied to this event in the client or wiki. Station Cash is the currency and reward, not an item, so items is empty.
Article 2125 (multi-game special events to thank players for patience) may be a related follow-up, but it is not Free Realms-specific and is not included as an occurrence.
The PS3 repair plan in 2119 is not part of this event. It is excluded.
Other 'Double Station Cash' hits (CVS 2012, Best Buy 2013, Festival of Hearts, Spring Celebration, Europe card promo) are separate events and are not included.

evidence.claim: SOE ran a one-day Double Station Cash promotion on Saturday, April 30, as a thank-you for player patience after a recent service interruption. The promotion covered SOE's game lineup, not Free Realms alone, so it is a portfolio-wide event with Free Realms as a participant.

The Double Station Cash day ran from 4 AM Saturday April 30 to 3:59 AM Sunday May 1, Brasilia time (8 AM to 7:59 AM Portugal time), across SOE's portfolio of games, as a thank-you for players' patience and an apology after a service interruption.

Article 2112 announced 'we will be hosting a Double Station Cash day on Saturday, April 30th' as a thank-you for players' patience during a recent service interruption. Its wording is future tense, so it is the announcement. Live status comes from the past-tense 'ran' lines in 2119 and 2125, not from 2112 alone.
Tentonhammer reports SOE offered a Double Station Cash event on Saturday for Free Realms players as compensation for a service interruption after a PlayStation Network security breach.

The year is 2011, sourced to Ten Ton Hammer. SOE's services, including Free Realms, were interrupted in April 2011 after an external intrusion, and the article gives April 21 as the date of the interruption.

SOE said it was working on a 'repair' plan for PS3 players of Free Realms and DC Universe Online, with details to follow. This is a plan, not a live event, and it is not counted as an occurrence. The pack's name 'Service interruption apology events' merges this plan with the Double Station Cash day, and the event here is the Double Station Cash day only.

Live status is 'yes' only on the strength of the wiki's July 29 to August 19, 2011 window and the article's 'limited time' wording. It is not a confirmed live window.

Items: ThunderCats T-shirt and Sword of Omens are sourced to articles 2237 and 2257 plus the wiki, so they are firm. Thundercats Seal has no tie to this promotion and is left out of items. ThunderCats Poster appears as several locale ids (435935, 435938, 435947) and the wiki title is 'Thundercats Poster'. Price is null: the items were free, and no currency is stated.

Zones, NPCs and quests are empty: no source names a zone, an NPC or a quest tied to this promotion. The Sword dialogue line is the weapon's own text, not an NPC. The quest-answer list in the pack was empty.
Recurring is null: only one occurrence (2011) is sourced, and no article says the promotion recurs.

The Memorial Day Pack promotion (7:00 AM PDT Fri 27 May to 11:59 PM PDT Mon 30 May 2011, 400 SC, 1300 SC value) is a separate event from this summer window. It is listed under open, not here.

open: The pack merges two events, so this answer covers one only. Event A, the summer Marketplace window, is the answer above. Event B should be its own calendar row with kind promotion, live yes, dated 2011-05-27 to 2011-05-30 PDT.

Article 2160 has no exact date. Its 'Posted 1 week, 6 days ago' relative date against the 2011-07-15 capture puts it around 2011-07-06 to 07-09, so the return is dated summer 2011 with the exact day unconfirmed.

Recurrence is unsure, not null. The Uncle Sam Outfit appears in a summer Marketplace in 2009 (articleId=137, Seaside Summer Splash, 2 July 2009) and in summer 2011 (articleId=2160, 2171). These may be different events, and the 2009 article ties the outfit to a different holiday. Same-event recurrence is not established.

Article 137 conflicts with the 2011 wiki and articles. It describes the outfit as a 2009 Seaside Summer Splash item. The 2011 sources place it at Memorial Day or summer 2011 and the wiki places it at Independence Day. Not resolved.
The summer sparkler name is unresolved. 2160 says Yellow, 2171 and the wiki say Golden. The client has no exact 'Yellow' string.
The Independence Day / 4 July window is only in undated wiki text. No dated article ties it to 2011.
Prices for the Uncle Sam Outfit and individual pieces are blank in the wiki and no article gives them. Price fields are null. The Summer Sparkler wiki pages also leave the price blank.
Zones, NPCs and quests: none in the pack or lookups. Left empty.
The pack title 'Uncle-Sam summer items' is a merged name. Its 'summer' label fits Event A. The May Memorial Day Pack in Event B is not a summer item.

The previous answer said the jacket and shoes could not be obtained specifically after 10 Aug 2011, which is narrower than needed. Article 2171's fact list does name the Uncle-Sam jacket and shoes as removed after that deadline, so that claim stands with the 2171 citation. The 2171 summary alone lists the outfit pieces together.

The Super Spooktacular is an annual event during the month of October in celebration of Halloween. The event features many objectives such as: stopping the Pumpkin Prince, Trick-or-Treat, ghost hunting, etc.

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

event.name: Merry Vale strange happenings (unconfirmed teaser, pack title)

evidence.claim: The pack title 'Merry Vale strange happenings' is the pack's own label. No source names it as an event. The only source is one archived 'What is New?' intro post, which says some visitors have reported strange happenings in Merry Vale and that the Mayor insists everything is fine. It is a hint in an introduction, not an announced event.
Article 254 is undated (date null) and its summary gives no dates, numbers or quest details. Nothing in the evidence gives a year, month or day for this event.
Article 254 is titled 'Meet Mayor McFairy' and introduces him as the cheerful mayor of Merry Vale who runs its festivities. The strange-happenings line is a hint in that introduction.
Mayor McFairy is listed under npcs on a thin tie: only the article line that the Mayor insists everything is fine. No other source ties him to the strange happenings.
Zone Merry Vale is named in the article as the location of the reported strange happenings.
Mayor McFairy is a Merry Vale NPC: the wiki page 'Mayor McFairy' (ns0) gives location only ('fairy NPC that can be found in Merry Vale'). The client names him as an NPC (locale:41231).

Video frame video:p5sDafXSQtQ/00010.jpg names the world Merry Vale and shows the Mayor McFairy nameplate. Frame video:p5sDafXSQtQ/00020.jpg shows the nameplate only, with world '-'. Location only, not tied to the event.

Client quest objective locale:441743 ('Shaggy Mysterychaser, an amateur detective in Merry Vale, needs me to find out what Mayor McFairy knows about the kidnappings') names Merry Vale. Locale:4420189 ('Talk to Mayor McFairy and see what he knows about the kidnappings!') carries no zone text. Both are a separate kidnappings mystery, and no source ties them to strange happenings, so they are not included as event items.

Lookup for 'strange happenings' and 'Merry Vale' across client, wiki, articles and video found no source tying a strange-happenings event to a quest, item, NPC, dated announcement or video frame. Article 254 is the only match.
evidence.source: lookup: strange happenings / Merry Vale (client, wiki, articles, video)

open: The event name is a teaser label from the pack, not a confirmed event name. The one article is an undated 'What is New?' intro that hints at strange happenings. It may not be an event at all, or it may be a story hook for a later event. It needs a dated article or a client quest before it becomes a real calendar entry.
Occurrences is empty: the only article is undated and the pack gives no year or month. Cannot say when, or whether it ran.
Live status is unsure: nothing shows the strange happenings went live. The pack's 'live' era tag is not enough to confirm it ran.
Recurring is null: one undated mention is not two occurrences and no article says it recurs.

NPCs: Mayor McFairy is listed on one article line only, the Mayor's denial. Wiki, client and video sources place him in Merry Vale but do not tie him to strange happenings. A calendar reviewer should confirm whether he belongs to this event or should be dropped.

Possible neighbour or alias: the Merry Vale kidnappings mystery (locale:441743, locale:4420189, Shaggy Mysterychaser) is a separate quest line that Mayor McFairy is part of. No source connects it to strange happenings, so it is not included. The merge or alias check should cover it. The pack title may also combine the teaser with other Merry Vale events (Festival of Hearts, Mysterious Merchant, Cakenstein, Birthday Party in Merry Vale, semi-formal dance); none is linked to strange happenings by a source here.
Quests, items, rewards and activities are empty: no source names any for this event. The pack's quest_answers list is empty.

Event name is verbatim from the pack, marked as a teaser. No aliases found in the evidence.

evidence.claim: The Station Cash Marketplace discount ran for three days, from 12:01 AM PDT on 8/10/2012 to 11:59 PM PDT on 8/12/2012. This run confirmed the times in the article 2716 index text (the earlier answer cited 2707 for them, but 2707 shows only the 8/12/12 end date).
The 2012 weekend sale gave 30% off Station Cash items on the marketplace during August 10 to 12, 2012.

Up to 30% off Station Cash items in the Marketplace, ends 8/12/12 ('Hurry, ends 8/12/12!'). This is the official news post for the Aug 2012 weekend sale. The membership exclusion is NOT shown in this post's indexed text.

The discount applies to Station Cash items in the Marketplace (article text says 'in the Marketplace'). The wording is 'in the Marketplace', not an explicit 'only'. This run did not find an explicit exclusion wording.

Article 2700 (Portuguese, 'Vem ai- Liquidacao do Fim de Semana!') gives its window as 8/10/2012 to 8/12/2012 with a 04:01 Brasilia start and 03:59 end. This is the same offer as the Aug 10-12 sale, with the pack's DD/MM reading (8 Oct to 8 Dec) wrong. Its publication date is unknown and it may be a pre-launch preview, so it is not used as a live-run source.

Other 2012 weekend Marketplace sales exist with different terms: a members-only 30% off Station Cash weekend sale (articles 2609, 2611). Their dates were not shown in this run's lookup output, so they are not dated here. They are separate events from the Aug 10-12 sale.

In-game UI banner 'Weekend Price Cuts' reads 'Everything in the Marketplace is 30% off!' with 'Time Left: 2 Days' (client locale:862, locale:863; video QPhBoJrHSDI frames 00040-00108). Its scope (everything, not only Station Cash) and dates are not tied to the Aug 2012 sale, so it is an unconfirmed candidate alias only.

open: Pack error: the pack's 'dates as written in DD/MM' reading of article 2700 (8 Oct to 8 Dec 2012) is contradicted by article 2716 ('12:01 AM PDT on 8/10/2012 to 11:59 PM PDT on 8/12/2012') and article 2712 ('August 10 to 12, 2012'). The correct live window is 8 Aug to 12 Aug 2012. The pack's DD/MM note should be corrected.

Merged events: the pack name 'Weekend Marketplace sale' covers at least three 2012 weekend sales (Feb, May, Aug). This answer covers only the Aug 10-12 Station Cash sale. The Feb and May sales need their own records. The Feb 17-20 dates (article 2528, locale:1420) and May 25-28 dates (articles 2609, 2611) were not rechecked in this run, so they are not stated here.

Membership exclusion: the earlier answer attributed 'memberships excluded' to article 2707. The indexed 2707 text does not show that exclusion (it has only a footnote asterisk). The French article 2710 ('subscriptions excluded') was not rechecked. The exclusion is unverified, so it is not stated as a claim.
Recurring is null. Weekend sales ran in Feb, May and Aug 2012 with different terms, and no article says they recur. The two-occurrence rule is not met.

Candidate alias 'Weekend Price Cuts' (locale:862, locale:863, video QPhBoJrHSDI frames) is not confirmed for this event. Its 'everything in the Marketplace' wording differs from the Station Cash scope in articles 2707 and 2712, and it is undated. It is not listed as a confirmed alias.

Article 2700 posting date is unknown (the pack has only 'about 2 months, 3 weeks ago' relative to capture), and its 'Vem ai' title suggests a pre-launch preview. Its window is not used as the live-run source.
Items: no specific item is named. The only item tie is 'all Station Cash items in the Marketplace', so the items list uses that group with no price beyond the discount.
No NPCs, quests, rewards, zones or quest answers are tied to this event. The pack's quest answers and wiki category are empty.

Undated items not used as occurrences: wiki images Summersalerotator.jpg and Newssale.png (Summer Madness and Back to School 50% off Marketplace sales, 'This Weekend ONLY'), and locale:1616 (Black Friday through Cyber Monday sales, which is FLAGged not_live). These may be other events of the same name.

Lookup queries with '%' or numeric time strings failed on FTS5 syntax in this run, so the time text was taken from a plain-word lookup of the articles index, not from a full-text match on the time string.

evidence.claim: SOE scheduled a community webcast on Free Realms changes and the Sunstone Valley area, streamed on Twitch TV, for Thursday 30 August 2012 at 20:00 Brasilia time (16:00 US Pacific), lasting about 15 minutes. This is the only occurrence in the pack.
The same webcast was announced for Thursday, August 30, 2012 at 4:00 p.m. US Pacific on Twitch TV, expected to last about 15 minutes. The two times are the same instant (23:00 UTC).

The webcast was to be hosted by producer Harvey Burgess with designers Eric Hankins and Chris Fritchoff, who would present the Sunstone Valley area and other game changes. Future tense in the quote, so this is a plan.
evidence.source: http://www.freerealms.com/article/detail.action?articleId=2748 (fact:event, quote: 'hosted by producer Harvey Burgess with designers Eric Hankins and Chris Fritchoff')

evidence.claim: Sunstone Valley was a new area of Free Realms that the webcast was to present, with other game changes also planned.
Article 2748 is a German-language post whose title is 'Free Realms erkundet das Sonnenstein-Tal'. The German title is an alias.

Article 2622 (June 14, 2012 webcast, 4:00 p.m. US Pacific, about 20 minutes) is a different webcast about the Shrouded Glade storyline, which teased Sunstone Valley's later in-game availability. It is not an occurrence of this event.
No source in the pack or lookup gives a second occurrence or says the webcast recurs.

open: Live is 'unsure', not 'yes'. The 2750 quote is future tense ('Junte-se a nos', join us on Thursday), and the 2748 quote is also future ('Seid am Donnerstag'). Only the scheduled date is sourced. No post-event report, Twitch VOD, or player account is in the pack or lookup. Confidence is capped until one is found.

Alias and source gaps: articleId=2748 German title 'Free Realms erkundet das Sonnenstein-Tal' is added as an alias. The pack's names_seen and article_summaries list only 2750, so 2747 and 2748 are cited but not in the pack lists. The past-tense '2012 webcast' gloss on 2748 is the summary's wording, not the quote, so it is not used as proof the event ran.

Time conflict in articleId=2748: its quote gives 'Seid am Donnerstag dem 30. August, 2012 um 1:00 CET auf Twitch TV'. 1:00 CET on 30 August is the evening of 29 August in Brasilia, so it does not match 20:00 Brasilia on 30 August. It is treated as an outlier and not used. The 2750 and 2747 times are preferred because they agree.
Article 2750 has date null. The year 2012 comes from the quote text and from 2747 and 2748, not from a stamped article date.

Article articleId=2622 is a separate June 14, 2012 webcast about the Shrouded Glade storyline, with Sunstone Valley teased for later availability. The pack's note that it was about Sunstone Valley is inaccurate. It is a separate event and not a live occurrence of this one.
Hosts Harvey Burgess, Eric Hankins and Chris Fritchoff are SOE staff, not in-game NPCs, so npcs is empty. Their names come from articleId=2748 (fact:event), not 2747 as the critique said.
Zones is empty. Sunstone Valley is the subject area previewed, not a zone the sources tie to the event window. articleId=2774 calls it a new adventure area in a separate developer video feature.
Activities is empty. The only sourced activity is the planned presentation, which is a plan and not a player activity. Watching the webcast is not an in-game player activity, so it is not listed.

Items, quests, rewards and video refs are empty. Sunstone Valley items (Sunstone Environment Bundle, Sunstone Mystery pieces), quests (Freewheelers chain, Arch Druid Camellia, Dorn Geargrinder escort) and exploration rares are area content with no source tying them to the webcast. Lookup locale hits for them are at lines 976, 1660, 1695 and 3793-3797. Video frames from lookup (b6QfVC_2YpQ, 1lZYJLpat5Q, WjpJl2U5OK0 and others) show the area in play, not the webcast.

evidence.claim: Pack event 'Super Secret Stuff: Sunstone Valley Part 2' is a single SOE news post (articleId=2774) announcing a developer video with Ryan Shannon giving an 'insider look' at Sunstone Valley, a new adventure area. It is a preview, not a live event.
The article has no written details about features, quests, mechanics or items, and no posting date can be determined from the capture.
Quote: 'Here's a video with Ryan Shannon from the development team.'
Sunstone Valley is a zone that exists in the client (locale:1695 'Sunstone Valley', locale:3793 'Sunstone Valley'). This is the zone name only; it does not tie any item, NPC or quest to this event.

Tentonhammer reports Sunstone Valley launched as Free Realms' first area expansion update, adding a new zone. This is a separate update announcement, not the Part 2 preview; its date is not in the pack.

A separate Super Secret Stuff video, hosted by artist Misty Michelle, previewed concept art and environments for the upcoming Sunstone Valley region. That is a different video in the same series, so the pack's name merges at least two Super Secret Stuff items.
Articles 2747 and 2750 describe a 2012 webcast presenting Sunstone Valley and its activities. This may be the live-webcast event the pack is missing, but the pack does not tie it to the Part 2 post.

'Super Secret Stuff' is a series label on several SOE videos (Clockwork Mystery Chests, Farming, Baron von Darkcheat expansion, TCG Expansion Heroes). It is not one event, so the name is not evidence of recurrence for this event.
evidence.source: wiki File:Free Realms Super Secret Stuff; http://www.tentonhammer.com:80/free-realms/news/soe-offers-a-peek-at-free-realms-upcoming-sunstone-valley-region

open: Event name and kind: the pack's 'Super Secret Stuff: Sunstone Valley Part 2' is a developer video preview (kind 'other'), not a live event. It has no live date and no occurrence in the sources, so the answer for this pack is not a live event.
Date: article 2774 has no date (null in the pack). No year or month can be stated from sources. A first-party date would need the freerealms.com article page or an archive capture with a timestamp.

Merge: the pack name 'Super Secret Stuff: Sunstone Valley Part 2' may merge the Ryan Shannon developer video (2774) with the Misty Michelle Super Secret Stuff video (Ten Ton Hammer). Both were previews of Sunstone Valley. They should be separate records, and the pack has no evidence that they are one event.

Possible missed event: the 2012 Sunstone Valley webcast (articleId 2747 and 2750, 'Free Realms Explores Sunstone Valley') may be the live event this pack is meant to cover. The pack does not link it, and no date for it is in the pack. Needs its article date.

Sunstone Valley zone launch (tentonhammer 'free-realms-launches-sunstone-valley-expansion') is an update, not an event. Its date is not in the pack. It may be the launch that followed the Part 2 preview, but no source here ties them.

Zones: only Sunstone Valley is sourced (client locale and articles). No sub-zone is tied to this event by a source. Rumble Ridge, Red's Haven and The Dig are wiki zone pages, but the wiki does not tie them to this preview.

NPCs, quests, items, rewards and activities: none are sourced to this event. The client has many Sunstone Valley quests and items (locale 976, 847, 848, 1836, 1847-1856, 1877, 3795-3797) and wiki NPCs (Sandscale Hunter). None are linked to the Part 2 preview, so I left them out.

wiki_page.title: Spring Eggstravaganza
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px|Alyssa Eggelyn
Spring Eggstravaganza was an event held everyday from the 28th of March to the 31st of March. There will be a quest given to you from Alyssa Eggelyn. You see, every year a group of robgoblins takes one of her eggs and hides it somewhere in the world. You will have to find hidden eggs in Sacred Grove, when you find one on it's appropriate day you will be able to color it and open it on the Spring Eggstravagansa day. If you find all 4 eggs, you can open the large egg on the Spring Eggstravagansa day too. Without her eggs, Alyssa will have nothing to open on Eggstravaganza Day, so it's up to you to find her missing eggs.

Quests
An option to teleport to Alyssa Eggelyn is available on the overlay that displays when players log in to the game. The series consists of four quests to locate an egg, with one quest unlocking each day. The reward for completing the daily quest includes an egg and an egg coloring kit. Completing all four quests rewards a special bonus egg which is the meta goal of the event.

Quest:The Spring Eggstravaganza
Quest:The Eggcellent Egg Hunt
Quest:The Eggcitingly Eggcellent Egg Hunt
Quest:The Eggxtremely Eggcitingly Eggcellent Egg Hunt

Locations of the Eggs
A list of locations where eggs can be found:
 In the Briarwood Maze a short distance from Snarling Hedges
 On the lake that borders the Blackspore Swamp
 On a hill near a house by Floren Forest
 Behind a large pile of colorful gems in the low level mine of Snowhill

Rewards
Small Eggs
These are the 4 possible rewards you receive when opening the 4 eggs.

 Handful of Jelly Beans x20
 Jack the Rabbit - Pet Pal
 Bunny Goggles
 Spring Eggstravaganza Basket
thumb|250px|Opening the eggs on March 31st
Big Egg
There is only one possible rewards to get when opening this egg: Big Bu

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

svhooligans.title: Farnum's Love the Land Party

evidence.claim: Event is Farnum's Love the Land Party, a community event at Farnum Farm where players dance, harvest, play games, wear farming clothes and visit friends.
evidence.source: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=1275 (fact:event and summary); locale:6539 ('Community Event: Farnum's Love the Land Party'); locale:6621 ('Every year Farnum Farm hosts a party honoring the land that grows the food for Free Realms')

evidence.claim: Article 1275 is a 'What is New?' post announcing the party with two session times on Server 1 in 2010: Thursday 22 April 2010 3pm Pacific (U.S. and Latin America), and Friday 23 April 2010 9:00am Pacific / 4:00pm GMT (UK and Europe).
Yearly recurrence is stated by two sources: article 1275 says Farnum Farm 'hosts a yearly community party' and locale:6621 says 'Every year'. Only April 2010 is attested with dates.
The pack key 'hooligans' is not an event. Its sources are a hostile faction and a location post: Cal, leader of the hooligans; a Hooligan gang led by Mac; article 624 (location post, no dates).
Article 624 is a Farnum Farmstead location post captured 2009-11-23 per its summary. It gives no event dates and is not an event announcement.

No quest, NPC, item, reward or station-cash price is tied to the party by any source read. The Pappy Farnum / Party Planning lines (locale:35635, 35634, 35627, 35625) are all FLAG not_live and concern a Queen of Sanctuary party. No source read links them to Love the Land.

open: Pack mismatch: the pack key 'hooligans' is not a live event. It names a hostile faction (locale:5495, locale:4420097) and a location post (article 624). The pack should be re-keyed to "Farnum's Love the Land Party" or dropped. The alias 'Love the Land Party' is supported by locale:6539 and article 1275. The pack's 'hooligans' key was never attested as an alias. Rerun the pack under the new name.

Live is 'unsure'. Article 1275 is an announcement and the pack gives no publish or capture date for it. The 2010 session times are scheduled dates from the announcement, not confirmed run dates. Recorded as an occurrence only.

Occurrences: one dated occurrence, 2010 (Thu 22 Apr 3pm Pacific, US and Latin America; Fri 23 Apr 9:00am Pacific / 4:00pm GMT, UK and Europe; Server 1), from article 1275. No other year is attested with dates.
Recurrence: yearly, stated by article 1275 and locale:6621. The month is confirmed only for 2010 (April). The recurrence month is not confirmed.

Zones: left empty. 'Farnum Farm' is a location name from article 1275, and 'Farnum's Farmstead' is a quest-objective location in locale:35635. Neither is confirmed as the party's game zone, so they need a separate lookup before a zone is recorded.
Items, rewards, price and currency are empty. No source ties any item to the party, and the pack lists none.

Quests and NPCs are empty. No source read ties the Party Planning quest (locale:35625 et al., FLAG not_live) to Love the Land. The shared Farnum name is not a link by itself. The quest is not confirmed as related to the party in any way.
Wireable: false. The 2010 session dates can be recorded as occurrences, but live status and any year beyond 2010 are unconfirmed, so the calendar cannot schedule the party yet.
Article 624 (captured 2009-11-23 per its summary) gives a capture date only, not an event date.

evidence.claim: Only one article in the pack covers this: a December 2009 'In The Works' preview. Its quote is 'Challenge your friends to see who can bounce the most times between multiple spots without missing!' The name 'Bounce platform challenge' does not appear in that quote or in the article text. It is a label from the pack's names_seen, not from a source.
The preview is a plan, not a live event. Its era is pre_launch_plan, and it describes a secret feature to come. Under the job rules it does not show the challenge ever ran.

The preview describes the bounce platforms as a world-wide network of platforms that catapult the player high into the air when they jump onto one. Players can bounce from platform to platform. It names Seaside and Snowhill as locations for the platforms, not for the challenge.
The preview says the platforms are part of a month that also brings housing, fishing and new pets. That month is not named or dated in the source, so no run dates for the challenge can be given.

The client has a chain-bounce launch-pad quest, Launching The Distance, where Hank Highjump sends the player to Morgan Webfoot on Shadeside Island. No source in the pack ties it to the challenge, so it is excluded from quests.
Parachutes and bouncepads appear in client text with Hank Highjump in Seaside. No source ties this to the challenge, so it is excluded from npcs and items.
The wiki Items page lists Medium Launch Pad and Large Launch Pad among platform items. The page is a general list, not a category tied to the challenge, so no item is listed for the event.

open: Pack merge risk: 'Bounce platform challenge' seems to combine one line of a feature preview (the bounce-platform network, article 679) with a challenge. The preview is the only source, and the pack's name is not in it. Treat the event as unverified.

live is 'unsure', not 'no'. The only source is a pre-launch plan, so nothing shows the challenge ran, and nothing shows it did not. Needs an article or forum post from the event month that confirms a run with dates.
occurrences is empty. The preview is dated December 2009 by its post, but the event month is not stated, and no source gives run dates for the challenge.
kind is 'other'. It is a player challenge inside a monthly feature preview, not a clear holiday, weekly or contest. Confirm the category once a live run is confirmed.
quests is empty. No exact quest title is tied to the challenge. Launching The Distance (locale:424932 / 424939) is a neighbouring chain-bounce quest with no source linking it to the challenge.
npcs is empty. Hank Highjump and Morgan Webfoot appear in client text, but no source ties either to the challenge.
items is empty. The wiki Items page lists launch pads and other platform items, but no source ties any item to the challenge, and the pack's wiki_category_members is empty.
rewards is empty. No source states any reward.
zones: Seaside and Snowhill are named in the preview, but only as locations for the platform network, not confirmed as the challenge's location. Left out of zones.

No alias beyond the pack label was found. Lookups on 'bounce platform', 'bounce challenge' and 'bounce' matched only article 679 for the event, plus unrelated client text (Yeti Bouncer, Lakeshore bounce text, Dares boombox items), which I excluded.
The preview's 'multiple spots' wording may be the planned name or rule set, but no source gives an official event name. The pack name is kept only as an unverified label.

svstation-cash-25-bonus-week.title: Station Cash 25% Bonus Week

evidence.claim: Promotion was a 25% Station Cash bonus on pre-paid Free Realms retail game cards, Starter Cards excluded, redeemable during a late-November 2009 window
Primary window per the Free Realms post: redeem between 10am PST Nov 23 and 10pm PST Nov 30, 2009. The quoted text has no year; 2009 comes from the TenTonHammer article.

TenTonHammer gives the promotion week as Monday Nov 23 through Sunday Nov 29, 2009, with cards to be redeemed within that week. This conflicts with the Free Realms end date and is kept as a secondary source.
Station Cash cards were redeemable in Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest II during the promotion. This is in the TenTonHammer article summary field, not a quoted fact.
The bonus is paid in Station Cash, the in-game currency
The promotion is tied to Thanksgiving week 2009 by the TenTonHammer summary

event.name: Station Cash 25% Bonus Week
aliases: Station Cash bonus promotion (retail cards, Nov 2009)

occurrences.when: 2009-11-23 10:00 PST to 2009-11-30 22:00 PST (Free Realms window, primary). TenTonHammer conflicting secondary: Mon Nov 23 to Sun Nov 29, 2009.

activities: Buy a pre-paid Free Realms retail Station Cash card at a participating retailer and redeem it in Free Realms during the window to get the 25% bonus (articleId=629)
rewards: 25% bonus Station Cash on the value of retail Station Cash cards redeemed in the window; Free Realms Starter Cards excluded (articleId=629)
open: Date conflict: the Free Realms post (primary) gives 10pm PST Nov 30 as the end. TenTonHammer gives Sun Nov 29. The when field uses the primary window. Confirm the end day against the live article before the calendar is loaded.

The Free Realms quote has no year. 2009 comes from TenTonHammer and the pack's capture date. Article 629 has no published date (date null in the pack). Its relative stamp, 'Posted 6 days, 1 hour ago' against a 2009-11-27 capture, would put posting around Nov 21, 2009. Not verified.
The EverQuest and EverQuest II redemption claim is confirmed only in the TenTonHammer summary field, not a quoted fact. Keep it as a secondary-source claim.
The title is the pack's label, not a quoted source name. Sources call it a Station Cash bonus promotion tied to Thanksgiving week and retail cards.
Recurring is null: only the 2009 occurrence is sourced. The 2012 CVS double Station Cash and the Feb 29 2012 Extra Day Extra Cash (locale:632, FLAG not_live) are separate promotions.
Client locale:4850 mentions a Station Cash bonus week for a Marketplace pet outfit sale. It has no date and no link to the retail-card promotion, so it is not attributed here.

No items, NPCs, zones or quests are tied to this event by any source. The wiki category is empty and the pack has no quest answers. Generic card bonus items (articleId=68) are not dated to this event.
Video ad frames (Cyber Monday Dec 2nd 25% BONUS SC, 7-Eleven 2013 SC promotion) are different events and are not attributed.

wireable stays false until the end day is confirmed. Once fixed as 2009-11-23 10:00 PST to 2009-11-30 22:00 PST, it can be wired as a one-time promotion with activity 'redeem retail Station Cash card' and reward '25% bonus Station Cash', excluding Starter Cards.

evidence.claim: Article 70 (undated post, captured May 2, 2009) states 'The Beta phase is over, and now there's even more to do and see!'. This is a one-time state change marking the end of the beta. The article has no post date.

The pre-launch FAQ says accepted beta testers could play free and use Members Only content during the beta, and that this access ends at launch unless the tester becomes a member. This is a pre-launch plan, not a live event, so it is context only. It links beta access to launch but does not set the beta-end date.

As of late February 2009 Free Realms had entered closed beta, with open beta registration accepted and open beta planned for early April 2009. This bounds the beta window to 2009 and gives no end date.

open: Membership is a separate standing product offer, not part of this event. Article 70 also offers a paid Membership upgrade at $4.99 per month plus applicable taxes, with Members getting exclusive content, extra Jobs (Wizard, Warrior), leaderboard access and more than one character. It is sourced to http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=70 (undated, captured May 2, 2009) and should be recorded as its own standing-product entry, not as this event's evidence or reward.

Timing: the year is 2009 only. Article 70 has no post date, and May 2, 2009 is a capture date, not a post date. The month of the beta-end transition is not confirmed. The beta-to-launch window is bounded by the tentonhammer note (closed beta late Feb 2009, open beta planned early April 2009). No date can be scheduled from the sources, so this event is not wireable.
Classification: kind is 'other' and live is 'unsure'. The source supports only a one-time state change (the beta is over). It does not show a live event that players ran, so no other kind fits.

The whatIsBeta.vm FAQ ties end-of-beta access to launch as a pre-launch plan. It is the only source linking beta end to launch. That plan does not confirm when beta ended, so the beta-end date remains unconfirmed.

Items, quests, NPCs, zones, activities and rewards: none are tied to this event by any source. The pack lists no quests, NPCs or wiki category members. Exclusive Beta Tester's Cap (wiki) is tied to beta testing, not the beta-end event, so it is left out. locale:430711 'Beta Test!' and locale:3018 are not tied to the beta-end event.

Aliases: only the pack title 'Beta phase end' is confirmed. The phrase 'The Beta phase is over' is a quote, not an alias. The pack may merge the beta-end state change with the membership sale under one name, which the standing-product note above separates.

Name collision: 'Beta' appears in unrelated client text (fishing quest 'Bitter Beta' at locale 409212 to 409523, and China Closed Beta What's New at locale 495 to 497, flagged not_live). Lookup also shows tentonhammer posts node 66937 (contest) and node 66931 (giveaway) about closed beta keys. These are separate promotions, not this event.
occurrences: one entry, year 2009, when unknown (after closed beta, before or around the May 2, 2009 capture). recurring is null because only one occurrence exists in the sources.

activities: Open PvP duel started from another player's radial menu 'Duel' option; accepting player moved to a private dueling area. Two regional time slots on Server 1 (US/LatAm 3-5 Pacific, UK/Europe 9-11 Pacific).

evidence.claim: Announced open player-vs-player duel at the Briarheart Warpstone on Friday December 4th, on Server 1, open to all levels and jobs, in two regional time slots: US/LatAm 3-5 Pacific and UK/Europe 9-11 Pacific. Stated as a pre-launch announcement; no source confirms it ran.
Duels start from another player's radial menu via the 'Duel' option; the accepting player is moved to a private dueling area.
The Briarheart Warpstone is the meeting point: players were told to show up there ready to duel.
'Briarheart Warpstone' is a client place name.

Year not given by article 651. The pack gives a null date and says the post was made 1 week and 3 days before capture. 2009 is only an inference (4 December is a Friday in 2009 within the live era), so it is not written as a sourced occurrence year.

A same-format duel event, 'Day of the Duel', ran at Highroad Junction on July 31, 2009, 3pm-5pm Pacific, with any class, level or weapon, and Ambassador Pex accepting duels. Different place and date from 651, so not merged. It may be the same event family.
The wiki 'Community Events' page lists 'Day of the Duel' as a warpstone duel event with combat jobs.

open: Year not stated in any source. Article 651 gives only 'Friday December 4th' and 'posted 1 week, 3 days before capture'. Occurrence year stays null and wireable is false until article 651's publication date is found. 2009 is an inference only.
Live status unsure: article 651 is a pre-launch announcement, and no second article, forum post or video confirms the duel ran.
Recurrence unknown: one undated occurrence (651) and one dated but different event (173) do not establish recurrence. No source says it recurs.

Name: 'Briarheart Dueling' is a pack-assigned name, not the article's title (651 is titled 'Free Realms - What is New?' and never names the event). It is kept as an alias; the event name uses the place and date instead. The pack may have merged or missed an alias: 'Day of the Duel' (article 173, wiki) has the same radial-menu duel format and may be the same event family. Not merged, because place and date differ. Needs the publication date of 651 and a check of whether the Day of the Duel series recurs.
Hours: the pack gives 3-5 and 9-11 as Pacific hours without am/pm. The article summary does not state am/pm, so none is written here.
Zone: only the Briarheart Warpstone is named. No zone name is given. Briarheart Palace and Briarheart Caverns are separate places tied to other content and are excluded.
Items, rewards and price: none tied to this event by an article list, a wiki category or a client name. Empty.

NPCs and quests: none named for this event in article 651 or the pack. Ambassador Pex is named only for article 173 (Day of the Duel), so he is not attached here. No quest answers mention this event. Empty.
Client 'Card Duelist' strings refer to the TCG and are not this event.

evidence.claim: Job Sampling Week ran Nov 9-13, 2009, with one job trainer meeting per day: Mon Nov 9 Archer, Tue Nov 10 Wizard, Wed Nov 11 Medic, Thu Nov 12 Blacksmith, Fri Nov 13 Warrior. The dates come from article 580's summary in the pack, not a quote from the article, and the article date is null in the pack.
Job Sampling is a community event week in which SOE staff met players at job trainers on consecutive days to socialize, answer questions, trade equipment and duel.
Archer job sampling on Monday November 9th, meeting at Lugabow, the Archer trainer, near the Bandit Hideout.
Medic job sampling on Wednesday November 11th, meeting at Nurse Naia in Sanctuary, southeast of the great tree.
Blacksmith job sampling on Thursday November 12th, meeting at Smitty, the Blacksmith trainer, just outside the Singing Crystals Mine.
Warrior job sampling on Friday November 13th, meeting at Drill Sergeant Dewey, the Warrior trainer near the Snowhill Town Hall.
Wizard job sampling on Tuesday November 10th, meeting at Fizzlesticks, the Wizard trainer, near the Robgoblin Trove north of Lakeshore.
A different job was highlighted each day of the week, with a new article daily and players invited to the Job Sampling Community Events.
Past-tense confirmation that the event week ran: a different job was featured each day, and players were invited to join the Job Sampling Community Events.

open: Free-account job access (article 572: characters created after November 1, 2009 on free accounts can play all jobs up to level 5 free; Members Only from level 5) is removed from rewards. Article 572 ties the policy to the name 'Job Sampling' only, not to the Nov 9-13, 2009 week, so it may be a standing policy rather than an event reward. Add it as an event reward only if a source ties it to Nov 9-13, 2009. The wiki Jobs page says jobs unlock with membership after level 4, so whether the free access ended is also unclear.

Pack merge risk: the pack's twice-daily Server 1 time slots (4pm-5pm PT for US/LatAm, 9am-10am PT for UK/EU) come from article 580, but the quote does not name Job Sampling. Article 580 is a multi-item 'What is New?' page, so those times may belong to another event. They are left out of the event facts until a source ties them to Job Sampling.

Dates: the pack gives article dates as null. The year 2009 comes from the pack's summary text ('Nov 9-13, 2009') and article 572's 'November 1, 2009'. The weekday-date pairs are consistent with 2009, but no article date is confirmed from the article itself. The Nov 9-13 dates should be cited to article 580's summary, not treated as a direct quote.

Aliases: 'Job Sampling', 'Job Sampling Week' (pack title and summary), 'Job Sampling Community Events' (articles 589, 605, 607). 'Job Sampling Week schedule' is the pack title only and is not confirmed as an article title.
Zones: none sourced. The sources name only landmarks (Bandit Hideout, Robgoblin Trove north of Lakeshore, Sanctuary, Singing Crystals Mine, Snowhill Town Hall), so zones is empty.
Quests: none. quest_answers_mentioning_it is empty and no quest title is sourced.
Items and prices: none sourced. The articles mention trading equipment but name no items, prices or currency. The wiki category for this event is empty.
Rewards: none sourced for the event. The only job-access perk (article 572) is listed in open, not rewards.
Locale 6649 'Job Sampling!' has no surrounding context, so it is a weak tie to the event and is not used as an occurrence source.
Live: set to yes from articles 589, 605 and 607 and the meeting schedule in article 580. Article 607 is the only past-tense confirmation that the week ran.
Recurring: null. Only one occurrence (Nov 2009) is sourced and no article says it recurs.

The post has no gameplay, quest, item or mechanics details. Its date is not stated; only a relative 'Posted 1 year, 1 month ago' against a 2011-02-08 capture is shown, so no year or month can be sourced from it.
Wiki page Chatty lists 'Free Realms [Holiday] [TV] [Spot]' under Appearances.
Wiki page Snowface lists 'Free Realms [Holiday] [TV] [Spot]' under Appearances.
Wiki page Abominable Snowman lists 'Free Realms [Holiday] [TV] [Spot]' under Appearances. This ties the NPC to the spot as a commercial appearance only, not to an in-game event.
Article 752 is a Spanish-language news post promoting the same new TV commercials and linking a new video. It may be the Spanish counterpart of 744, but this is not confirmed in the pack.

Other TV commercial posts exist and are separate spots, including 'Tiger Ride TV Spot' (articleId 1747), 'Party Time' (articleId 1199), and the Spanish posts 2148/2149 showing biking, houses, outfits and farming. None of these is tied to the holiday spot by any source here.

open: Event kind: this is a TV commercial announcement, not a playable live event. 'promotion' is the closest kind, but the event may not belong in the events calendar at all. Bryce should decide.
live is 'unsure': the post is an official news item that says the spot is 'newest' and 'on TV yet', but no date or in-game presence is sourced. The pack gives no real date for this event.

occurrences is empty. The article has no year or month, and the pack gives no second occurrence. The 'Holiday' name hints at a holiday season, but no source states the year or days. Needs the article's archived page date (Wayback capture of articleId=744) or the TV air dates.
recurring is null: one article, and no source says it recurs.

NPCs Chatty, Snowface and Abominable Snowman appear only as wiki 'Appearances' of the spot. They are not confirmed as event participants. wiki_category_members in the pack is empty, so no category tie was found. Listed here with that caveat.

Possible merge or alias risk: articleId 752 (Spanish) may be the same post as 744. The pack lists only the English title. Other TV spots (Yeti [TV] [Spot], Snow Days Commercial, Tiger Ride, Party Time, the 2148/2149 posts) are separate commercials and were not merged. Confirm before merging.
zones, quests, activities, items, rewards are empty: no source ties any of them to this event. The Chatty page's 'Quest:Meet and Greet' is not linked to the spot in the sources read and was left out.
locale search for TV spot / commercial terms returned no matches, so the client side has no tagged evidence for this spot.
lookup with the query 'articleId=744' failed (FTS5 syntax error on '='), so article 744's own page text was not read directly. Only the pack's summary and the fact row were used.

evidence.claim: The pack's only event-level fact is that clicking the party cake in a party area gives a temporary illusion. The label 'Party area cake' is the pack's own name, not an article title or event name.
Party Planner NPCs teleport Members to party areas in Sanctuary, Lakeshore and Briarwood. Members can teleport non-Member friends into a party.
Courtney Lakebash is the Lakeshore party planner; she teleports Members to a tree house party area on a walkway.
Mandy Vide (pack-era spelling in article 763) is the Briarwood party planner near the Bristlewood warpstone; her party is in the towers above Tanglewood Fort. Article 937 spells the name Mandy Vice.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

wiki_page.title: SOE Live
wiki_page.text:
right
SOE Live is an annual convention based around SOE games. The event features SOE staff, game panels, contests, parties, and more. Formerly the celebration had been named SOE Fan Faire up until it switched to SOE Live in 2012.

Free Realms has been included in these events since SOE Fan Faire 2008. Along with inclusion, each annual event has featured announcements on the plans for the future of Free Realms and attendee exclusive Free Realms perks.

Years of SOE Live
SOE Fan Faire 2008
center|500px

SOE Fan Faire 2009
center|500px

SOE Fan Faire 2010
center|500px
SOE Live 2010 was held at Bally's, Las Vegas from August 5th through August 8th, 2010.

evidence.claim: Demos of The Agency and Free Realms were planned for SOE's 2008 Fan Faire. This is a pre-launch plan, not a confirmed live demo.
SOE's 2008 Fan Faire was scheduled for August 14-17, 2008 at the Las Vegas Hilton, Las Vegas, Nevada. These are convention dates, used only as context.
The 2008 Fan Faire promotional art reads LAS VEGAS 2008, AUGUST 14 - 17.

Free Realms has been included in SOE Fan Faire / SOE Live events since SOE Fan Faire 2008, and each annual event featured Free Realms plan announcements and attendee-exclusive perks. This is general wiki text, undated per year, and does not confirm that the 2008 demo ran.
Post-event day-one recap node/41251 has only brief, pre-launch remarks on Free Realms. Day-two recap node/41337 mentions Free Realms once, as a teaser. Neither confirms a demo.
Post-event day-one write-up node/41260 quotes SOE CEO John Smedley at length on Free Realms, calling it more than a teen/tween game with deep gameplay. It does not say a demo ran at the event.
Attendees of the 2008 Fan Faire were flagged for Free Realms beta access starting April 16, 2009. The headline in node/66944 is undated and is not used for timing.
Free Realms was only a podcast segment at Fan Faire 2007 (August 2-5, Las Vegas), so it is not this event.

Locale ids: 435899 is named for SOE Fan Faire 2011, 156926 and 156928 are named for Fan Faire 2010, and 436136 is named for Fan Faire 2011. These are convention items from later years. locale:435898 ('Fan Faire Pack') carries no year in the index, so its convention is unknown.

open: Not wireable: no source confirms the Free Realms demo ran at the 2008 Fan Faire. The only dated timing is a pre-event plan (node/30684), so the calendar must not schedule this as a live event. live stays unsure.

Name fix: the pack title merges two things. SOE Fan Faire is a yearly SOE convention (2007-2011), renamed SOE Live from 2012 per wiki page:ns0 SOE Live. The Free Realms showing is a single planned 2008 event, and this entry covers only the showing. The convention is context only. A separate convention entry would be needed for the Fan Faire itself.

Aliases: the pack misses the wiki's naming for the convention, SOE Live, and the bare '[Fan] [Faire]' form. Both name the convention rather than the 2008 showing, so they are left out of this event's aliases. 'SOE Fan Faire 2008' is also left out for the same reason.
Activities: the 'attended a showcase demo' entry was a pre-launch plan, so activities is empty. It can return only after a post-event source names a demo.
Rewards: the beta access is a convention-attendee reward, not a demo reward. It is kept in rewards with that label and the April 16, 2009 start date (node/66874).

Items stay empty. No source ties any 2008 item to the showing. The Fan Faire Pack and T-shirts that appear in the index are from later conventions. locale:435898 has no year, so its convention is unknown and it is not attributed.

Recurring is null. The wiki (page:ns0 SOE Live) says Free Realms was included in each annual event since 2008, but that is an undated wiki claim, not an article that dates each occurrence. The showing itself has one dated occurrence.

Unresolved lead: freerealms.com article detail.action?articleId=156 is a Free Realms news post written after the Las Vegas Fan Faire, summarising John Smedley's State of the Game (planned Kart Racer and Demolition Derby quests). The lookup shows no date, and the year is not stated. If it is dated to August 2008, it could be the post-event source the showing needs. Date it before using it.

Excluded as unrelated: the CES 2009 Free Realms demo (node/61373), the 2009 Comic-Con '[Demo] Derby' items, and the 2009 SOE Podcast #66 (node/70751). The July 22, 2009 forum thread relays Fan Faire 2009 plans, not 2008.

evidence.claim: Event is the Zadira Coin Exploration player meetup: meet at the warp stone of a designated area, then explore until all rare and elite coins of that area are found. Source names it only in the wiki page, with no year.
Schedule line on the same page reads 'Every other Friday' for the Coin Exploration event. It is undated, so no occurrence can be given.

The 'Every Saturday night' line on that page describes a separate weekly trading party hosted by Marisol Bluesurf at the Merry Vale warp stone. It is not the coin hunt and does not contradict the Friday line.
Zadira Kindleriver is listed as a Mystic Mayhem guild member and organiser. The pack does not show that this person is an NPC, so npcs is left empty.

Rare Exploration Coin (locale 386170) and Elite Exploration Coin (locale 4412) are the two coin items. Both ids were confirmed by ids. The Zadira page names rare and elite coins as the hunt target, so they are listed as items of this event, with no price.
evidence.source: locale:386170; locale:4412; wiki page:ns0 | Zadira Kindleriver

evidence.claim: The June 2009 forum thread about Explorer coin locations shows player interest only. It describes no event being held, so it is not an occurrence.
The standing Exploration and Rare Exploration collections are separate from this hunt. They belong on their own collections entry, not this one.

open: Critique 1 fixed: the Saturday line is not a contradiction. It is a separate weekly trading party, so recurring stays null because the Friday line is undated, not because of a conflict.

Critique 2 fixed: items now lists Rare Exploration Coin (locale 386170) and Elite Exploration Coin (locale 4412), sourced to the Zadira wiki page, which names them as the hunt target. The date remains unresolved.
Critique 3 fixed: the source is cited as 'wiki page:ns0 | Zadira Kindleriver' with no NPC label. npcs is empty because the pack does not show Zadira as an NPC.
Live is unsure. The pack has no dated announcement and no year. Do not schedule this as a live event until a dated article confirms it.
Name merge is unresolved. The pack's name 'Explorer coins' may be the collection coins, this hunt, or another event. Not used as an alias here.
The forum thread is kept as player-interest evidence only, not an occurrence.
Zones and rewards are empty. No source names a zone or reward for this event.
Lookup note: quest_cli.py lookup crashes on non-ASCII output under -I with the default cp1252 console. Running it with python -X utf8 -I works.

Not checked in this run: the Explorer Chests wiki page, the locale 119094 to 119103 'Find all Rare Exploration coins in <area>' entries (collection tasks, to be checked on the collections entry), and article 144's 'Sanctuary Rare Exploration coins' alias.

aliases: Buttercup Webbywand spider rescue (Spanish articles name the NPC Flori Telarañas)
Eight-Legged Friend (client quest title, from earlier pass; not re-checked here)

zones: Briarwood (quest zone; wiki Category:Briarwood on Buttercup Webbywand; article 924 route starts at the Briarwood warpstone)
Grexan's Camp (location where the spider is held; locale:162 'Grexan's Camp')
npcs: Flori Telarañas (articles 927 and 928 only; Spanish; likely the same character under another name, unconfirmed)
quests: Eight-Legged Friend (locale:390870, taken from the earlier pass; this pass's locale lookup by ID failed, so re-verify)
activities: Teleport to the Briarwood teleport stone or warpstone and climb the hill to the tunnel (article 924 and 928)
Find the NPC just outside the tunnel (articles 924, 927, 928)
Explore Grexan's Camp and rescue the captured pet spider (locale:116034 'Free the spider held captive in Grexan's Camp.'; locale:390663 'Save Buttercup Webbywand's spider from Grexan's Camp.')
Avoid being wrapped in a cocoon (article 928, Spanish quote 'te podrías ver envuelto en una crisálida si es que te descuidas')

evidence.claim: Article 924 (Buttercup Webbywand) gives the quest: teleport to the Briarwood warpstone, head up the hill to a large tunnel, find Buttercup, explore Grexan's Camp and rescue the spider.
Article 928 (Spanish) gives the same route with Flori Telarañas: Briarwood teleport stone, climb the hill, find Flori outside the tunnel, rescue the pet spider, beware the cocoon.
Article 927 (Spanish) gives a Thorny Forest teleport-stone route to the same camp and the same Flori rescue.
Article 98 names Buttercup Webbywand with the task 'Rescue the spider kidnapped by trolls' at Grexan's Camp.
Buttercup Webbywand is a wizard pixie NPC in Briarwood whose pet spider is captured when she explores Grexan's Camp.
evidence.source: wiki page 'Buttercup Webbywand' (ns0; Category:NPC, Pixie, Wizard, Briarwood)

evidence.claim: Client text ties the rescue to Buttercup's spider.
evidence.source: locale:390663 'Save Buttercup Webbywand's spider from Grexan's Camp.'

evidence.claim: Client text ties the rescue to a captive spider in Grexan's Camp.
evidence.source: locale:116034 'Free the spider held captive in Grexan's Camp.'

evidence.claim: Articles 924 (Buttercup), 927 and 928 (Flori) describe the same story: same camp, same Briarwood/Thorny Forest route, same hill-and-tunnel approach, same captured pet spider. This points to one storyline under two NPC names (likely a Spanish-localized or re-titled copy), but no dated source names both.
Flori Telarañas is a mage whose pet spider is captured by a troll at Grexan's Camp, and she asks players to rescue it.

open: Dates: articles 924, 927, 928 and 98 carry no year or month in the pack or this lookup, so occurrences is empty and the live window is unknown.

live = unsure: article 928 is titled 'Free Realms - What is New?', which hints at a live announcement, but there is no date. Locale 390727 ('not_live? no; see note') is unresolved and could indicate a pre-launch preview. Treat as unscheduled.

Alias/identity: Flori Telarañas and Buttercup Webbywand share the same story and route. The merge is likely but not confirmed; no dated source names both. Keep them as aliases only after a dated source links them. Flori appears only in Spanish articles 927 and 928.
Quest title 'Eight-Legged Friend' (locale:390870) and its objective/dialog IDs came from the earlier pass; the ID lookup failed in this pass, so re-verify before wiring.

'Train A Spider' (locale:390662) is dropped from quests: its only link is the rescue objective (locale:390663), and its sub-objectives point to the General Grexan spider-training battle (locale:5667 'Defeat General Grexan before the trolls become unstoppable!' and locale:18948 'Defeat General Grexan.'). That battle is a separate content line and is not counted here.
Items: locale:390551 (item named 'Buttercup Webbywand') is not tied to this event by any source, so it is excluded. Spider Sprayer and Spider-Etched Gravestone are unrelated.
Rewards: no source found for any reward.
recurring stays null. 'Each time she explores' is in-story flavour, not a schedule; only one undated storyline is known.

Zones: Briarwood and Grexan's Camp are supported by the wiki category and article 924; Thorny Forest is only the teleport route in article 927. Whether Grexan's Camp is its own zone is not established.
wiki_category_members and quest_answers_mentioning_it were empty in the pack. Do not wire this into the calendar until a dated source is found.
