evidence.claim: Smedley's keynote at the ION Games Conference 2008 discussed Free Realms and The Agency, in May 2008, before launch. This is a real-world industry conference talk, not an in-game event.
The May 2008 keynote was covered in a Ten Ton Hammer article that says Smedley discussed Free Realms among other topics.
Pre-launch interview after the ION keynote previews Free Realms as a title for younger players, with a parent-funded wallet and anti-farming approach. These are plans, not a live event.
A May 2008 pre-launch interview at the ION Game Conference covers Free Realms; the only design detail is a planned economy with no farming.
No client, wiki or quest source ties any item, NPC, zone or quest to this conference in lookup results.
evidence.source: lookup: 'ION Games Conference' and 'ION Smedley Agency Free Realms' across client,wiki,articles,video; locale 'ION|Games Conference' returned no matches

open: The pack is wrong to treat this as a Free Realms live event. 'ION Games Conference 2008' is a real-world industry conference where SOE's John Smedley gave a May 2008 keynote that touched on Free Realms. It is not an in-game holiday, theme, webcast, contest or promotion. Recommend excluding it from the events calendar or moving it to a Research or history note.

Kind is set to 'other' and live to 'no' because the only sources describe a pre-launch talk and a pre-launch interview, which are plans and not a live event. No in-game occurrence exists in the evidence.

Occurrences are empty. The only dated item is the May 2008 conference keynote (article 34035 dated 2008-05-22). It is a single conference appearance, not a recurring or in-game occurrence, so no recurrence is claimed.
The keynote video (article 34035) is not in the captured text. Its content about Free Realms is unknown, so no design details are claimed.
Aliases could include 'ION 2008' and 'ION Game Conference' (article 33642 uses the singular form). The pack name may also be merged with other ION or SOE talks; the evidence does not show that.
No zones, NPCs, quests, activities, items or rewards are tied to this event by any source. The lookup found no client or wiki matches.

evidence.claim: The only article is a freerealms.com news post announcing the latest Free Realms television ad, "Super Ego", viewable on the site. It is a promotional ad post, not a game event, and gives no gameplay, quest, item or event details.

The post has no exact date. The only date text is the relative label "Posted 1 month, 3 weeks ago" against the 2009-07-14 capture. Any month estimate is derived from that label, not stated by the article, so no occurrence is recorded.

Wiki page Chatty lists a Super Ego commercial among its Appearances, alongside the other Free Realms TV commercials and trailer. The FTS index shows it as "Free Realms [Super] [Ego] Commercial"; the brackets are match marking, so the exact unbracketed title is not confirmed by the source text.
Client lookup finds no in-game items, NPCs or quests named for Super Ego.

Quest "Meet and Greet" (locale:429030) is a Camp Chatty counselor quest. Its objective locale:429046 reads "Meet the camp counselors of Camp Chatty." It is not tied to the Super Ego ad by any source, despite the shared phrase in the wiki Chatty Appearances entry for Quest:Meet and Greet. Not counted as an event quest.

open: Pack merges an ad with an event: "Super Ego" is a TV commercial promotion, not a live event. live is "no" because the sources show no in-game activity. A reviewer may decide the ad counts as a promotion, but there is nothing to run.

Exact date unknown. The article gives only the relative label "Posted 1 month, 3 weeks ago" against the 2009-07-14 capture. An exact date needs another source, such as an archived copy with a dated post or a Ten Ton Hammer article. occurrences is empty for that reason.

Aliases: the pack title is "Super Ego TV Spot". The wiki Appearances entry for the same ad is listed as a Super Ego commercial, but its exact unbracketed title is not confirmed by the source text. The pack name may not match other archive titles.
Chatty wiki page lists the commercial as an appearance. This ties the ad to the Chatty mascot, but no source says Chatty is an NPC of this event, so npcs is empty.

Quest "Meet and Greet" (locale:429030, not "Camp Chatty Meet and Greet") is a separate counselor quest. Objective ids locale:429046, 429047, 429049, 429051 and 429053 exist. locale:429048, 429050 and 429052 return DOES NOT EXIST, so no range is cited. The shared name is a possible alias trap, and quests is empty.
No items, prices, zones, activities or rewards are sourced. Items and rewards are empty, not guessed.
Kind is "other" rather than "promotion". This is an advertisement with no reward or gameplay, so "promotion" would overstate it.

evidence.claim: The evidence pack's only event fact is SOE Official Podcast #59 (an SOE-wide podcast), which included an interview with Free Realms Community Manager Jason "Pex" Ryan about Free Realms. This is a podcast episode, not an in-game Free Realms event.
The article gives no game mechanics, quest, item, price, or activity details, and it was posted before the April 2009 launch, so it describes a plan, not a live event.
The pack's release date of April 28, 2009 comes from sidebar template data on the article page, not from article text, so it is not used.

SOE podcasts are a recurring series (#33 in April 2008, #39 July 2008, #59 April 2009, #61, #68, #81 March 2010, #83), but Free Realms is only one topic in some episodes, and this does not make Podcast #59 a recurring Free Realms event.
A later podcast-news post (2009-05-13) lists a 'Free Realms - Launches!' segment, so the launch announcement came after podcast #59. This pack does not establish the launch date.
Jason "Pex" Ryan is the Free Realms community manager and in-game Ambassador [Pex]. He is an NPC, but the sources do not tie him to Podcast #59 as an in-game event, so he is not listed under npcs.

open: The evidence pack is mislabelled. It names an SOE-wide podcast episode (SOE Official Podcast #59), not a Free Realms live event. The 'event' is a broadcast with one Free Realms segment, so the pack's framing does not match the events calendar's purpose. Recommend dropping this pack or re-scoping it to a real in-game event.

No occurrence is recorded as a live Free Realms event. The only date (2009-04-13) is a pre-launch preview post, which describes a plan, so occurrences is empty and live is 'no'. If the episode aired on or around 2009-04-13, that is a podcast air date, not a game event.
kind 'other' is used because no enum value fits an SOE podcast episode. 'webcast' was considered but the source calls it a podcast, not a webcast.
No zones, quests, activities, items, or rewards are supported by any source. The pack's quest_answers_mentioning_it and wiki_category_members are both empty.

Aliases are only the pack's own names: 'SOE Official Podcast #59', 'SOE Podcast #59', 'Podcast #59'. The pack may have merged this with another SOE podcast; the lookup shows a different SOE podcast (#81, 2010-03-18, St. Patty's Cast) used the same numbering series.

lookup for 'Podcast' and 'Pex' returned matches (including the Podcast #59 fact, the 'Ambassadors' wiki page and Day of the Duel / Demo Derby articles) but none tie a Free Realms in-game event to podcast #59. The Day of the Duel and Demo Derby items are separate events, not part of this pack.
The launch date is unresolved. The 2009-05-13 article shows the launch was announced after podcast #59, but no source here fixes the launch day.

The index lists 'Obama Promotion Days' alongside vbPlaza gift and collectible releases, an Easter Egg series and a Hershey Kiss gift set. The page does not tie the promotion to any of these.
Lookup of 'Obama' returns only the forum index, and locale 'Obama' has no matches. The pack's wiki category and quest answers are empty.
evidence.source: quest_cli lookup 'Obama'; quest_cli locale 'Obama' (no matches); pack wiki_category_members and quest_answers_mentioning_it

evidence.claim: The lookup for 'Promotion Day' returns other SOE and Free Realms promotions (Leap Day 2012 Wally promo, SOE 12 Days of Holidays, Summer Sizzle, Presidents' Day, one-day Double Station Cash). None names Obama, so none is tied to this event.
evidence.source: quest_cli lookup 'Promotion Day' (articles: freerealms.com article IDs 2523, 2457, 2112, 2037, 2186, 2119, 1885)

open: Canonical title: sources show plain 'Obama Promotion Day #N' (and 'Obama Promotion Days' in the index summary). The bracketed forms in the first critique were search highlighting, not title text. Aliases kept to these two. Confirm against the thread pages before treating them as one event.
Kind is unknown. The name says 'Promotion', but no source says what was promoted, so kind 'promotion' is a name-based guess. The earlier 'promotion' label stays a guess.

Live status is unsure. Threads Day #2 to #4 were posted 2009-01-21 to 2009-01-24, which suggests the event ran. Day #1 is not in the pack or the lookup. The forum index does not confirm in-game activity, so live is 'unsure', not 'yes'.
Occurrences: one only (January 2009, Day #2 to #4 seen). Recurrence is not evidenced, so recurring is null.
Pack date is null. The date range comes from the lookup fact text, not the pack. Pull the full thread pages to confirm.
No zones, NPCs, quests, activities, items or rewards are sourced. The pack has no client, wiki or quest tie to the event.
Possible merge or alias: the index also lists other 'Obama Promotion Days' entries and vbPlaza promotions. The index does not say they are the same event. Not confirmed.
Next step to resolve: fetch the thread pages for Day #1 to #4, or check archived Ten Ton Hammer or official-site news for January 2009 that names the promotion.

evidence.claim: Senior Producer Andy Sites discussed planned summer 2009 additions: racing, demolition derby, soccer and housing. The June 2009 E3 interview describes plans, not shipped content.
The June 2009 interview was posted after the April 2009 launch and reports 2 million players. The plan is a post-launch plan, not a pre-launch preview.
The same interview blurb says a new area was planned for fall 2009. This is a plan only, and the article does not name the area.
Racing, soccer, housing and demolition derby were announced as coming to Free Realms over summer 2009. This is a teaser, so it confirms the plan only.
Stickers for racing and demolition derby pilots were added to the store so players can decorate their car. No date is given in the lookup output, so this is undated.
A client string names a scheduled community event called Demolition Derby. The string has no date, so it does not establish when it ran or whether it belongs to the summer 2009 plan.

The fan forum's Racing and Demolition Derby subforum was captured 2009-05-26, before the June interview. A player thread there asked whether there were quests for racing or derby jobs, last posted 05-24-2009. This shows kart racing and derby discussion was active before the summer plan. It is context only and sets no occurrence date.
Demolition Derby is a live minigame and job (Demolition Derby Driver) in later articles, which is not tied to a summer 2009 event.
Soccer became a job and a 3D minigame in the Goal Time update, announced October 5, 2009. That is a later release, not a summer 2009 event.
A soccer community event ran July 8-9, 2010 on Server 1, during the Summer Camp 'Semana Deportiva' theme. This is a separate 2010 live event, not part of the summer 2009 plan.
The Seaside Summer Splash holiday event began July 2, 2009. It is a different event from the planned content, and the pack's name may merge the two.

open: Event object: name "Summer 2009 content plans (racing, demolition derby, soccer, housing)", kind "other", live "no". The pack describes a post-launch plan from a June 2009 E3 interview (tentonhammer node/69471, 2009-06-10), posted after the April 2009 launch. No source shows a live occurrence, so occurrences, recurring, zones, npcs, quests, activities and rewards are all empty.

Possible match not resolved: the Speedway Thunder update (articleId=169 and 170) added kart and Demolition Derby quests, a racetrack and new karts. articleId=170 says about 40 quests for the Kart Driver and Derby Driver jobs. The lookup output shows no date for either article. Tentonhammer node/71823 showed Sandstorm and Thunder Speedways as upcoming with July 2009 images. The release date is unknown, so the update cannot be placed in summer 2009 and is not attributed to this pack. It may deserve its own pack, with the article date checked first.
Item source correction: the decal article is articleId=199 in the lookup output. The critique cited articleId=197, which did not appear in any lookup result, so it is not used.

Pack name merges planned content with the Seaside Summer Splash (articleId=137, started July 2, 2009). Splash is a separate live holiday event with its own items (Star Shot Candle via wiki, Sparkler Bundle via articleId=136). It should get its own pack if Bryce wants it in the calendar.

open: Event name and aliases: the only name in the pack is ConnecDING, and the article calls it 'effectively' that name. The article's phrase 'social networking reward promotion' is an alias for the same event. Another name may exist in a source not in the archive here.

The one article (2009-12-12) gives the window in past tense in the pack's fact, but its quoted text is future tense ('will be offering players a chance to earn some prizes'; 'will be able to claim'). Activities are social-media actions only (following the Twitter and Facebook pages, and reaching goals). The article gives no in-game activity, so this is not gameplay.

Critique fixes: (1) The Station Cash claim is kept with the article as the source, because the archive lookup returns the same article saying each goal gave a Station Cash prize. wiki_page.title: Festival of Hearts
wiki_page.text:
thumb|300px
The Festival of Hearts is an annual Valentine's Day-themed event held from February through March in Merry Vale. Stone Heart and the Heart Breakers are out to ruin love in Merry Vale; it is up to the players to stop them.

History
Festival of Hearts celebrates an ancient tale of love between Rylan and Arianna. These two young pixies met long ago in what would later become Merry Vale, but were separated by magic.

At the heart of the festival is a special flower planted by the couple before they were forced apart that still blooms today. It stands out from the rest of the sunflowers in Merry Vale because of its red, pink, and magenta colors.

Every year, the fairies of Merry Vale celebrate the magic the flower contains: love, friendship, and kindness. This is a time of joy and laughter that draws visitors from all over Free Realms.

 Festival Story 
The story of the Festival of Hearts begins before the game. A young pixie woman by the name of Arianna meets a pixie man by the name of Rylan, and they fell in love at first sight. They planted a flower in MerryVale. Each day they met, the flower grew bigger from the love they shared, eventually becoming what we know today as the Heart Flower. After 13 days, Arianna wasn’t able to meet due to her parents, but they promised to reunite later, but later never came. When Arianna returned to their flower an unmentioned time later, Rylan was nowhere to be found. Arianna returned to their flower one day, waiting for Rylan to return, and after waiting for hours, she decided to take a nap on the banks of the lake surrounding MerryVale, falling into a deep slumber. 

Years later, a festival was formed to celebrate the love those two had for each other. This festival is the Festival of Hearts, but unfortunately for the festi

wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

wiki_page.title: Super Spooktacular
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px

The Super Spooktacular is an annual event during the month of October in celebration of Halloween. The event features many objectives such as: stopping the Pumpkin Prince, Trick-or-Treat, ghost hunting, etc.

Questline
Starting in Sanctuary
Since Halloween Harry is used in so many of these quests, he now has his own quick-click transport icon on the game Atlas during the event!

 Candy Gram from Halloween Harry
 A Formal Report from Halloween Harry
 A Trip to the Swamp from Greyli Dustywings in Queensfields
 Spectral Spectacles from Greyli Dustywings 
 A Ghostly Discovery from Lucinda in Blackspore Swamp 
 Guardians of the Tomb from Lord William IV in Blackspore Swamp 
 Sealed with a Signet from Lord William IV 
 The Pumpkin Prince from Lucinda 

 Spooky Hide 'n Seek from Tabitha in Pixiewood Hills (must complete the above series first, repeatable once per day)
 Ghostly Games from Hector in Pixiewood Hills (must complete the above series first, repeatable once per day)

 The Great Scare from Ghost Hunter in Pixiewood Hills

 Delicious Goo'd Candy from Halloween Harry (repeatable whenever you have 15 Ectoplasmic Goo in your inventory)

 Going Batty from Vladimir in Pixiewood Hills (repeatable once per day)

evidence.claim: Event ran Friday August 7, 2009, 2pm to 4pm Pacific, on all servers at the Wildwood Speedway Demolition Derby track (quote: 'Today, August 7th, 2009, from 2pm to 4pm Pacific time, the Community Team challenges everyone').
Event was run by the Community Team; players learned to drive karts from Mad Jack and joined demolition derby races.
Players reached the Demo Derby Lobby by clicking the demo derby icon at the turnstiles and choosing the Demo Derby Lobby to start or join races.

Wildwood Speedway is a kart racing location just south of the Crossroads, containing a Demolition Derby track. The same location is stated in article 101 ('located south of the Crossroads warpstone, one of four speedways offering kart racing and demolition derby').
The wiki Community Events page lists Wildwood Demolition Day as an event where players fought in the Demolition Derby Driver job at the Wildwood Speedway, with games hosted by Ambassador Pex.
Article 188 gives no reward, price or rule detail beyond the schedule, lobby access and the Mad Jack driving lesson.

open: Event object: name 'Wildwood Demolition Day'; aliases from article title 'Community Event: Wildwood Demolition Day'. Only one dated occurrence (2009-08-07) is sourced, so recurring is null.

Possible sibling, not merged: article 1910 announces a 'Demolition Day' at Thunder Falls Speedway, Server 1, on Nov 18, 2010 (US/LatAm 3pm PT) and Nov 19, 2010 (UK/Europe 9am PT). Different track and date. It may be the same community series, but no source says so, so it is not counted here. Locales 6674 and 6678 point to Thunder Falls with SERVER 1, so they fit the 2010 event, not Wildwood.

Ambassador Pex, named as host, comes only from the wiki Community Events page; no article in the pack names him for this event. The wiki category members list in the pack is empty, so this is an unverified-by-article host claim.

No quests, items, prices or rewards are tied to this event by any source. Locale 395095 ('Come in 1st place during the demolition derby', Wildwood Demo Derby Base) is an unlinked quest objective. Locales 3383 and 406402 ('Demolition Derby') are generic strings with no event link.
The Wildwood Speedway kart racing events (articles 2045, 1700, 101, 2049 'Bois Sauvage' French article) are a different community event type (racing) and are not included.
Video frames (V45-eAlBzn0 'Be the dominant car in the Wildwood Demolition Derby!') show the minigame but carry no date, so they are not dated evidence for the event.
Kart racing is a separate activity from the derby; the 'Demolition Derby Driver' job is the player-job layer, not the event.

Critique fix applied: the location claim now cites article 188 (which does state 'just south of Crossroads, containing a Demolition Derby track') and article 101 (which states it explicitly). Articles 2045 and 1700 also place the Speedway south of the Crossroads Warpstone but describe racing events, so they are not cited for the derby.

Alias gap or merge: SOE Podcast 83 (tentonhammer node 83296) also covers the first birthday, and Podcast 81 is a different episode. Decide whether 83 and 84 are one event or two before the calendar stores either.
Recurring is null: SOE Podcast is a numbered series, but the pack has no article that says this episode recurs on a schedule, and the series is not Free Realms-specific.
Podcast content is not described in any source. The activities field only says the episode was listened to or watched; no details of what was discussed are sourced.

occurrences.when: Jan 15-18, 2010 (until 11:59pm PST on Jan 18)

activities: Bought Zando in the Free Realms Station Marketplace with 500 Station Cash during Jan 15-18, 2010 (source: http://www.tentonhammer.com:80/node/79740). SOE contributed $10 per Zando purchase to Haiti relief. The recipient is named 'Haiti relief' in 79393 and 870, 'American Red Cross Haiti Relief' in 79740 and the Zando wiki page, and 'Haiti Relief and Development Effort' in locale:4761. Likely the same drive, not confirmed as one recipient.

items.name: Zando
items.source: http://www.tentonhammer.com:80/node/79740 (spiked T-Rex pet, Haiti Relief item, 500 SC, Jan 15-18 2010); locale:4760-4761; wiki page Zando; wiki page Pets

evidence.claim: The Free Realms Station Marketplace promotion ran Jan 15-18, 2010 (until 11:59pm PST on Jan 18). Players could redeem 500 Station Cash toward drive items, and SOE contributed $10 per redemption.

The $10 per-purchase match applied to Free Realms Station Marketplace purchases during the drive. The $25,000 cap belongs to the whole SOE drive across EverQuest, EverQuest II and Free Realms, not to Free Realms alone. The Free Realms share of the cap is not stated.

Zando, a spiked T-Rex pet, was the Haiti Relief item sold in the Free Realms Marketplace Jan 15-18, 2010 for 500 Station Cash. SOE donated $10 per sale, with a maximum donation of $25,000 stated for the drive.
Client string for Zando (locale:4761) names the Haiti Relief and Development Effort and the 1/15/10 to 1/18/10 window, and carries a FLAG not_live tag.
Zando wiki page: introduced as a Haiti Relief item; SOE donated $10 per purchase to American Red Cross Haiti Relief.
Pets wiki page: Zando is no longer available; sales benefited Haiti Earthquake Relief.
Only one promotion window is documented, and no source says it recurs, so it is treated as a single promotion.

open: The pack says the drive covered Free Realms items, plural. Article 870 and 79393 say 'these items' and 'items', but only Zando is named in any source. Other Free Realms drive items are unconfirmed.

The $25,000 cap and the $10 per-purchase match are stated for the whole SOE drive across EverQuest, EverQuest II and Free Realms (79393). The Free Realms share of the cap is not separately stated. The pack's merged summary treats the drive as one Free Realms event, which needs a check.

Donation recipient differs by source: 'Haiti relief' (79393, 870), 'American Red Cross Haiti Relief' (79740 and the Zando wiki page), 'Haiti Relief and Development Effort' (locale:4761). Likely the same drive, unverified.
Article 79740 has no date in the pack. Its window is given only as January 15-18, 2010, so it is not used as a dated source.
Locale:4761 carries FLAG not_live, in tension with live = yes. The articles (2010-01-17 and the 870 post) support a live run, so the flag is treated as a client-copy tag. Needs a human check.
The pack merges the SOE-wide charity drive (EverQuest, EverQuest II, Free Realms) with the Free Realms part. Only the Free Realms part belongs to this event record.
No zones, NPCs, quests or rewards are tied to this event by any source. The pack's quest answers list is empty.

The 2010-01-20 capture date and the 'Free Realms - What is New?' page title for article 870 were dropped. The pack does not confirm them, and the critique could not confirm them. The Jan 15-18 window and 11:59pm PST cutoff stay attributed to article 870.
Articles 2922 and 2899 (Wiki Wednesday) mention contribution only in a different sense; they are not part of this event.

evidence.claim: Event is the SOE social networking promotion called ConnecDING. Players who followed Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest 2 on Twitter or Facebook could earn in-game prizes when SOE reached social networking goals.

The article is dated 2009-12-12 and is written in future tense ('SOE will be offering', 'players will be able to claim'). The Dec 10, 2009 to Feb 10, 2010 window is therefore a planned period announced in advance, not a confirmed live run.

The article states a window of December 10, 2009 through February 10, 2010. The pack's fact statement 'ran from' is a past-tense extraction that the article's future-tense announcement does not support.

Currency is Station Cash. Each time SOE reached a Facebook or Twitter goal, players could claim a Station Cash prize (article wording: 'players will be able to claim a Station Cash prize'). This is a planned reward, and no prize amount is given.
SOE created Twitter and Facebook pages for Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest 2 in December 2009. The article gives no exact creation date.
The article names no quest, item, zone, NPC or named prize for Free Realms. The only in-game reward it names is a Station Cash prize.

Lookup for ConnecDING across client, wiki, articles and video returns only this article. No wiki page, client string or video frame ties to the promotion, so there is no second source to confirm it ran.
The freerealms.com whatIsParty.vm page is a different feature (the in-game social networking page) and is excluded.
A separate Station Cash bonus promotion ran Nov 23 to Nov 29, 2009 (Thanksgiving week, 25% bonus on retail cards). It is a distinct event and is not merged with ConnecDING.

open: Live is 'unsure'. The pack's era tag 'live' is not supported. It rests only on the 2009-12-12 announcement, whose body uses future tense. A pre-launch announcement is a plan, not proof of a live event. The window is recorded as a planned period, so occurrences stay empty.
Occurrences are empty. The Dec 10, 2009 to Feb 10, 2010 window becomes an occurrence only when a second source confirms it ran.
recurring is null. Only one planned window is sourced, and no source says it recurs.

Station Cash is sourced (critique fix applied). Currency is 'station_cash' and the prize is a reward, not a named item, so items is empty. Prize amounts and the number of goals are not given anywhere in the pack.

Zones, NPCs, quests and client activities are not sourced. The locale search for 'connec' and 'social' finds no ConnecDING string in the client. Video lookup for ConnecDING returned no frames. wiki_category_members and quest_answers_mentioning_it are empty.

wireable is false, which is not a field in this format. The calendar should not schedule this event yet. Blockers: (1) no second source confirms the window ran, (2) no prize list or amounts are sourced, (3) no items, quests or activities are sourced to schedule.

The Station Cash bonus at node/77125 is a separate event. Its dates are Nov 23 to Nov 29, 2009 in TTH, but freerealms.com article 629 gives Nov 23 10am PST to Nov 30 10pm PST, so the end date conflicts across sources. Record it separately, do not merge it with ConnecDING, and resolve the end date before wiring it.

The pack may merge two events under one name. 'ConnecDING promotion period' and 'social networking reward promotion' are the same article's wording, so no merge is apparent. The alias 'SOE social networking promotion' is descriptive, not a separate event.
The ids check was not run because no quest or item ids were supplied.

evidence.claim: The 5M Party Wheel event was a limited-time event celebrating the 5,000,000th registered Free Realms player.
Players had to log in during the event window of September 16, 2009 to September 23, 2009.
Players could log in daily to spin the Party Wheel.
The special virtual rewards from the 5M event were one Party Crate, one Silly String can, three Party Poppers, and one Grab Bag.
Client item name 'Party Crate' exists (locale:407352), matching the article's reward name by exact name only; the client does not tie it to the 5M event.
Client item names 'Blue Silly String Can' (locale:407382) and 'Silly String - Blue' (locale:407384) exist; the article does not give a colour, so the exact can is unconfirmed.
Client item names for Party Popper exist in base and coloured variants (locale:407420, 407460-407464); the article does not name a colour, so the exact popper is unconfirmed.
Client item name 'Grab Bag' exists (locale:141315) alongside Small, Medium and Large Grab Bag (locale:43-45); the article does not say which bag was given.

open: Post date 2009-09-16 is inferred, not stated: the article summary says it was inferred from the capture date and the relative 'posted 6 days, 3 hours ago' stamp. The window dates (Sept 16-23, 2009) are stated in the article text, so the year and days are sourced.
Only one article (articleId=316) supports the event. No second article, forum post, or video frame was found for the wheel, so occurrence count and live confirmation rest on one source.
Recurring is null: one occurrence only, and no source says it recurs.
Kind is set to 'promotion'; 'community' (a milestone celebration) is also defensible.

5M GM Crate (locale:407348, 407350, 407351) is named with the 5M event in client text, but it is an internal GM spawn item (locale:407351 is FLAGged dev_note 'Used by GMs for 5M player event'). It is left out of items and needs a decision on whether GM-only items count.

locale:407385 ('Used for 5M item: Silly String Can') and locale:407421 ('Used for 5M item: Party Popper') are FLAGged (dev_note; placeholder sample text). They are not used as membership evidence; the article is the tie for those items.

Name collision risk for 'Party Crate': the Birthday Party Crate (locale:5664, wiki 'Birthday Crates', Birthday Bash, Marketplace-sold, first-anniversary item) is a different item. Nothing ties it to the 5M event, so it is excluded. Locale 'Party Crate' (407352) has a separate quest_objective (407775) and an encounter-312 label (407354) that are also unrelated.
No prices, currencies or purchase terms appear in any source; price and currency are null (reward items).

wiki_page.title: Birthday Bash
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Birthday Bash is an annual event held throughout the month of April in celebration of launch day for Free Realms on April 29th, 2009. The event features party items, and Cakenstein, along with his minions out to take the Birthday Cake, it is up to the players to stop them.

Questline
The quests for this event are centered in Sanctuary, but send you all around Sacred Grove. Speak with Camellia to get things started.

 A Piece of Cake from Camellia in Sanctuary  - repeatable once per day
 Undelivered Confections from Camellia
 Mysteriously Cakey Remains from Chef Jarvie in Merry Vale
 Cakey Clue from Mayor McFairy in Merry Vale
 To Bake a Pretty Cake from Glerga in the Robgoblin Camp 
 Perfecting the Batter from Glerga 
 All Cakensteins Must Die from Glerga 
 Forgivable Matter from Glerga 

 Birthday Cake Bake-Off from Camellia
 Helping the Local Chef - repeatable once per day with your chosen chef
 Birthday Invitation from Flitter in Sanctuary - repeatable once per day
 Bundles of Balloons from Quills in Sanctuary - repeatable once per day
 Cakey Madness from General Glowlight in Sanctuary - repeatable once per day
 Downing Cakenstein from Commander Kiggle in Sanctuary - continuously repeatable
 Feeding the Crowd from Helga Humbleloaf in Pixiewood Hills - repeatable once per day
 Mystery Meat Mystery from Sal Monella in Blackspore Swamp - once per character (so if done in a previous year, it will not be offered again)

Where's the Party?
All of the major towns in Sacred Grove each have their own special party location.

 Sanctuary - On the island south of the Royal Palace
 Merry Vale - At the cooking table
 Seaside - At the Ocean Treasures Cafe
 Briarwood - At Chugilda's camp kitchen in Nettleseed
 Snowhill - Near the cooking table and the skating pond

evidence.claim: Free Realms passed 12 million registered users by late June 2010, shortly after the virtual Summer Camp release on June 7, 2010 (article dated 2010-06-26).

Events were planned to celebrate the 12 million user milestone and the upcoming Fourth of July holiday, but the article describes no events and gives no dates or contents. This is a plan, not a confirmed live event.

A separate Fourth of July weekend promotion ran in July 2010: prepaid Station Cash retail cards redeemed in the window returned double value, and a free trial membership weekend was offered. No source ties this promotion to the 12 million milestone.
Summer Camp was a 13-week community event season starting the week of its announcement in summer 2010. It is a different event from this milestone celebration and is not included here.

open: The pack's only source (tentonhammer node/86237, 2010-06-26) says events were planned but gives no contents, dates or proof they ran. Live status is unsure, and no occurrence can be confirmed from sources. The milestone celebration may never have run as a separate event.

The pack title likely merges two events: the 12 million milestone celebration and the July 4 2010 weekend promotion (freerealms.com articleId=1590). Keep them as separate entries unless a source ties them together.
The July 4 promotion has only an archived summary here. Its exact dates, items and rewards need the full article or a second source before it can be recorded as an event.

Wiki page 'Uncle Sam Jacket' says it is available during the Fourth of July. That ties it to the July 4 holiday, not to the 12 million celebration, so it is not listed as an item here. It is a candidate item for the July 4 event.

Summer Camp (community season, June 2010) is a separate event from this pack's entry. The pack did not name it, but it is the same weeks as the milestone article and may be the event people remember under this name.

Client lookups for '12 million' and 'Fourth of July' returned no client text tied to this event. Quest and NPC fields are empty because no quest answer or client locale ties them to this milestone event.

The application window, deadline and submission channel are not in the pack. Only the June 2010 winner announcement is dated.

Live status is 'no': this is a real-world contest that had concluded by 2010-06-08, not an in-game live event. It should not go on the in-game calendar as a runnable event.

The FTS query 'G.I.R.L.' failed on the period character (fts5 syntax error), so the client, wiki and video searches for it were not run. The retry used the scholarship and concept-art terms. A query with the period stripped (for example GIRL or Gamers in Real Life) would close this gap.

open: Critique fix 1 (occurrences): the 2009 entry is removed from this event. It is a separate event: 'Mother's Day roses redeem code', May 2009, source http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=80. The lead should record it as its own events-calendar row. No link to this event is made. Only sourced occurrence here: 2010-05-06 (article 1370).

Critique fix 2 (items): the bouquet stays as an item because article 1370 ties it to the update. Price and currency are null. The 44 price appears only in undated video frames 00742 (station_cash) and 00778 (coins). The two frames also disagree on currency, and the Boombox prices differ, so they may come from different stores. Price is not sourced.

Critique fix 3 (kind): 'holiday' is changed to 'update', the enum value that fits article 1370 ('What is New?' update page). The Mother's Day name is the only holiday link and no holiday page is sourced.
Critique fix 4 (activities): 'bought from the Marketplace' is replaced with 'available in the Marketplace from May 6, 2010'. No purchase is sourced.
Variant count: article 1370 says four variations. The client has one bouquet name (locale 3074). The four 44-price entries in frame 00778 may match but are not confirmed.

Mother's Day Sunflower (locale 756, 757) is excluded: article 1370 does not list it and the client name alone does not tie it to May 2010. Frames 00742 and 00778 show it at 224 (station_cash and coins). Unresolved candidate only.

Recurring is null. Two sourced occurrences a year apart with the same name look annual, but the 2009 one is a different mechanism and item, so there is one sourced occurrence for this event. Keep null until a 2011+ source or item lineage is settled.

Live is 'unsure'. The start (2010-05-06) is sourced, the end is not, and the price and currency conflict. Wireable is not in the answer format. Critique response: wireable=false. A start-only placeholder with price null is possible only if the lead decides so. This answer does not make that call.
Quests 'Strange Bouquet' (locale 92094), 'Postman: Beautiful Bouquet' (locale 117017) and 'Beautiful Bouquet' are not tied to Mother's Day by any source, so they are not listed.
Alias check: article 80 calls its item a 'bouquet of roses' and its event a 'Mother's Day gift event'. These belong to the 2009 event and are not added as aliases here.
Zones, NPCs, quests and rewards are not sourced for this event. The wiki category is empty and the quest-answer list is empty in the pack.

The Template:News trade-again line is undated and sits beside a Game Update 122 entry dated 12/03/2013. It does not show that the line belongs to that entry, so the trade status of the 2010 bouquets is unknown.

evidence.claim: PS3 Free Realms players could not play in the week before April 25, 2011 because of a PlayStation Network outage (the outage stopped PS3 players of Free Realms and DC Universe Online).
As of April 28, 2011, PS3 players of Free Realms had been unable to access the game for a week because of the PSN outage. Sony Online Entertainment's systems are separate from PSN.
Per SOE's statement, services were interrupted on April 21, 2011 by an external intrusion, and PSN was being rebuilt, so PS3 connections stayed down with no set return date.
This is a platform outage (PSN), not a scheduled Free Realms live event. No event items, NPCs, quests, zones, rewards or activities are tied to it in any source in the pack.

open: Not a Free Realms live event. It is a PlayStation Network outage that blocked PS3 play in April 2011. The pack title and kind do not match an events calendar entry. Recommend the calendar drop it or log it as an incident, not an event.
Pack title is 'PSN outage affecting Free Realms (PS3)'. No merge or alias problem found, but the pack holds no event content to build an entry from.
End date of the outage is not in the pack. Only the start (April 21, 2011, per SOE statement) and status as of April 25 and April 28, 2011 are sourced. Restoration date unknown.
Start date April 21, 2011 comes from the article's report of SOE's statement, and the article is secondary. Free Realms is only a secondary subject in these articles.
Kind is 'other' (outage) and live is 'no' because no scheduled event ran. Confidence is moderate because the facts are well sourced but the object is not an event.
Zones, NPCs, quests, activities, items and rewards are empty. Lookup of the wiki and client found no event content, and the pack lists no wiki category members or quest answers.
Two articles (97837 and 97926) both report on the outage. No other occurrences or recurrence found.

open: Season span: the sourced window is June 2010 (opening, June 4 update) to Sept 2-3 2010 (Pet Parade, last Summer Camp event). The 13-week figure from TenTonHammer node 85170 fits roughly June to early September, but it is a secondary report and was not reconciled against article dates for each week.

Exact in-game dates for Fashion Week, Sports Week, Crafting Week and Treasure Hunting Week are not stated in the sources reviewed. Only Fashion Week has an article date (2010-07-01). Do not schedule the weeks.
Sports Week's Snowhill soccer challenge and the Fashion Week Tue/Thu/Fri times (articleId=1593) were not re-verified, so they are not stated as facts.

Quest titles: 14 camp land quests and daily questlines are reported (node 85170), but their exact titles are not confirmed. Jojo objective text (locale 441711, 441715, 441719, 441832) ties Jojo to the Summer Camp place. No quest is tied to event dates. The Ninjato/Jintaka lines (locale 441723, 441727) name no Summer Camp location; excluding them from the event is an inference.
Adventure Week (articleId=1552) and Arts and Crafts (1624) were not verified in this pass and are left out.
Printable calendar (articleId=1661, 1737) and the daily JCC/TCG events are general server features, not Summer Camp items; excluded.

Items: no store prices or currency are sourced for any camp item. Specific housing and camp item names (tent, campfire, banner, totem) are not named in any source. Marshmallow (pet, one wiki line 'Only available during Summer Camp') is excluded as unconfirmed.
Name merge risk: 'Summer Camp' names both the 2010 community event season and the in-game camp place. The virtual camp release (June 7, 2010) is a separate milestone and not an alias.

aliases: Station Cash double day (Portuguese: Station Cash em Dobro)

occurrences.when: Saturday April 30, 2011 (one day). Brasilia window 04:00 Apr 30 to 03:59 May 1 (Brasilia time, from the Portuguese post).

activities: Earn double Station Cash on the promotion day (announced; the purchase channels that counted are not stated in any source)
rewards: Double Station Cash on the promotion day

evidence.claim: SOE announced a one-day double Station Cash day on Saturday April 30, 2011, across its games, as an apology/thank-you for players' patience after a recent service interruption. Announcement only.

The announcement is SOE's site-wide notice across its games. Free Realms is named in the same post only in the sentence about a repair plan for PS3 players of DC Universe Online and Free Realms. The phrase 'not Free Realms alone' is an extractor paraphrase, not article text, and is dropped.

The Ten Ton Hammer article dated 2011-04-29 says SOE offered a Double Station Cash event on Saturday for Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest II, after a PlayStation Network security breach caused a service interruption. This is the only source that names Free Realms as a Double Station Cash recipient.
The Brasilia-time window is 04:00 Apr 30 to 03:59 May 1 (08:00 to 07:59 Portugal time). The UTC equivalent 07:00 Apr 30 to 06:59 May 1 is derived arithmetic.
The same Ten Ton Hammer post says Free Realms also got double experience through Saturday. No start time is given. Not an item of this event.

open: Live status is 'unsure'. Every source is a pre-event announcement (2112, 2118, 2119, 2125, node/97967). No post-event source confirms the day ran as announced. Upgrade to 'yes' only with one.

Pack merge: the name covers several separate promotions and they are not occurrences of this event. These include the 2011 Europe card redemption Oct 7-10 (articleId=2294), Labor Day Sep 1-3 2012 (articleId=2754 German, 2763 Portuguese; the earlier 2758/2759 citations did not match the index), Walmart buy-and-redeem Oct 12-14 2012 (articleId=2790), US 7-Eleven card redemption (articleId=2806/2807, dates not in snippet), Best Buy card (articleId=2719; the wiki image Freerealmsnews4.jpg shows a Double Station Cash card for Aug 16-18 2013, which conflicts with the earlier 'Aug 17-19 2012' claim and needs rechecking), and a purchase-based double weekend (articleId=1970, ran until Dec 19, year unverified). The card-redemption IDs 1590, 346, 1186, 1974 and tentonhammer node/74525 are not classified. Spring Celebration (articleId=2893) has no year.
Regional start times: only the Brasilia window is established. North American and European start times are unknown.
The Free Realms double experience (node/97967) has no start time and an unclear duration. It is not an item.
No source says which purchases or card redemptions counted toward double Station Cash.
The earlier claim of a service interruption on April 21, 2011 (node/97837) was not verified and is left out. The cause named in node/97967 is a PlayStation Network security breach.
Items, NPCs, zones and quests are empty. No client, wiki or quest source ties any of them to this event. locale:510210 is not cited.
Recurrence: only one occurrence is supported and no article says it recurs, so recurring is null.
Wireable: false. The calendar can record only a date and a multiplier. It becomes wireable once a post-event source confirms the day ran, or once a regional window beyond Brasilia is added.

evidence.claim: Free Realms was announced to get double experience through Saturday, alongside EverQuest and EverQuest II. The source is future tense ('will enjoy double experience through Saturday'). Nothing here confirms the bonus ran.

A double experience bonus was announced for Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest II through Saturday. The article does not say the bonus applied service-wide, and it names no other scope. Scope is therefore unknown beyond those three games.
The pack's xp_multiplier value of 2 matches the article's word 'double'. Recorded as a pack value only, not as a schema field.
The article is titled 'SOE Offers Double Station Cash and Double Experience Event This Weekend'. The title supports the alias 'Double Experience Event'.

The same article announces a separate Double Station Cash event on Saturday for Free Realms, offered after a PlayStation Network security breach caused a service interruption. It is a different event and is not part of this answer.
Lookup across client, wiki, articles and video for 'double experience' returns only this one article. No second source confirms the bonus ran.
Locale search for double/xp/experience patterns returns no matches, so no locale source is cited for this event.

open: Pack fact era is wrong and must be fixed in n495.json (not edited here, read-only). Set era to 'announced' and the statement to 'announced to get double experience through Saturday'. The current 'live' era and 'received' wording overstate the source, which is future tense.

Pack merge: the pack title 'Double experience weekend' merges two events from one article. This answer covers only the double-XP announcement. The Double Station Cash compensation event (Saturday, after the PSN breach outage) needs its own pack, citing http://tentonhammer.com/node/97967.

Occurrence date fixed: the source gives 2011 and an announcement date of 2011-04-29. It says the bonus runs 'through Saturday' but does not name the day. The 2011-04-30 date is an inference and is dropped here. Pack should record 'announced 2011-04-29 for the weekend, through Saturday (day not stated)'. Nothing confirms it ran, so the event stays out of any schedule until a second source confirms it ran with dates.
Live status unsure: one 2011-04-29 news post, future tense, and no second source. Set live to yes only after a second source confirms it ran.

Scope unknown: the critique is right that 'service-wide' is not in the source. The article names Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest II and nothing else. The earlier 'service-wide' wording has been removed. The pack's xp_multiplier 2 is kept as a pack value only.

Modifier not activity: double XP is a 2x experience bonus, not an activity, zone, NPC, quest or item. The format has no modifier field, so activities, items and rewards stay empty. A modifier field would be needed in the schema.
Wireable not in format: the format has no wireable field. Treat the event as not schedulable (wireable false) until a second source confirms it ran with exact dates.
Aliases: the alias 'Double Experience Event' is supported only by the article title. The pack and article omit that EverQuest and EverQuest II also received the bonus.

Locale checks: locale:615 (President's Day TCG sale), locale:465 (CVS redemption promo) and locale:510210 (Best Buy SC cards) are unrelated and not cited. Locale search returns no string for this event.
Other lookups return unrelated events (Spring Celebration articleId 2893, a December weekend articleId 1970, European game-card promos and a Best Buy 2013 promo). None are this event.
The ids check was not run because n495 is a pack id, not a content id.
No items, NPCs, quests, zones, rewards or activities are tied to this event by any source. Recurring is null because there is one occurrence and no article says it recurs.

Critique item 2 (pre-launch vs live) fixed: 2066, 2068 and 2070 future-tense text is kept as announcement evidence with no date. Only the live-sale entries (2071 dated 2011-03-25, and 2068's past-tense 'were sold' line) feed the occurrence.

Recipient conflict unresolved: articles 2066, 2068, 2070, 2071 and 2076 name the American Red Cross; locale:434305 names the Japan Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Effort. A human should pick the recipient string for the record.
Recurring is null: only one year (2011) is sourced and no article says it recurs.

Items: only the Cherry Blossom Tree is named in the client (locale:434304). The articles say 'Cherry Blossom items' (plural) but no other item names are resolved. Moment of silence (locale:434534) is an undated client UI string with 'SERVER 1' and no sale tie. Listed here only as an unconfirmed related item, not as event evidence.
Zones, NPCs and quests: none found in the lookup results or the wiki. Left empty, not guessed.

Haiti relief (Zando, Jan 15-18 2010, articles/870 and tentonhammer node 79740) is a different event, not merged here.
The 2066 and 2070 posts also mention EverQuest and Clone Wars Adventures. The multi-game framing is only context; only the Free Realms lines are used.

evidence.claim: Community Team Ambassadors held a kart racing community event called the Wildwood Racing Challenge at the Wildwood Speedway, with a party held just outside the race course
The Wildwood Racing Challenge ran on Server 1 on Thursday 10 March 2011 at 3pm Pacific Time for U.S. and Latin America players

A second session ran on Server 1 on Friday 11 March 2011 at 9:00am Pacific Time for UK and Europe players. Article 2045 also prints 4:00pm GMT for this session, which is a source error: 9:00am PST on 11 March 2011 is 17:00 GMT, and PST applied until 13 March 2011

The French article 2049 gives the same two dates (jeudi 10 mars and vendredi 11 mars 2011) on Serveur 1 for the kart race at the Bois Sauvage circuit, south of the Crossroads teleport stone. Its 18:00 CET figure for Friday is also 17:00 GMT, so it has the same one-hour GMT error
Racers were told to wear a helmet, and non-racers could join an off-track party beside the race
The event dates are stated in the article text (10 and 11 March 2011). The pack's inferred-date note for article 2049 is out of date

open: Event and kind: the event is a community kart race; 'community' is the kind because the articles name Community Team Ambassadors as hosts. Live is 'yes' because the articles announce specific held sessions with dates and the pack holds no source that says they were cancelled, but neither article records that the sessions ran. Treat as likely live, not confirmed.

Merge problem: the pack name 'Wildwood Speedway' is the venue, not the event. Other Wildwood events are separate and are not counted here: Summer Camp Racing Week kart community event (article 1700, date not in pack), and a Demolition Derby community event on 7 Aug 2009, 2pm-4pm Pacific (article 188). The wiki's Wildwood Demolition Day with Ambassador Pex is also a separate event.

Alias: none recorded. 'Bois Sauvage kart race' was the author's label, not an event name in article 2049. The French article names only the Bois Sauvage circuit, the French name of the venue, so it is a venue name, not an alias.

Quest name match (moved out of evidence): the client holds a quest titled Wildwood Racing Challenge (locale:7142), and its NPC dialog reads Do you wanna go fast? Head to the Wildwood Speedway and drive against the best! (locale:7118). Both ids exist with that text, but no article links them to the March 2011 sessions, so they are a name match only and are not listed as event quests or as evidence.

Quests tied to the Kart Driver job: the pack lists ten quests that name the track: Kart Driver: Target Acquired (locale 3490), Even the Odds, Ready to Redline (locale 3494), Challenging T.R., You Want to Go Fast? (locale 3495), Exploder's League Sponsorship, Wildwood Sprint Challenge (locale 3319 and 3497), Wildwood Endurance Challenge (locale 3320 and 3504), Dominating at Wildwood (locale 3321 and 3509), and Guest of Honor. Ids 3490, 3494, 3495, 3497, 3504, 3509 and 3511 (SG Tour 400: Wildwood) were checked by ids and carry the names given. The other pack quests were not checked by id. No source ties any of these to the March 2011 event, so quests is empty. Article 170 says an update added 40 Kart Driver and Derby Driver quests, but the update's date is not in the pack, so it cannot be linked to this event.

Items: no source ties an item to this event, so items is empty. The helmet is an instruction, not a named item. Rewards: the article summary says nothing about rewards or race rules, so rewards is empty.
NPCs: the hosts are described only as Community Team Ambassadors or Free Realms ambassadors. No named NPC is tied to this event, so npcs is empty.

Recurring: not established. A weekly community kart format exists for other tracks (Thunder Falls, article 2009, dated 27 Jan 2011; Torrentrueno, article 2013, undated), but the pack has only one Wildwood Racing Challenge occurrence (two sessions on consecutive days in one week).

Time conflict in the sources: article 2045 gives 4pm GMT for 9am Pacific on 11 March 2011, and article 2049 gives 18:00 CET for the same session. Both equal 17:00 GMT, so both GMT figures are wrong. The Pacific times and Server 1 agree across both articles, so the occurrences use the Pacific times only.

Zone conflict in the wiki: the Speedways page places Wildwood in Sanctuary, while the Southern Wilds page lists Wildwood Speedway under Southern Wilds. The zone field gives the article's own location (south of the Crossroads teleport stone) and does not resolve this.

Pack summary of article 2049 says the date is inferred from the first event date. The article text states 10 and 11 March 2011 directly, so the inference note is outdated. The page header's relative age ('posted 2 months, 3 weeks ago') is not used.

The outage began with an external intrusion on April 21, 2011, and PS3 players could not play the week before April 25, 2011.

SOE said it was preparing a 'make good' compensation plan for the PS3 MMOs DC Universe Online and Free Realms. The article gives no Free Realms gameplay, quest or item details, so the plan is not confirmed as an event or as delivered.
A second article says SOE was working on the make-good plan, with details to be posted later on the Free Realms PS3 forums. The article gives no details of the plan itself.
A May 2011 article covers a second Sony intrusion and Sony's revised earnings forecast after the outage. Free Realms is mentioned only in passing and no Free Realms event is described.
The locale index has no Free Realms entries for an outage, compensation or make-good event. The only PSN hits are unrelated UI strings: 'PSN Wallet' (430733) and 'Add to PSN Friends' (432682).

open: The evidence pack names this 'PSN outage', which is a service disruption, not a live Free Realms event. The pack merges the outage with the make-good compensation plan, which may be a separate promotion. Whether that plan was ever delivered in game is not in the evidence.
No aliases beyond 'PSN outage' and 'PlayStation Network outage' were found. 'Make good plan' may be a separate compensation promotion; it needs its own pack before it gets a calendar entry.
Article 98028 was not read in full; the claim about it rests on the lookup summary and fact snippet.
No client, wiki, or quest source ties any item, NPC, zone, quest or reward to this outage or to any make-good compensation, so those fields are empty.
The pack's article dates are only partly confirmed. The 97926 date is 2011-04-28 and the 97837 date is stated only as 'April 2011' in the summary; the exact publication date was not confirmed.

Client search (locale regex and free text) finds no G.I.R.L. or scholarship strings. The only hits are unrelated 'girl' lines. The event has no in-game zones, NPCs, quests or activities in the client.

wiki_page.title: Snow Days
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Snow Days is an annual event during the months of December throughout January in celebration of the Winter Holidays. The event takes place in Snowhill where the The Gifting Tree gives presents to all of the residents of Snowhill. The evil snowman boss named the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen try to take all the presents for themselves, and Candi Ivy, who gives you quests, will up to stop the Abominable Snowman and his evil snowmen.

Questline
The Snow Days questline begins in Snowhill.

 The Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Present Problems from Candi Ivy
 Holiday Cheer from Candi Ivy
 Silversnow's Sapling from Candi Ivy
 Guarding the Gifting Tree from Candi Ivy
 The Perfect Disguise from Candi Ivy
 Robgoblin Robbery Ring from Candi Ivy
 Snowmen Disassembly from Candi Ivy
 An Unexpected Gift from Candi Ivy

 Party Animal from Preston Daly next to the Sanctuary Warpstone
 Snowman Showdown from Everett (continuously repeatable)

These repeatable quests only become available after completing the quest series:
 Bye-Bye Supplies! from Candi Ivy (repeatable once per day)
 Curious Gift Baskets from Downey (repeatable once per day)
 Holiday Recital from Mayor Crystalline (repeatable once per day)
 Pretty Presents from Annabelle (repeatable once per day)

After you've finished the quest series, you will be able to go back and interfere with the Robgoblins' snowman building at any time.

Snowmen Invaders
To defeat the Abominable Snowman, you must participate in the live minigame in one of the following places that the Abominable Snowman will spawn on Snowhill in every 15 minutes.

There's a game-wide announcement to let you know that snowmen invaders are attacking the Gifting Tree. You should be able to find and grab some snowballs f

open: Pack merges three things: (a) the April 21, 2011 outage (node/97837), not a schedulable event; (b) this Double Station Cash day; (c) the PS3 / PSN repair plan (articleId=2118, 2119), which has no dates or details in these sources and needs its own record.

Year 2011 is inferred: the articles give month and day (Saturday April 30) and the outage was April 2011; no quoted article line states the year explicitly. Confirm against article records before scheduling.
articleId=2112 (pre-launch plan) was not retrieved; it is not used as evidence here.
Scope: articleId=2118 and 2119 say 'across SOE's games'. Specific games are not verified. node/97967 names Free Realms players only in the fact line; its EverQuest scope is unverified.
Activities and item purchases/redemptions are not stated in any source; left empty. Do not infer earning or spending.

Zones, NPCs, quests: no source ties any to this event. Locale hits for 'intrusion' and 'interrupt' are unrelated dialogue.
Recurring: null. One occurrence; no source says it recurs.
The pack title 'SOE service interruption' is not the event name; the name comes from articleId=2119, 2125 and node/97967.

Critique fixes applied: removed the claim that 2125 was confirmed by lookup text earlier (it is now confirmed by a fact line on this lookup, Portuguese post); corrected purpose to apology/thank-you per source; removed earning/spending activity guess; dropped the unverified EverQuest scope; marked 2119 as undated/late April 2011 and 2118 date as capture date; dropped the unverifiable 2112 claim.

wiki_page.title: Birthday Bash
wiki_page.text:
thumb|350px
The Birthday Bash is an annual event held throughout the month of April in celebration of launch day for Free Realms on April 29th, 2009. The event features party items, and Cakenstein, along with his minions out to take the Birthday Cake, it is up to the players to stop them.

Questline
The quests for this event are centered in Sanctuary, but send you all around Sacred Grove. Speak with Camellia to get things started.

 A Piece of Cake from Camellia in Sanctuary  - repeatable once per day
 Undelivered Confections from Camellia
 Mysteriously Cakey Remains from Chef Jarvie in Merry Vale
 Cakey Clue from Mayor McFairy in Merry Vale
 To Bake a Pretty Cake from Glerga in the Robgoblin Camp 
 Perfecting the Batter from Glerga 
 All Cakensteins Must Die from Glerga 
 Forgivable Matter from Glerga 

 Birthday Cake Bake-Off from Camellia
 Helping the Local Chef - repeatable once per day with your chosen chef
 Birthday Invitation from Flitter in Sanctuary - repeatable once per day
 Bundles of Balloons from Quills in Sanctuary - repeatable once per day
 Cakey Madness from General Glowlight in Sanctuary - repeatable once per day
 Downing Cakenstein from Commander Kiggle in Sanctuary - continuously repeatable
 Feeding the Crowd from Helga Humbleloaf in Pixiewood Hills - repeatable once per day
 Mystery Meat Mystery from Sal Monella in Blackspore Swamp - once per character (so if done in a previous year, it will not be offered again)

Where's the Party?
All of the major towns in Sacred Grove each have their own special party location.

 Sanctuary - On the island south of the Royal Palace
 Merry Vale - At the cooking table
 Seaside - At the Ocean Treasures Cafe
 Briarwood - At Chugilda's camp kitchen in Nettleseed
 Snowhill - Near the cooking table and the skating pond
